By Layli Foroudi
SAINT-DENIS, France, Oct 7 (Reuters) – In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting “stop.”

Bagayoko said he has been supporting the students in his working-class Parisian suburb and on Tuesday was asking the police not to charge.

“They had decided to charge and effectively go after the students, many of whom had shown no aggressive behaviour whatsoever toward the police officers,” Bagayoko, who is part of the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday at his town hall office in Saint-Denis, on the northern outskirts of Paris.

Show Full Article

In the end, the police fired tear gas at the group, including the mayor, he said. 

The wave of student protests, which began in Paris’ marginalised suburbs, has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace French President Emmanuel Macron. 

There have been more than 6,000 arrests and dozens of student injuries since the protests began. Rights groups and unions accuse the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flashball guns. Authorities say hundreds of police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked. 

The town of Saint-Denis, where poverty levels are more than double the national average, was one of the first sites of student protests in late September over overcrowded and unsanitary classrooms, teacher shortages and unequal opportunities.

“Protests are not new here, they happen at every start of the academic year,” Bagayoko said. “The Republican promise (of equality) — in particular for the working-class neighbourhoods, and also rural areas — is not respected.”

He said the government should prioritise investing in education and levy heavier taxes on billionaires. 

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Wednesday that the government would review demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October, but gave no details.

The government has suggested that LFI politicians were behind the protests, an accusation that Bagayoko dismissed as insulting to the young protesters.

A father of four, he said that “the high school children who were in the street could be my children … it is my responsibility to be at their side.”

(Reporting by Layli Foroudi, Editing by Rosalba O’Brien)

items.title: Applied Digital's revenue soars, loss widens on growing AI investments
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Applied Digital's first-quarter revenue more than quadrupled, while its net loss widened from a year earlier as the company stepped up investments to meet growing demand for data center services.
items.body:
Applied Digital's (APLD.O) first-quarter revenue more than quadrupled, while its net loss widened from a year earlier as the company stepped up investments to meet growing demand for data center services.
Shares of the Dallas, Texas-based company, which develops and operates data centers to support AI and other high-performance computing tasks, were up nearly 2% in volatile extended trading on Wednesday.
Here are some details:
Its first-quarter revenue surged to $341.9 million from $80.9 million a year earlier, surpassing analysts' average estimate of $133.8 million, according to data compiled by LSEG
Net loss attributable to common stockholders stood at $221.0 million, or $0.76 per share, compared with $18.5 million, or $0.07 per share, a year earlier
As of August 31, Applied Digital had $3.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, along with $6.4 billion in debt
Total costs and expenses jumped to $404.3 million in the quarter, from $90.7 million a year earlier
Applied Digital said costs rose due to higher spending to prepare data centers for customers, increased stock-based compensation and higher interest expenses as it expanded its AI infrastructure
"We are building for the long term, with a clear focus on developing large-scale, sustainable AI factory campuses and securing durable, high-quality, long-term contracts with proven, tier-one, investment-grade hyperscalers that are leaders in the AI industry," CEO Wes Cummins said in a statement

items.title: Aces G Jewell Loyd (leg) ruled out for Game 2 vs. Valkyries
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Las Vegas Aces veteran guard Jewell Loyd has been ruled out of Wednesday night's Game 2 semifinal contest against the host Golden State Valkyries due to a left leg injury.
items.body:
Las Vegas Aces veteran guard Jewell Loyd has been ruled out of Wednesday night's Game 2 semifinal contest against the host Golden State Valkyries due to a left leg injury.
Loyd was injured during the third quarter of Game 1 on Sunday and she missed the rest of the contest. Loyd was scoreless in 17 minutes.
The 2023 WNBA scoring champion, who averaged 24.7 points per game for the Seattle Storm, is now a role player for the Aces. The 12th-year pro, who turned 33 on Monday, is averaging a career-low 8.0 points per game.
Loyd, a six-time All-Star, has a career average of 15.4 points per game.
Las Vegas managed a season-low point total in Sunday's 71-60 loss to Golden State in Game 1 in San Francisco.
Aces coach Becky Hammon mentioned being shorthanded after the loss.
"We don't have a lot of time to sulk about it," Hammon said. "Nobody feels bad for us. It's the next woman up."
Forward Stephanie Talbot (left leg) is questionable for Las Vegas, while guard Dana Evans (right knee) has been upgraded to probable. Both players missed Game 1.
--Field Level Media

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ　７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ　７日　ロイター] - 米マイクロソフトは７日、パソコン（ＰＣ）上で直接実行可能な人工知能（ＡＩ）コーディングモデルと、ＡＩエージェントが許可なくデータにアクセスするのを防ぐ新たなセキュリティー技術を発表した。個人向け機器へのＡＩ導入を進めるアップルに対抗する動きとなる。 

同社はサンフランシスコで開かれたイベントで、半導体大手エヌビディアのＰＣチップ「ＲＴＸスパーク」を搭載した高性能ノートＰＣ「Ｓｕｒｆａｃｅ　Ｕｌｔｒａ」も発表した。マイクロソフトは、ＡＩエージェントがコンピューターコードの作成や複雑な業務プロジェクトの処理などをデスクトップやノートＰＣ上で行うためのプラットフォームへと「ウィンドウズ」を変革させようとしている。

マイクロソフトにとって今回の動きは、同社の高コストなクラウドコンピューティングプラットフォーム「Ａｚｕｒｅ（アジュール）」のデータセンターで行われている作業の一部を、企業や家庭にある高性能なウィンドウズマシンに移行できるとの見込みに賭けた戦略となる。

エヌビディアにとっては、ウィンドウズＰＣ市場に食い込むことができれば、インテルやアドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（ＡＭＤ）が支配する最後の主要市場の一つを切り崩せる可能性がある。

新型「Ｓｕｒｆａｃｅ　Ｌａｐｔｏｐ　Ｕｌｔｒａ」の価格は２５９９ドルからで、２０コアのプロセッサー、１２８ギガバイトのメモリー、１テラバイトのストレージを搭載したモデルは５８９９ドル。

items.title: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans assumes defensive play-calling duties
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Houston Texans rode the NFL's top-ranked defense to a wild-card berth in 2025.
items.body:
The Houston Texans rode the NFL's top-ranked defense to a wild-card berth in 2025.
They returned 10 starters from a unit that allowed a league-low 17.4 points per game.
But after an 0-4 start to the 2026 season, head coach DeMeco Ryans announced Wednesday that he would take over the defensive play-calling responsibilities from coordinator Matt Burke.
"If there's a lack in communication, I look at myself first, so it starts with me and making sure I'm a better communicator," Ryans said during his Wednesday news conference. "If our guys are saying communication is not right, then ultimately it falls on me. So, it's on me to get it fixed.
"It's no slight against coach Burke. He's done an outstanding job. Just want to make sure I can streamline communication in the best way possible so that isn't the theme when I stand up here the next time I see you guys and talk about communication."
Ryans and Burke both came to Houston in 2023, and the defense has never allowed more than 21.9 points per game.
However, the Texans are 20th in yards allowed per game (343.8) and 27th in points allowed per game (27.3).
The final straw came Sunday when, after holding the Dallas Cowboys to six first-half points, Houston permitted 28 in the second half of a 34-30 loss.
"It's a tough decision to make. Also, as a head coach, I have a lot of tough decisions I have to make," Ryans said. "My decisions are not always a popular opinion. I'm not in this role to please a lot of people's opinions.
"I have to do what's best for this team and make sure I'm leading in that way, and unfortunately, everybody isn't happy when you make changes, when you make decisions from my chair. Everybody isn't happy, and that's OK because I know everything that I try to do and strive to do is for the men in that locker room: to give those guys the best chance possible to go out and win our first football game."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Preços do petróleo recuam com acordo para liberação acelerada de estoques
items.author: Georgina Mccartney
items.creator: Georgina Mccartney
items.summary: Os preços do petróleo fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, após um pregão volátil, depois que a Agência Internacional de Energia concordou em acelerar a liberação de reservas de petróleo e priorizar o diesel, em uma tentativa de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis, à medida que a guerra no Irã reduz a oferta global.
items.body:
Os preços do petróleo fecharam em baixa nesta quarta-feira, após um pregão volátil, depois que a Agência Internacional de Energia concordou em acelerar a liberação de reservas de petróleo e priorizar o diesel, em uma tentativa de conter os preços recordes dos combustíveis, à medida que a guerra no Irã reduz a oferta global.
Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam com queda de 0,38%, a US$100,20 o barril. Os contratos futuros do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA fecharam com queda de 1,3%, a US$88,28.
A agência afirmou que concluir as liberações anunciadas anteriormente o mais rápido possível poderia colocar cerca de 100 milhões de barris no mercado, embora analistas e alguns governos tenham dito que o número não representava necessariamente uma nova intervenção dessa magnitude.
A França liberará 10 milhões de barris de diesel de seus estoques estratégicos, informou a rádio Franceinfo nesta quarta-feira, citando fontes anônimas.
Enquanto isso, os estoques de petróleo e de destilados dos EUA caíram, enquanto os estoques de gasolina aumentaram na semana passada, informou a Administração de Informações sobre Energia (EIA).
Os estoques de petróleo caíram 3,2 milhões de barris, para 424,1 milhões de barris, na semana encerrada em 2 de outubro, informou o governo, em comparação com as expectativas dos analistas em uma pesquisa da Reuters que apontavam para um aumento de 1,7 milhão de barris.

items.title: Lululemon puts Nike veteran in charge of product as CEO O'Neill looks to right ship
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Lululemon Athletica on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill.
items.body:
Lululemon Athletica (LULU.O) on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill.
Investors are closely watching O'Neill's turnaround plan as the sportswear maker grapples with finding its footing against newer rivals and keep pace with changing customer preferences beyond its signature leggings.
Here are more details:
Gauger will join Lululemon on October 26, and was most recently CEO of Gap's performance apparel brand Athleta, following a long stint at Nike, alongside O'Neill
Gauger takes charge of product at Lululemon at a time the company has struggled with [USN:L4N44W0MR TEXT:"product missteps"] that have triggered consumer backlash and recalls
Lululemon also appointed Joseph Godsey as chief operating officer
"This is an important first step in reinvigorating our enduring connection with guests and is designed to establish the foundation for sustainable, long-term growth," O'Neill said of the appointments
Lululemon's shares have nearly halved in value so far this year, and are on track for a third straight year of declines
The company's net income is expected to drop nearly 40% this year from fiscal 2024, according to data compiled by LSEG
Lululemon also said chief brand officer Nikki Neuburger and chief supply chain officer Ted Dagnese would leave the company, effective November 6, and that it was searching for candidates to fill the roles
It added that CFO Meghan Frank would oversee global brand and technology functions until those appointments are made
items.raw_description: Lululemon Athletica on Wednesday named industry veteran and former Nike vice president Maggie Gauger its chief product officer as the struggling apparel maker overhauls its leadership under new CEO Heidi O'Neill.

items.title: Democrats sue Trump to halt taxpayer-funded TV ads that praised him
items.author: Jan Wolfe
items.creator: Jan Wolfe
items.summary: Democratic Party officials sued US President Donald Trump on Wednesday, seeking a court order blocking his administration from using taxpayer money to pay for election-related TV ads.
items.body:
Democratic Party officials sued US President Donald Trump on Wednesday, seeking a court order blocking his administration from using taxpayer money to pay for election-related TV ads.
The lawsuit , filed by the Democratic National Committee in federal court in Washington, accused Trump of a "blatant violation of the statutory ban on the use of appropriations for 'publicity or propaganda purposes.'"
Taxpayer-funded television ads glorifying Trump began airing in late September, sparking a bipartisan backlash.
In a post on his Truth Social site on Monday, Trump [USN:FWN45R1HF TEXT:"said"] he considered the ads to be "a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A." but that they would no longer be funded by taxpayers. The White House said this week his MAGA PAC would fund the ads.
The DNC, the main governing organization of the Democratic Party, said in its lawsuit that the ads continued to air after Trump's comments.
"With less than 30 days remaining before the midterm election and millions of public dollars apportioned to pay for propaganda ads still unspent, the DNC has no choice but to take action in defense of free and fair elections," the lawsuit stated.
The ads ran during football games as recently as Sunday and during other programming. The New York Times reported that Trump personally directed the White House budget director to use taxpayer money for the TV spots, citing sources.
One ad features Trump declaring that "America will never be a communist country" while a chorus repeats the words "love me." Another combines images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a "golden age of America."
Another new ad recently has featured ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. A source briefed on the matter told Reuters the government-funded ads will end this week.
The White House said Trump's political action committee will not reimburse taxpayers for the ads that have run to date.
The ads end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government.

items.title: Exportação de suco de laranja do Brasil cresce quase 10% no 1º tri da safra 26/27, diz CitrusBR
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: As exportações brasileiras de suco de laranja pelo porto de Santos somaram 203,2 mil toneladas no primeiro trimestre da safra 2026/27, iniciada em julho, avanço anual de 9,6%, informou nesta quarta-feira a associação CitrusBR.
items.body:
As exportações brasileiras de suco de laranja pelo porto de Santos somaram 203,2 mil toneladas no primeiro trimestre da safra 2026/27, iniciada em julho, avanço anual de 9,6%, informou nesta quarta-feira a associação CitrusBR.
Os dados de embarques por Santos, que concentram as exportações das associadas da CitrusBR e responderam por 92% do total embarcado pelo Brasil, indicam "alguma recuperação" nas vendas externas do maior exportador global da commodity.
"Porém esse mesmo volume ainda está 14% abaixo da média das últimas cinco safras, que é de 237 mil toneladas", disse o diretor-executivo da CitrusBR, Ibiapaba Netto, em nota.
O setor vem enfrentando safras ruins no Brasil nos últimos anos, embora a colheita do ano passado tenha crescido na comparação com o ano anterior, quando a produção mais baixa em décadas reduziu oferta da matéria-prima.
A situação ajudou a elevar os preços do suco a níveis recordes na bolsa de referência de Nova York em 2024, afetando a demanda em mercados como a Europa.
Para 2026/27, a expectativa é de nova queda na produção de laranja da principal região citrícola do Brasil, [USN:L1N452127 TEXT:"de 10%"], segundo a última projeção do fundo de pesquisas Fundecitrus.
Os preços em Nova York, contudo, seguem próximos de US$1,45/libra-peso, abaixo dos mais de US$5 vistos ao final de 2024.
Questionado se os resultados do primeiro trimestre da safra indicam uma recuperação consistente, em meio a preços mais baixos para os consumidores, Netto disse que ainda é cedo para tal avaliação.
"Acho que a melhor parte é a recuperação parcial da Europa. Ainda está abaixo da média dos últimos cinco anos, mas é um passo...", disse ele, referindo-se ao continente europeu, antes o principal destino do suco do Brasil, lugar agora ocupado pelos Estados Unidos.
Em receita, os embarques totalizaram US$489,7 milhões, uma queda de 34,4% na mesma base de comparação.
Entre julho e setembro, Estados Unidos e Canadá importaram 96 mil toneladas de suco (em FCOJ equivalente a 66° Brix), ante 90,2 mil no mesmo período do ano passado. Já a Europa demandou 91,8 mil toneladas, alta de 4,8%, segundo a associação.

items.title: Medical device maker Centinel Spine discloses revenue rise in US IPO filing
items.author: Pragyan Kalita
items.creator: Pragyan Kalita
items.summary: Medical device maker Centinel Spine revealed a 42% rise in first-half revenue in its US initial public offering filing on Wednesday.
items.body:
Medical device maker Centinel Spine revealed a 42% rise in first-half revenue in its US initial public offering filing on Wednesday.
The filing comes against an uncertain backdrop for the fall IPO market, as rising bond yields and high interest rates have dampened investor appetite and prompted several major companies to delay their listings.
Here are some more details:
The West Chester, Pennsylvania-based company posted net income of $10.2 million on revenue of $85.2 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a net loss of $503,000 on revenue of $60.1 million a year earlier.
Centinel Spine develops replacement discs designed to preserve movement in the cervical and lumbar spine, offering an alternative to spinal fusion, which permanently eliminates motion at the treated level.
Its prodisc platform has been used in more than 300,000 implantations worldwide and is supported by more than 590 peer-reviewed clinical papers, according to the company.
"One of the notable factors in Centinel's filing is its ability to combine strong revenue growth with profitability, which distinguishes it from many healthcare companies approaching public markets," IPOX Research Associate Lukas Muehlbauer told Reuters.
"At the same time, the company's exclusive focus on total disc replacement creates concentration risk, leaving it somewhat exposed to changes in reimbursement policies and competing technologies."
Centinel Spine plans to use the offering proceeds to repay debt and invest in its sales infrastructure, patient-awareness programs, clinical trials etc.
Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, Piper Sandler, Canaccord Genuity and BTIG are underwriting the offering.
It plans to list its shares on NYSE under the symbol “CNTL.”

items.title: Wolfspeed secures $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment from US defense department
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Chipmaker Wolfspeed said on Wednesday it has received a conditional loan commitment for up to $1.5 billion from the US Department of Defense to expand domestic production of silicon carbide materials and power devices, sending its shares surging 27% in extended trading.
items.body:
Chipmaker Wolfspeed (WOLF.N) said on Wednesday it has received a conditional loan commitment for up to $1.5 billion from the US Department of Defense to expand domestic production of silicon carbide materials and power devices, sending its shares surging 27% in extended trading.
Wolfspeed makes chips using silicon carbide, which are more energy-efficient and used in applications that require huge amounts of power conversion such as electric vehicles, solar inverters and industrial power systems
The company said the conditional 30-year commitment, through the defense department's Office of Strategic Capital, reflects its efforts to optimize its capital structure and improve its financial foundation
It plans to use the financing to upgrade its gallium nitride technology for next-generation communications infrastructure and electronic warfare systems and develop radiation-hardening capabilities
The funding is subject to due diligence, definitive agreements, government approvals and other conditions
Under the proposed terms, Wolfspeed would be required to issue to the department warrants to purchase up to 7.5% of Wolfspeed's fully diluted equity

items.title: トランプ氏、ノーベル平和賞「そろそろその時期」　受賞に期待も懐疑的
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Doina Chiacu　Bo Erickson

[ワシントン　７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Doina Chiacu　Bo Erickson

[ワシントン　７日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は７日、ノルウェー・ノーベル賞委員会が９日に発表する２０２６年のノーベル平和賞について、自身が受賞すべきとの考えを改めて示した。ただ、受賞の可能性に懐疑的な見方も示した。

トランプ氏は大統領執務室で記者団に対し「ノーベル委員会がどのような決定を下すか分からないが、おそらく私のような人間には授与しないという評判がある」と語った。

トランプ氏は昨年ホワイトハウスに復帰して以降、ノーベル平和賞を受賞するに値すると繰り返し主張。この日も「そろそろその時期だ」と発言。「前回は、受賞者が『歴史上、トランプ大統領ほどこの賞にふさわしい人物はいない』と言ってくれたことで、間接的に受賞したような大変な栄誉を感じた」と述べた。

昨年のノーベル平和賞を受賞したベネズエラ野党指導者マリア・コリナ・マチャド氏は、受賞から数週間後、自身の民主化運動への支持拡大を狙い、ノーベル賞の金メダルをトランプ氏に贈った。

items.title: トランプ氏、8日の科学イベントに出席　マスク氏らに全米科学賞授与へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Courtney Rozen

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は、８日にホワイトハウスで開催される科学的発見をテーマとするイベントに出席する予定だ。ホワイトハウスのクラツィオス顧問（テクノロジー政策担当）がＸへの投稿で明らかにした。

また、ホワイトハウス当局者によると、トランプ大統領は、スペースＸのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）、アルファベット傘下グーグル共同創業者のセルゲイ・ブリン氏、エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯ、アドバンスト・マイクロ・デバイセズ（ＡＭＤ）のリサ・スーＣＥＯに全米科学賞を授与する見通し。同賞は科学者や技術者に対する米国最高の栄誉とされる。

さらに、デル・テクノロジーズのマイケル・デルＣＥＯとマイクロソフトのサティア・ナデラＣＥＯには、技術的功績に対する米国最高の栄誉とされる全米技術・イノベーション賞が授与される見通しという

items.title: Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say
items.author: CNA
items.summary: A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems.

Türkiye sending technical, defensive support to Saudi Arabia to help fight Houthis, officials say

A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems.

Members of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces fire a tank during what they say are clashes with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis in a location given as near Al-Hazm, Yemen, Sep 9, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Media Centre Of The Yemeni Armed Forces)

ANKARA: Türkiye is sending mainly defensive and technical support to Saudi Arabia to help it fight Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis , two officials said on Wednesday (Oct 7), after the NATO member and Pakistan pledged to act on the collective defence commitment of their newly formed alliance.
Türkiye , Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August , under which an armed attack on one member constituted an attack on all. They have been working to set the parameters of the new alliance and have held political and military meetings in response to the Houthi attacks.
On Monday, the countries said they had agreed to move immediately to implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the "rapid deployment" of military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia .
Türkiye , which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust defence industry, has condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia , voiced willingness to help meet Riyadh's technical military needs, and agreed to join a Saudi -led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

A Turkish official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the support expected from Türkiye was only in the form of military equipment, intelligence sharing, and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place as part of the alliance so far.

DRONE OPERATORS, FINE-TUNING DEFENSIVE MEASURES Officials have said that Turkish support for Saudi Arabia - including air defence systems - would largely be in a bilateral capacity for now, as Türkiye's parliament has not officially ratified the joint pact. The amount and nature of the support would increase after ratification, they have said.
A US official briefed on the matter said that Türkiye had so far decided to send capabilities that were broadly defensive , including strategic planning support and help with logistics. The official said the assistance included drone operators and help with fine-tuning defensive measures, as well as intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, speaking to state media after an extraordinary meeting of the Mecca alliance in Riyadh, said the sides had discussed what support to provide Saudi Arabia to help its defensive capabilities.
"We had our Defence Minister and Chief of General Staff with us, and they especially provided very fruitful views on military issues, operational issues, and technical matters," he said on Monday.

Related:

Houthis say Saudi Arabia launches dozens of strikes on Yemen capital

Three in four families go hungry in parts of Yemen from new fighting

Omer Celik, spokesman for Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party, said later on Wednesday that the Mecca pact was expected to be submitted to parliament for ratification "in a few days", adding that the process on further steps would become clear then.
Pakistani and regional officials have said Ankara and Islamabad have provided Saudi Arabia with military equipment that the kingdom is using in Yemen.
This week, Yemeni government forces with Saudi -led coalition air support launched a counter-offensive to recapture strategic territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an international shipping route for energy exports and other trade.
Officials had told Reuters last week that Saudi Arabia was planning an offensive against the Houthis , with options being considered including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or an assault on multiple fronts.

Source: Reuters/fs

"We had our Defence Minister and Chief of General Staff with us, and they especially provided very fruitful views on military issues, operational issues, and technical matters," he said on Monday.

Omer Celik, spokesman for Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party, said later on Wednesday that the Mecca pact was expected to be submitted to parliament for ratification "in a few days", adding that the process on further steps would become clear then.
Pakistani and regional officials have said Ankara and Islamabad have provided Saudi Arabia with military equipment that the kingdom is using in Yemen.
This week, Yemeni government forces with Saudi -led coalition air support launched a counter-offensive to recapture strategic territory near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, an international shipping route for energy exports and other trade.
Officials had told Reuters last week that Saudi Arabia was planning an offensive against the Houthis , with options being considered including a coastal push to secure the Red Sea shipping route or an assault on multiple fronts.

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 7 : A sea of red swept across global stocks on Wednesday as the bond market selloff picked up again and lifted long-dated US yields to 24-year highs, although a strong 10-year Treasury auction and minutes of the Fed's last policy meeting eased some of the upward pressure on borrowing costs.
In my column today, I ask how much longer Wall Street can continue scaling fresh peaks while the bond market rout continues to push yields ever higher. It will depend on whether rising borrowing costs reflect strong growth expectations, or other risks captured by the 'term premium', which is now racing higher also.
Today's Key Reads
• Fed policymakers divided over rate-hike logic in September, minutes show

• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Japan -1 per cent, South Korea -2 per cent. Europe -1 per cent, UK -0.8 per cent. S&P 500 and Nasdaq -0.2 per cent, Dow -0.7 per cent.SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 fall, four rise. Industrials -2 per cent, healthcare +1 per cent. Caterpillar -6 per cent, SpaceX -2.6 per cent. Moderna +5 per cent, Micron Technology +4 per cent.FX: US dollar back up to Monday's 17-month high, euro at 17-month low. Euro/sterling down for 9th day, longest losing streak since Feb 2021.BONDS: European bonds back under pressure, French/German spread widens 10 bps to 138 bps. US 10y and 30y yields touch fresh 24-year highs but cool after 10-year auction draws highest demand since 2016. US mortgage rates highest since 2023.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil slips - Brent -0.5 per cent, WTI -1.3 per cent. Gold -1 per cent, other precious metals -3 per cent.
Today's Talking Points:
United yet divided
We know that the Fed's decision to raise interest rates last month, the first hike in three years, was unanimous. What we learned from the meeting minutes published on Wednesday is policymakers were divided on the rationale for raising rates. Some saw it as a precautionary move to cool energy-driven price pressures or inflation expectations, others saw it as the first step in a battle against demand-driven inflation.
This matters because it suggests there will be less certainty and unanimity at upcoming decisions, starting with the October 28-29 meeting. The Fed rarely does "one and done" rate hikes, so it's reasonable to assume there will be more tightening to come. But how much more, and the pace, are up for more debate. This may be what Chair Kevin Warsh wants. Market pricing suggests a rate hike this month is off the table, but remember, only a week ago it was very much on the table. Three weeks is a long way away.
Term premium
Fed officials — and policymakers elsewhere — will surely be looking at the bond market with an increasing sense of nervousness and unease. If the rise in yields is a function of investors pricing in strong economic growth driven by demand and investment, that's one thing. If it's because of inflation fears, that's another. But if it's being driven by the 'term premium' — the extra premium investors demand for general 'risk' — then that's more worrying.
And the US term premium is beginning to rise. Rapidly. It has surged 40 bps in the last two weeks, and on Monday hit a 12-year high of 96 bps. Bank of America analysts note that the term premium is also gathering force in other key bond markets, and suggest three key factors investors should watch in Q4: US fiscal and funding issues, ECB willingness to stabilize spreads, and long-end JGB dynamics.
AI spaghetti
The news that SpaceX is in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia's AI chips has shone the spotlight back on the debt, deals and spaghetti-like circular financing that's driving the artificial intelligence revolution.
Investors are trying to grapple with a surge in corporate bond issuance to fund AI data center construction and investment, more than $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet debt, according to Morgan Stanley, and the bilateral loans, leases and agreements between several of the big players. A growing number of investors, including veterans like Jim Chanos, Steve Eisman and Michael Burry, warn that the circularity and opacity of it all spells danger.
What could move markets tomorrow?
• Samsung earnings (Q3, prelim)
• European Central Bank chief economist Philip Lane speaks
• Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill speaks
• US Treasury sells $22 billion of 30-year notes at auction
• US Federal Reserve officials scheduled to speak include Governor Chris Waller, Minneapolis Fed's Neel Kashkari and St. Louis Fed's Alberto Musalem

items.title: French mayor caught in viral video clash says student protesters 'could be my children'
items.author: Layli Foroudi
items.creator: Layli Foroudi
items.summary: In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop."
items.body:
In a video that has gone viral on social media, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis, stands facing police at a march in Paris on Tuesday, shielding young protesters and shouting "stop."
Bagayoko said he has been supporting the students in his working-class Parisian suburb and on Tuesday was asking the police not to charge.
"They had decided to charge and effectively go after the students, many of whom had shown no aggressive behaviour whatsoever toward the police officers," Bagayoko, who is part of the hard-left France Unbowed party (LFI), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday at his town hall office in Saint-Denis, on the northern outskirts of Paris.
In the end, the police fired tear gas at the group, including the mayor, he said.
The wave of student protests, which began in [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"Paris' marginalised suburbs"], has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace French President Emmanuel Macron.
There have been more than 6,000 arrests and dozens of student injuries since the protests began. Rights groups and unions accuse the police of using heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flashball guns. Authorities say hundreds of police officers have also been injured, schools have been burned or ransacked, and teachers and members of the public have been attacked.
The town of Saint-Denis, where poverty levels are more than double the national average, was one of the first sites of student protests in late September over overcrowded and unsanitary classrooms, teacher shortages and unequal opportunities.
"Protests are not new here, they happen at every start of the academic year," Bagayoko said. "The Republican promise (of equality) — in particular for the working-class neighbourhoods, and also rural areas — is not respected."
He said the government should prioritise investing in education and levy heavier taxes on billionaires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Wednesday that the government would review demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October, but gave no details.
The government has suggested that LFI politicians were behind the protests, an accusation that Bagayoko dismissed as insulting to the young protesters.
A father of four, he said that "the high school children who were in the street could be my children ... it is my responsibility to be at their side."

By Mireia Merino and David Latona
MADRID, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Trade unions in Spain on Wednesday announced a nationwide general strike over housing issues for November 11, a protest that will take place a few weeks before a snap election in which rising rents and evictions have become campaign topics.

The country’s two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, said they had agreed on the date, although it still needs to be formally ratified by other unions in a meeting later on Wednesday. It will be the first general strike jointly backed by Spain’s two largest unions in 14 years.

The strike will be the latest in a series of demonstrations provoked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid, with activists camping on one of the capital’s main squares calling for solutions to a mounting housing crisis.

Show Full Article

Those protests, along with parliament’s rejection last week of decrees aimed at curbing evictions and limiting rent pressures, prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call an early election for November 29.

Sanchez is seeking to shift the political narrative from his government’s handling of a migrant crisis in Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta and a series of corruption cases involving his Socialist Party and his family to the housing crisis, an area in which he believes he can harness growing resentment about rising rents.

Spain has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to more than a million by 2028, according to the Bank of Spain.

With fewer people able to afford a home, renting has increased sharply, putting pressure on that market. The average rental price of €1,176 ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7% of a young person’s average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.

“We cannot ignore the fact that housing is where most of our wages go. What is the point of raising the minimum wage if housing costs are rising three, four or five times faster?” said Tenants’ Union spokesperson Valeria Racu.

($1 = 0.8946 euros)

(Reporting by Mireia Merino and David Latona; Editing by Charlie Devereux and Xevi Fontdegloria)

items.title: AI wants to cure disease. It needs data first
items.author: Krystal Hu
items.creator: Krystal Hu
items.summary: Months after the OpenClaw frenzy, personal AI agents are looking promising again.
items.body:
Months after the [USN:L4N406097 TEXT:"OpenClaw frenzy"], personal AI agents are looking promising again.
The latest to join the party is OpenAI, which [USN:L1N45L06P TEXT:"unveiled"] its own personal agents, “dots,” at its annual dev day last week. Meta's Muse and the startup Instinct have both launched agents that are already gaining traction, built around reading your messages and acting on your behalf.
Despite a glitchy demo, OpenAI is making the case that always-on dots can chase down a user's goals across apps on their own. It’s also trying to send a message: this isn't the same breed of agent that famously[USN:L6N45H0LE TEXT:" went rogue this summer"], infiltrating everything from Hugging Face to government websites.
As someone who uses these things, I keep getting stuck on the same trade-off: how much of my personal information am I willing to hand over, for how much usefulness I get back?
And sometimes, the limits aren't even up to me. Businesses are increasingly blocking these agents outright, wary of losing control over their own customer relationships. Amazon, for one, has cut off Meta's Muse from shopping on its website entirely, accusing it of pulling customer data without permission. Meta says it is acting in a secure manner. It's both a security story and a turf war: every major platform wants to own its customer relationship.
This week, we dive into the next frontier AI keeps promising us — curing disease. How close are we, actually, to the AI-cures-cancer headlines? Scroll on.
OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L8N3ZL1UG TEXT:"Companies cutting jobs as investments shift toward AI"]
[USN:L4N45S0BH TEXT:"DeepSeek set to net over $12 billion in new fundraising, source says"]
[USN:L4N45R19C TEXT:"Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models"]
[USN:L6N45R0XK TEXT:"McDonald's hit with class action alleging AI-powered menu price-fixing"]
[USN:L4N45T0O0 TEXT:"Existential threats join bubble fears as AI mood sobers at Singapore forums"]
AI'S BIOLOGY RACE By now you've probably heard, more than once, that AI is going to help us cure cancer. But how far away are we, actually?
From AI labs to pharma giants to Big Tech, everyone is betting that biology is the next holy grail of AI promises. We're in the early innings, researchers and scientists told me. And one major obstacle standing between AI and drug discovery's big breakthroughs? Data.
Large language models got good by scraping the internet's text — an enormous, already-existing corpus. Biology has no equivalent. There is no "internet of cells" sitting around waiting to be ingested.
"We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," Alex Rives, head of science at the nonprofit Biohub, told me. Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells; an accurate predictive model will need billions, eventually trillions. That gap — several orders of magnitude — is the real bottleneck for now, Rives said.
So Biohub is trying to build that dataset from scratch, and has [USN:L6N45T078 TEXT:"rallied an unusual coalition"] to do it: the US government, Google, and Meta have joined the project, bringing total investment to $1.8 billion. Rives says the group is compressing work that would normally take decades into five years, with a first dataset expected to be ready in about a year, and usable models possible within five.
Even then, the path from dataset to actual treatment is uncertain. Rives said researchers can only begin training models once the data exists, then test whether those models can accurately predict how a cell responds to change. If that works, it could help scientists pinpoint exactly which part of a diseased cell to target.
Some are already taking the experiments into the physical world. Danaher, the life sciences giant, said this week it plans to launch its [USN:L4N45T0TZ TEXT:"first AI-powered autonomous research lab"] by early 2027, aiming to design, build, and test new antibodies up to eight times faster than conventional methods.
Anthropic is making a similar bet. The company has quietly set up its own [USN:L6N45814Q TEXT:"wet lab"] in the Bay Area, where human scientists and AI agents work side by side.
Eric Kauderer-Abrams, Anthropic's head of life sciences, told my colleague that the final test for any biology claim still has to happen on a lab bench, not inside a model. Anthropic says it isn't chasing drug discovery for now; it's targeting neglected corners of basic biology instead.
While the industry waits for a full "virtual cell," it's also trying to make some corners of the predictions work today: a wave of AI companies are running virtual drug trials, simulating how an experimental medicine might perform before it ever reaches a real patient.
The stakes are real. The biopharma industry spends roughly $140 billion a year on human clinical testing, and only about 12% of drug candidates ever win regulatory approval — a rate that's barely budged in decades. One startup, BioinvestGPT, says it [USN:L1N45M12V TEXT:"correctly predicted"] the outcome of five of six high-profile trials ahead of time, including, this past July, forecasting that Novartis' muscular dystrophy drug would fall short — months before the actual trial missed its goal and erased $30 billion in market value.
The simulation side of this is already saving companies money and time. The "cure cancer" side is a different story — one that might require building a model that doesn't exist yet, at a scale nobody has ever attempted. Investors are pricing in the first story while trying to predict the timeline of the second.

items.title: Açúcar bruto atinge nova máxima em 19 meses; café arábica recua
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram.
items.body:
Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE atingiram uma nova máxima em 19 meses nesta quarta-feira, antes de recuarem com o abrandamento da recente onda de compras por parte dos fundos, enquanto os preços do café e do cacau também caíram.
AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto ficou praticamente inalterado no final do pregão, a 20,83 centavos por libra-peso, após ter atingido mais cedo máxima de 21,24 centavos.
* Operadores afirmaram que a alta nos preços contribuiu para a fraqueza da demanda no mercado físico.
* Eles observaram que a alta foi impulsionada, em parte, pelas chuvas no Brasil, que devem reduzir a produção de açúcar nesta safra.
* "As chuvas no centro-sul do Brasil retardaram a colheita, o que significa que agora parece provável que a produção de açúcar fique aquém das 39 milhões de toneladas previstas pela OIA há seis semanas", afirmou a Organização Internacional do Açúcar em um relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira
* O fenômeno climático El Niño também foi visto como um fator que restringiu a produção do adoçante, particularmente na Ásia.
* O preço do açúcar branco também apresentou poucas variações, ficando em US$555,70 por tonelada métrica
CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em queda de 11,75 centavos, ou 3,9%, a US$2,927 por libra-peso, revertendo em grande parte os fortes ganhos da sessão anterior; o mercado havia subido 4,1% na terça-feira.
* Os corretores afirmaram que o forte ritmo das exportações do Brasil, principal produtor, garantiu que haja atualmente oferta abundante.
* As exportações brasileiras de café verde em setembro totalizaram 235.800 toneladas métricas, ou 3,93 milhões de sacas de 60 kg, o maior volume em 20 meses, de acordo com dados do governo divulgados na terça-feira
* No entanto, as preocupações de que o fenômeno El Niño reduza a produção global na safra 2027/28 continuaram a sustentar os preços, enquanto os estoques certificados nas bolsas também permanecem baixos
* O café robusta registrou queda de 2,9%, para US$ 3.485 por tonelada
CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou em queda de £57, ou 1,3%, a £4.174 por tonelada.
* Os corretores observaram que as chuvas previstas devem melhorar as perspectivas para as safras na Costa do Marfim, principal produtora.
* "As chuvas que se aproximam vão amenizar significativamente as preocupações com a seca na principal safra de cacau da Costa do Marfim, mas podem não ser suficientes para garantir a recuperação dos frutos novos", afirmou a LSEG Research and Insights em uma nota
* O cacau de Nova York recuou 2,1%, para US$5.582 por tonelada.
(Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

items.title: Missouri sued over alleged decades of underfunding at historically Black university
items.author: Bianca Flowers
items.creator: Bianca Flowers
items.summary: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.
items.body:
Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.
The complaint, filed in federal court in the US District Court for the Western District of Missouri Central Division, seeks compensatory damages under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act for what plaintiffs describe as "educational and economic injuries" caused by decades of underfunding. It also seeks an injunction requiring Missouri to fully match Lincoln University's federal land-grant funding in the future.
Some of the funding they are requesting would include campus repairs, faculty hiring, student services, financial aid and agricultural research programs.
Lincoln University, in Jefferson City, is the state's first historically Black land-grant institution. The University of Missouri is the state's predominantly white land-grant institution.
The plaintiffs allege Missouri appropriated less per student to Lincoln than to the University of Missouri in most fiscal years between 1987 and 2020. They cited a September 2023 letter in which the US agriculture and education secretaries calculated that Missouri had underfunded Lincoln by $361.6 million over that period, based on federal higher education data.
According to the complaint, Missouri provided no state matching funds for Lincoln's federal land-grant allocation from fiscal 2000 through 2007, and supplied only a portion of the required match in subsequent years. Lincoln allegedly diverted about $43.5 million from its general operating budget between 2000 and 2016 to cover the state's share, and returned nearly $8 million in federal funds from 2016 through 2018 when it could not meet matching requirements.
Missouri fully matched the University of Missouri's land-grant allocations during the same period, the complaint said.
The University of Missouri declined to comment, citing "ongoing litigation." Lincoln University of Missouri did not respond to an immediate request for comment.
The lawsuit names the State of Missouri, the state Coordinating Board for Higher Education, Governor Michael Kehoe, Higher Education Commissioner Bennett Boggs and University of Missouri System President Mun Choi as defendants.
State officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The lawsuit argues the funding gap perpetuates the legacy of Missouri's formerly segregated higher education system, under which the University of Missouri served white students and Lincoln was established for Black students.
"Lincoln is constantly putting Band-Aids over bullet wounds because they do not have the resources to fully address the blow," Makhi Jaff, a plaintiff, said in the lawsuit.
Plaintiffs include alumni who attended Lincoln in the 1980s and 1990s, a former student who left without a degree in 2024, and four current students. They describe deteriorating residence halls, limited dining and health services, scarce course offerings, inadequate advising and financial hardship.
One student stated in the lawsuit that she lost weight because dining services closed before band practice ended. Another student said a scholarship she expected to cover her education was withdrawn, requiring her to take loans and work up to 30 hours weekly.
items.raw_description: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated the US Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.

items.title: Trump dice que se merece el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero duda de que se lo concedan
items.author: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
items.creator: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
items.summary: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que libra una guerra contra Irán y aún no ha logrado negociar un armisticio en Ucrania, dijo el miércoles que debería ganar el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero reconoció que tenía dudas sobre sus posibilidades.
items.body:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, que libra una guerra contra Irán y aún no ha logrado negociar un armisticio en Ucrania, dijo el miércoles que debería ganar el Premio Nobel de la Paz, pero reconoció que tenía dudas sobre sus posibilidades.
"No sé cuál va a ser su decisión", dijo Trump sobre el premio de 2026, que el Comité Noruego del Nobel anunciará el viernes. "Tienen fama de no concedérselo a gente como yo".
Desde su regreso a la Casa Blanca el año pasado, Trump ha dicho en repetidas ocasiones que se merece el que podría ser el premio más prestigioso del mundo.
"Ya va siendo hora", dijo Trump a los periodistas en el Despacho Oval. "Pero fue un gran honor recibirlo indirectamente la última vez de manos de la galardonada, quien dijo que nadie en la historia lo merece más que el presidente Trump".
La líder de la oposición venezolana, María Corina Machado, entregó su medalla del Premio Nobel de la Paz de 2025 a Trump en enero, en un intento por conseguir el apoyo de Estados Unidos a sus esfuerzos en Venezuela.
Trump dijo que debería recibir el premio tras haber intervenido en ocho conflictos desde que asumió el cargo.
Los líderes de Camboya, Israel y Pakistán dijeron que postularon a Trump, aunque no hay forma de verificarlo.
A Trump no le ha sido posible alcanzar una solución a la guerra de Rusia en Ucrania, a pesar de que prometió ponerle fin el primer día de su segundo mandato en la Casa Blanca.
Los ataques conjuntos de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán han dado lugar a un conflicto latente de siete meses que ha trastocado el suministro energético mundial y ha provocado una subida de los precios de la gasolina.
El papa León, la Corte Penal Internacional y la relatora especial para los Territorios Palestinos, Francesca Albanese, estan entre los favoritos para ganar este año.

items.title: Raise a glass: League to allow drinking celebrations after 'juice' saga
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: NFL players will not be disciplined for celebrations that imitate drinking a beverage, the league and union said on Wednesday, after a high-profile saga involving 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk this season prompted outcry and mockery from fans.
items.body:
NFL players will not be disciplined for celebrations that imitate drinking a beverage, the league and union said on Wednesday, after a high-profile saga involving 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk this season prompted outcry and mockery from fans.
The NFL was once known derisively as the "No Fun League" for its hard line stance on end-zone celebrations but relaxed its rules in 2017, allowing for [USN:KCN1PQ4H5 TEXT:"elaborate dances and routines"] in a largely well-received shift.
But the line between what is and is not permitted in the heat of celebration became blurred [USN:L6N45G1AA TEXT:"last month"] when Juszczyk was fined for a gesture that the NFL said imitated swigging a beer during an on-field celebration.
Juszczyk, who appealed the decision, posted several examples of his drinking celebration that went unpunished, saying that the celebratory sip was a nod to his nickname "Juice." He told ESPN's NFL insider Adam Schefter : "I don't even drink beer!"
"Recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline," the NFL and NFLPA said in a joint statement.
Juszczyk also saw his fine rescinded on Wednesday, according to media reports.
The joint statement reminded players that certain gestures, including those depicting violence, the use of weapons, smoking or drug use were not permitted.
"The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules," the statement read.
"When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines."
items.raw_description: NFL players will not be disciplined for celebrations that imitate drinking a beverage, the league and union said on Wednesday, after a high-profile saga involving 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk this season prompted outcry and mockery from fans.

items.title: シリア、サウジへの軍事支援検討　フーシ派との戦闘激化で＝当局筋
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Timour Azhari

[リヤド ７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Timour Azhari

[リヤド ７日 ロイター] - 親イラン武装組織フーシ派との戦争が激化する中、シリアがサウジアラビアへの軍事支援を慎重に検討していることが分かった。この件について説明を受けた米国当局者とシリア軍当局者が明らかにした。

情報筋によると、検討されている選択肢には、サウジを攻撃から守るための防衛支援や、イエメン暫定政府軍のフーシ派掃討を後押しするための部隊派遣などが含まれるという。

米当局者によると、サウジはシリアに対し、フーシ派と戦うための部隊の派遣を要請したという。

シリア外務省へのコメント要請に対し、あるシリア外交官は、同国はフーシ派の攻撃に直面するサウジを断固として支持するとしつつも、政府の最優先事項は内戦からの復興といった国内課題にあると述べた。

同外交官は声明で「サウジが軍事協力や専門知識の共有を要請した場合、それは公式ルートを通じて、かつ両兄弟国の関係を規定する二国間協定の枠組み内でのみ行われる」と述べた。

シリアのシャラア暫定大統領は６日にサウジの首都リヤドを公式訪問し、サウジのムハンマド・ビン・サルマン皇太子と会談した。米政府当局者によると、シャラア氏はこの会談で、サウジへの軍事支援の可能性などを協議したという。

items.title: Penguins deal D Filip Hallander to Oilers for F Spencer Stastney
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: In a depth trade, the Pittsburgh Penguins sent forward Filip Hallander to the Edmonton Oilers for defenseman Spencer Stastney on Wednesday.
items.body:
In a depth trade, the Pittsburgh Penguins sent forward Filip Hallander to the Edmonton Oilers for defenseman Spencer Stastney on Wednesday.
Pittsburgh general manager Kyle Dubas has traded Hallander twice and acquired him once. As general manager of the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2020, he acquired Hallander in a trade that sent Kasperi Kapanen to Pittsburgh.
Dubas then dealt Hallander back to Pittsburgh to acquire Jared McCann, who was subsequently selected by Seattle in the 2021 expansion draft.
Now, Dubas has shipped Hallander north of the border.
Hallander, 26, had an outstanding opening night, scoring a goal and adding two assists in Pittsburgh's 7-0 win at Philadelphia. He played 9:39 on Oct. 3 against Montreal and was a healthy scratch Monday against Winnipeg.
In parts of four seasons with the Penguins, Hallander has played 18 games, recording two goals and five assists while posting a plus-8 rating.
Stastney was a healthy scratch for Edmonton's first three games. The 26-year-old native of Woodridge, Ill., split time between Edmonton and Nashville last season, appearing in 66 totl games, after playing 51 games for the Predators from 2022-25.
He has four goals, 15 assists and 30 penalty minutes in 117 career games.
Stastney is not expected to crack the Penguins' top six defensemen but adds NHL-caliber depth to the group.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it
items.author: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
items.creator: Doina Chiacu, Bo Erickson
items.summary: US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump , who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the [USN:L8N3AO23E TEXT:"Nobel Peace Prize"] but acknowledged doubt about his chances.
"I don't know what their decision is going to be," Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday. "They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me."
Since his return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world's most prestigious award.
"It is about that time," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. "But I was very honored to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump."
Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gave her [USN:L5N3VQ11X TEXT:"2025 Nobel Peace Prize medal"] to Trump [USN:L1N3YG0T8 TEXT:"in January"] as she sought US support for her efforts in Venezuela.
Trump said he should get the prize after wading into [USN:L1N3U8067 TEXT:"eight conflicts"] since taking office last January.
The leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated Trump, though there is no way of verifying that.
Parties to some conflicts Trump claims to have resolved dispute the US president's diplomatic role, and fighting has flared again in some of those regions, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the border between Cambodia and Thailand.
A resolution to Russia's war in Ukraine has eluded Trump, who promised to end it on the first day of his second White House term. US-Israel strikes on Iran have led to a seven-month simmering conflict that has upended global energy supplies and driven gas prices up before November's midterm elections.
Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, the special rapporteur for the Palestinian Territories, are among the favorites to win this year.
items.raw_description: US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances.

items.title: Fed Minutes Show Hawkish Unity Behind September Hike
items.summary:
All 19 Federal Reserve officials backed the decision in September to raise interest rates, with many supporting the move to guard against the risk of intensifying inflation pressures. Jennifer Welch of Bloomberg Economics examines what it means for the state of conflict in the Middle East at large. Lumen CEO Kate Johnson discusses the impact of AI on the telecom sector. Plus - Apple's upcoming push into smart home devices will include a doorbell, thermostat and other accessories developed through an unusual partnership with LG Electronics. items.title: Leak exposes payments made to hacking group that has extorted millions from law firms
items.author: A.J. Vicens
items.creator: A.J. Vicens
items.summary: Leak data posted to the internet has exposed payments made to a hacking group known for extorting large sums of money from law firms, blockchain investigations firm Chainalysis said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Leak data posted to the internet has exposed payments made to a hacking group known for extorting large sums of money from law firms, blockchain investigations firm Chainalysis said on Wednesday.
The findings come after an unknown party posted troves of data allegedly associated with Silent Ransom Group, a prolific cyber extortion group. The FBI warned in May that the group was stealing data from law firms with hacks and demanding millions of dollars to prevent it from being posted.
The FBI says the SRG targets specific firm employees with phone calls, emails and sometimes in-person visits to gain access to victims' computers in order to enable access to targeted computer networks.
A website titled "The Luna Moth Files," published earlier this week by an unknown party, posted what it alleged was troves of the group's data, including chat logs, alleged ransom demand totals, documents and other materials associated with the group's work, and dozens of cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the site's claims or data, but Chainalysis said in an X post on Wednesday that "certain leaked SRG addresses sit downstream of millions of dollars in ransomware payments that SRG has extorted from victims."
Chainalysis said certain cryptocurrency addresses contained in the leaks include addresses Chainalysis was already tracking prior to the leak, including one that reflected a $10 million victim payment SRG collected in mid-2026.
SRG has been alleged to be involved in hacks on prominent law firms including [USN:L6N42H14I TEXT:"Fox Rothschild"] and [USN:L6N40P0LU TEXT:"Jones Day"], Reuters has previously reported.

items.title: Peso mexicano anota pocos cambios y se mantiene por debajo de umbral de 18/dlr
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El peso mexicano terminó con leves cambios el miércoles, después de moverse entre bajas y alzas durante la sesión, tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
items.body:
El peso mexicano terminó con leves cambios el miércoles, después de moverse entre bajas y alzas durante la sesión, tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos.
* Los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed estuvieron divididos el mes pasado respecto de los motivos para subir las tasas de interés, mostraron el miércoles las actas del encuentro de mediados de septiembre del banco central.
* Los mercados proyectan que la Fed mantendrá estables las tasas en su reunión de finales de este mes, pero descuentan un alza para diciembre.
* El dólar avanzó frente a sus pares apoyado más temprano por un alza de los precios del crudo, que generó temores sobre las presiones inflacionarias, pero posteriormente cedió parte de sus alzas mientras el petróleo revertía su curso luego de que la Agencia Internacional de Energía dijo que aceleraría la liberación de reservas y daría prioridad al diésel.
* Los mercados ahora aguardan la divulgación de los datos locales de inflación y las minutas del último encuentro de Banxico, que se conocerán el jueves.
* La moneda local cotizaba en 17.9800 por dólar hacia el final de los negocios, con una ligera baja del 0.02%, luego de tres alzas seguidas, pero manteniéndose por debajo del umbral de las 18 unidades luego de varias semanas de un rápido deterioro que la llevó a tocar la semana pasada las [USN:L1N45N0ZE TEXT:"18.4330 unidades"], su nivel más débil desde noviembre de 2025.
* "El tipo de cambio muestra una leve corrección a la baja y ya cotiza por debajo del nivel de 18.00 pesos por dólar. Sin embargo, aún sería muy prematuro decir que esto podría ser un cambio de tendencia a la baja, pues los indicadores de oscilación muestran que aún hay las presiones al alza. Por ello, no se descarta que el tipo de cambio vuelva a subir a un canal entre 18.30-18.50 pesos por dólar", dijo Banco Base.
* "Al alza, las resistencias técnicas se ubican en 18.0672 y 18.4320 pesos por dólar. A la baja, los soportes clave se ubican en 17.8415, 17.6590 y 17.4766 pesos por dólar", agregó.
* Mientras, la bolsa mexicana cortó su racha de tres jornadas de ganancias. El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) retrocedió un 1.01%, a 64,653.33 puntos.
* Destacó un descenso del 4.25% a 361.80 pesos de las acciones del Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, GAP (GAPB.MX) , tras divulgar sus cifras de tráfico de septiembre.
* "En septiembre del 2026, Gap presentó un ajuste en el tráfico total de pasajeros de 7.3% vs septiembre 2025, resultado de un retroceso en el tráfico de pasajeros nacional e internacional de 9.5% y 3.2%, respectivamente", dijo Monex, que recomendó "mantener" con un precio objetivo de 480 pesos para finales de este año.
* En renta fija, el bono gubernamental mexicano a 10 años cotizó con un rendimiento del 9.391%, frente al 9.411% del cierre anterior, mientras que la deuda a 20 años ofreció un retorno de 9.804%, que se compara con el 9.839% de la sesión previa.

items.title: Glaukos says late-stage eye disease treatment shows lasting benefits after single dose
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Glaukos said on Wednesday patients treated with its late-stage eye disease therapy maintained improvements in vision and corneal shape three years after a single treatment for keratoconus, a disease that can progressively distort vision.
items.body:
Glaukos (GKOS.N) said on Wednesday patients treated with its late-stage eye disease therapy maintained improvements in vision and corneal shape three years after a single treatment for keratoconus, a disease that can progressively distort vision.
The medtech firm said patients who received a single Epioxa treatment did not require additional intervention during the three-year follow-up period.
Epioxa-treated eyes showed a 1.9-diopter improvement in maximum corneal curvature from baseline after three years, indicating sustained flattening and stabilization of the cornea.
About 29% of Epioxa-treated eyes gained two or more lines on a standard vision chart, while 20% gained three or more lines from baseline.
The results add to evidence supporting Epioxa, which was approved as a less invasive option for keratoconus because it does not require removal of the cornea's outer protective layer before treatment.
The study included 38 eyes from 35 patients, and 92% of treated eyes completed the three-year assessment.
Glaukos said there were no serious adverse events, treatment-related adverse events or treatment discontinuations linked to Epioxa during the follow-up period.
Keratoconus typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood and can lead to worsening vision and, in severe cases, the need for a corneal transplant, according to Glaukos.

items.title: Maduro se enfrentará a nuevos cargos por presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses: funcionario
items.author: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
items.creator: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
items.summary: El expresidente Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, se enfrentarán a nuevos cargos penales en Estados Unidos por la presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos en Venezuela, dijo el miércoles un funcionario en Washington.
items.body:
El expresidente Nicolás Maduro y su esposa, Cilia Flores, se enfrentarán a nuevos cargos penales en Estados Unidos por la presunta tortura de ciudadanos estadounidenses retenidos en Venezuela, dijo el miércoles un funcionario en Washington.
Los nuevos cargos podrían presentarse tan pronto como el jueves, según el funcionario, quien fue informado sobre la investigación.
Maduro y Flores fueron detenidos por el ejército estadounidense en Caracas el 3 de enero y trasladados a Nueva York para responder a cargos de tráfico de drogas. Ambos se han declarado inocentes y está previsto que sean juzgados a partir del 1 de junio de 2027.
Un portavoz de la Fiscalía de Manhattan, que presentó los cargos, no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.
Los abogados de Maduro y Flores no respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios.
La posibilidad de nuevos cargos fue reportada inicialmente por CNN el miércoles. No se dispuso de inmediato de detalles sobre los nuevos cargos, incluidas las identidades de las presuntas víctimas de tortura.
El mandato de Maduro estuvo marcado por tensiones con Estados Unidos. Washington acusó a su Gobierno de detener a estadounidenses como medida de presión para obtener concesiones, tales como el alivio de las sanciones financieras.
Entre los estadounidenses clasificados por Estados Unidos como detenidos injustamente durante el mandato de Maduro figuraban cinco ejecutivos petroleros arrestados bajo cargos de corrupción. Fueron liberados en 2022 a cambio de dos sobrinos de Flores que habían sido condenados en Estados Unidos por narcotráfico.
Entre los detenidos también figuraban dos exmiembros de las Fuerzas Especiales del Ejército de Estados Unidos, arrestados en Venezuela en 2020 en relación con una incursión fallida destinada a derrocar a Maduro. Fueron liberados en 2023 como parte de otro intercambio de prisioneros.
Desde la captura de Maduro, Venezuela ha sido dirigida por su exvicepresidenta, Delcy Rodríguez, quien ha aumentado la cooperación con la administración de Donald Trump.
Maduro, de 63 años, y Flores, de 69, han permanecido recluidos en una cárcel federal de Brooklyn. Flores tiene previsto comparecer el jueves ante un tribunal federal de Manhattan para solicitar al juez de distrito Alvin Hellerstein su excarcelación antes del juicio por motivos de salud. La fiscalía se opone a su liberación.

items.title: US proposes to boost transit funding to areas with higher marriage, birth rates
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The US Transportation Department said on Wednesday it is proposing to boost grants for major transit projects by 10% in areas that have above-average marriage and birth rates and imposing strict deadlines to ensure projects remain on schedule.
items.body:
The US Transportation Department said on Wednesday it is proposing to boost grants for major transit projects by 10% in areas that have above-average marriage and birth rates and imposing strict deadlines to ensure projects remain on schedule.
Democrats criticized the plan, which would apply to 40 major projects already in the program that funds light rail, bus and commuter rail projects and said it could result in lower spending in cities controlled by Democrats.
The Transportation Department awards about $20 billion annually in transit grants. Democrats in August criticized the agency for not awarding $1.9 billion for major transit projects.
"Tying funding for transit projects to marriage rates and how many babies a woman has is the sort of bizarre and dystopian idea you’d expect in a TV show, not actual policy put forth by the U.S. government," Democratic Senator Patty Murray said on Wednesday.
The projects that risk facing spending cuts include Washington's Red Line subway modernization program, Boston's Green Line subway project, an expansion of the BART train in Silicon Valley and an Austin light rail project, Murray said.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy in January 2025 signed a memo giving preference for transit grants to communities with higher marriage and birth rates.
Murray cited a study showing the change would likely deprive historically underfunded urban neighborhoods of funding while benefiting higher-income areas and those with larger white populations.
The Transportation Department said the changes included setting strict deadlines and demanding local accountability on projects up front "so we can finally build these systems faster, better, and safer... If you want federal funding, your project needs to align with where communities and families are actually growing."
Murray said the new guidance could force "transit agencies and local and state governments that have already spent years planning and designing projects to follow a whole slew of new rating and cost-share requirements."
She argued it was "another attempt by the Trump administration to penalize blue states and slow down and delay transit projects."
In October 2025, the Transportation Department froze billions of dollars in funding for infrastructure projects in New York and Chicago after Trump blamed a partial government shutdown on Democrats in Congress, but those decisions were overturned by judges.

items.title: 米国株式市場＝反落、米長期債利回り上昇が重し
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は反落。米長期債利回りが上昇する中、インフレと債務拡大を巡る懸念が再燃した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とダウ工業株３０種は５営業日ぶり、ナスダック総合は６営業日ぶりの反落となった。

小型株で構成するラッセル２０００は１．３％下落し、大型株をアンダーパフォームした。

北海ブレント先物の清算値は１バレル＝１００ドルを上回り、米長期債利回りは一時、２４年ぶりの高水準を付けた。

イラン戦争に伴う供給懸念で原油価格が高騰し、インフレ懸念が再燃するとともに、中央銀行による利上げサイクル長期化の可能性が高まっている。こうした懸念に企業や政府の債務拡大が重なって世界的な債券売りを招き、ここ数週間、各国市場を揺さぶっている。

グローバルトのシニアポートフォリオマネジャー、トーマス・マーティン氏は「投資家は原油価格が幾分落ち着くことを期待してきた。そうなれば金利も落ち着き、株式市場の支援材料になる」と指摘。「第３・四半期は相場が弱含み、調整が入るはずだった。それが起きなかったので、ひとまず歓迎しつつ利益を確定しようという流れだ」と語った。

国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）が軽油を優先して石油備蓄の放出を加速することで合意し、原油価格が下落に転じると、株価は下げ幅を縮小した。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が７日公表した９月１５─１６日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）議事要旨では、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていたことが分かった。一部の参加者はエネルギーなどの価格ショックの影響を抑えるために必要と判断した一方、よりタカ派的な参加者は、需要主導のインフレが生じつつあることへの備えとして必要と捉えていた。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場が織り込む１０月会合での利上げ確率は１７．２％と、１週間前の３７．６％から低下している。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種では、工業の下落率が最大となった一方、ヘルスケアが上昇率トップだった。

米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が発表した先週の３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利が約３年ぶりの高水準となったことを受け、住宅株指数が２．３％、住宅建設株指数が２．９％、それぞれ下落した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は１．２％下落。年初来では８０％超上昇している。

イーロン・マスク氏率いる宇宙企業スペースＸは２．５％安。エヌビディア製半導体の購入資金として４００億ドルの調達を目指しているとの報道を嫌気した。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を３．３４対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも２．３７対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６２億１０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７５億７０００万株。

イラン戦争に伴う供給懸念で原油価格が高騰し、インフレ懸念が再燃するとともに、中央銀行による利上げサイクル長期化の可能性が高まっている。こうした懸念に企業や政府の債務拡大が重なって世界的な債券売りを招き、ここ数週間、各国市場を揺さぶっている。

グローバルトのシニアポートフォリオマネジャー、トーマス・マーティン氏は「投資家は原油価格が幾分落ち着くことを期待してきた。そうなれば金利も落ち着き、株式市場の支援材料になる」と指摘。「第３・四半期は相場が弱含み、調整が入るはずだった。それが起きなかったので、ひとまず歓迎しつつ利益を確定しようという流れだ」と語った。

国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）が軽油を優先して石油備蓄の放出を加速することで合意し、原油価格が下落に転じると、株価は下げ幅を縮小した。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が７日公表した９月１５─１６日の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）議事要旨では、利上げの理由を巡って当局者の見解が分かれていたことが分かった。一部の参加者はエネルギーなどの価格ショックの影響を抑えるために必要と判断した一方、よりタカ派的な参加者は、需要主導のインフレが生じつつあることへの備えとして必要と捉えていた。

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場が織り込む１０月会合での利上げ確率は１７．２％と、１週間前の３７．６％から低下している。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種では、工業の下落率が最大となった一方、ヘルスケアが上昇率トップだった。

米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が発表した先週の３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利が約３年ぶりの高水準となったことを受け、住宅株指数が２．３％、住宅建設株指数が２．９％、それぞれ下落した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は１．２％下落。年初来では８０％超上昇している。

イーロン・マスク氏率いる宇宙企業スペースＸは２．５％安。エヌビディア製半導体の購入資金として４００億ドルの調達を目指しているとの報道を嫌気した。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を３．３４対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも２．３７対１で値下がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６２億１０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７５億７０００万株。

items.title: Levi Strauss lifts annual profit outlook on tariff refunds, holiday demand
items.author: Angela M, Danielle Kaye
items.creator: Angela M, Danielle Kaye
items.summary: Levi Strauss raised its annual profit forecast on Wednesday, after benefiting from tariff refunds, as it bets on strong holiday demand for its premium denim and sweaters.
items.body:
Levi Strauss (LEVI.N) raised its annual profit forecast on Wednesday, after benefiting from tariff refunds, as it bets on strong holiday demand for its premium denim and sweaters.
Still, the company's shares fell 2% in extended trading after it reported weaker-than-expected sales in the United States and Europe.
Here are more details:
Levi's received $79 million in refunds during the quarter ended August 30 for tariffs paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and plans to redeploy about $60 million this year on promotions and marketing
Comparable sales for its direct-to-consumer business were flat in the third quarter. CEO Michelle Gass said the business fell short of expectations as sales fell in the US, while "unseasonably" warm weather weighed on traffic in Europe
The back-to-school US campaign focused too heavily on loose-fitting pants rather than popular low-rise styles, Gass said
Nevertheless, the jeans maker's women's line emerged as a bright spot, driven in part by a push beyond denim into tops, skirts and dresses. Products apart from denim bottoms accounted for about half of the quarter's top-line growth, Gass said
Levi's Blue Tab premium denim line grew double-digits, Gass added, as the jeans maker pushes to draw in higher-income shoppers
Meanwhile, sales growth in Asia was fueled by a 13% uptick in China and new collaboration with singer Rosé
The company raised its outlook for annual organic revenue growth to 6%, the upper end of its previous forecast of 5.5% to 6%
It raised its forecast for full-year adjusted earnings to $1.54 to $1.56 per share, from $1.46 to $1.52 per share previously
Net revenue for the quarter ended August 30 rose 4% to $1.61 billion, largely in line with estimates of $1.62 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG
It earned 48 cents per share on an adjusted basis in the quarter, compared with analysts' estimate of about 36 cents per share
Direct-to-consumer performance in the third quarter was softer than expected, independent retail consultant Bruce Winder said, adding that the US market remains challenging due to elevated fuel prices
