The unrest follows June clashes between protesters and police in Brussels over education reforms, including a tuition increase for most students in Belgium's French-speaking Community to €1,194 (US$1,280) from €835.
Videos circulating on social media in recent days showed shattered glass, fires and hundreds of mostly young protesters in Liège, while other footage showed police blocking roads.
During Wednesday's (Oct 7) protest, police were seen checking students for weapons.

A person throws an object into a burning structure on a street, on the day of a spontaneous street protest of high school students against education reforms introduced by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation government and an increase in student fees, in Liege, Belgium, Oct 7, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Stephanie Lecocq)

IN TOUCH WITH FRENCH STUDENTS Some students told Reuters they were in touch with French counterparts.
"We support each other because we're facing pretty much the same issues," 19-year-old student Alfred said.
Amelia Di Salve, also 19, who is studying to become a teacher, said Belgium's student movement began earlier this year and was reignited after students saw the demonstrations in France .
"When we saw nothing was changing without protests , we decided we would start ... France did influence us a little," she said.
Liège mayor Willy Demeyer told Belgian broadcaster RTBF he hoped calm would return and "that dialogue can be established and that the young people can express their grievances in a peaceful way and, if possible, have those concerns heard".

At least 24 killed in Ukraine, Zelenskiy condemns one of Russia’s most ‘vile strikes’

By Olena Harmash and Vladyslav Smilianets
KYIV, Oct 7 (Reuters) – Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most “vile strikes” on Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, killing at least 24 people, including children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure.

The heaviest death toll was in Pryluky in Ukraine’s northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile obliterated a five-storey residential building. At least 18 people, including four children, were killed there, local officials said.

Zelenskiy said the strike coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s birthday.

Show Full Article

“Today, as a birthday ‘gift’ to Putin, the Russian army destroyed a residential building in Pryluky…,” Zelenskiy said, adding that six more people were also killed in Kyiv, Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the massive attack.

In total, Russia fired 70 missiles at Ukraine overnight – many of them high-velocity ballistic munitions – and dozens of Shahed attack drones, he said.

“The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively. This was one of the most vile strikes.”

In Pryluky, an excavator and dozens of rescuers with shovels sifted through rubble at the site where several sections of the apartment block had collapsed.

Emergency workers used ladders to get to the upper floors of what remained of the building, and brought out 15 people alive as they worked their way down through the rubble. Around 55 people were wounded in the town, regional officials said.

“There’s a lot of destruction, especially in the town centre,” said Danylo Savenko, deputy mayor of Pryluky, who said he had run to an air raid shelter with his wife as soon as he heard the missiles flying.

BIG JUMP IN REPORTED DRONE INTERCEPTIONS

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had carried out a “massive strike” on military-industrial facilities in Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions, using high-precision land-, sea- and air-launched weapons, as well as drones.

Ukraine’s air force said it had downed just over 80% of the 46 jet-powered drones launched by Russia — a sharp increase from recent weeks when, on average, air defences took down 50% to 60%.

Since the summer, Russia has used increasing numbers of the new high-velocity drones in round-the-clock attacks on Kyiv and other cities, with Ukraine’s air defences struggling to cope with their speed.

The air force did not explain the jump in the interception rate and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Zelenskiy said the Russian ballistic missiles remained the major challenge for Ukraine, adding that he and his team were “every day looking for Patriot (missile interception) systems that can and must protect people’s lives”.

Ukraine received a new €1.2 billion ($1.34 billion) tranche from the European Union on Wednesday and will channel the funds towards defence needs, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said.

The US-made Patriot system is the only weapon in Ukraine’s arsenal capable of stopping high-velocity ballistic missiles but tight global supplies have been drained by the Iran war as well as the Ukraine conflict.

Russia’s defence ministry said its targets included sites where Ukrainian defence company Fire Point manufactures and stores its Flamingo cruise missiles and medium- and long-range drones in Kyiv as well as regions of Kyiv, Chernihiv, Kirovohrad, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava and Kharkiv.

Last week Zelenskiy said Ukraine had fired its first domestically made ballistic missile in combat, produced by Fire Point. In an interview with Reuters, he said he expected the company to have a longer-range FP-9 missile ready by the autumn. Fire Point has said that weapon will be able to reach Moscow.

PEOPLE SHELTER OVERNIGHT IN KYIV METRO

Zelenskiy said Ukrainian troops hit four targets in Russia over the past 24 hours, including two Russian oil facilities and a training ground in the Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions.

In the Reuters interview, Zelenskiy said Ukraine would hit Russia’s energy assets in response to Moscow’s escalating strikes on civilian infrastructure.

Ukrainian officials and military intelligence shared warnings of the upcoming attacks on Wednesday, and many Kyiv residents took shelter in the city’s deep underground metro stations.

Several loud explosions reverberated through the capital during the night.

“The metro is better because we live on the 9th floor of a high-rise, and it’s really scary when you’re on the 9th floor and missiles are flying at you,” Lesia, a 49-year-old Kyiv resident, told Reuters.

Ukrainian officials said Russian ballistic missiles as well as the drones had targeted Kyiv.

Overnight air strikes on the southeastern city of Dnipro damaged an industrial facility, transport infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia and apartment buildings in Kremenchuk, regional officials said on the Telegram messaging app.

($1 = 0.8947 euros)

(Reporting by Olena Harmash in Kyiv and Vladislav Smilianets in Pryluky, additional reporting by Yuliia Dysa, Jekaterīna Golubkova; Editing by Daniel Flynn, Andrew Heavens and Gareth Jones)

items.title: Christa Pike 'angry and confused' about Tennessee's failed execution effort, lawyers say
items.author: Jonathan Allen
items.creator: Jonathan Allen
items.summary: Christa Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving Tennessee's botched effort to execute her, her lawyers said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Christa Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in a hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving Tennessee's botched effort to execute her, her lawyers said on Wednesday.
A week ago, Pike, 50, was taken from the execution chamber to a Nashville hospital, unconscious, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two injections of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital [USN:L1N45N0VS TEXT:"failed to kill her"] at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution.
As late as Monday, her lawyers believed Pike was brain dead and that life support would be removed the next day following the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, which has renewed scrutiny of capital punishment in the US .
"But on Tuesday, to the shock of everyone, including me, including her team, and including the medical team, Christa woke up and began talking," Randall Spivey, one of her lawyers, told reporters after a court hearing on Wednesday, where a judge ordered Tennessee officials to preserve syringes and other evidence from the botched execution.
"She is angry and confused about everything right now," Spivey said. "She is very aware that the state tried to execute her."
Governor Bill Lee has suspended all executions for the rest of the year while investigators look into the botched executions of Pike and of Tony Carruthers in May, when prison officials were unable to set up intravenous lines.
Pike remains very sick and shackled to her hospital bed, facing a long road to recovery, her lawyers said. She cannot swallow or eat, has pneumonia, cannot move her "tremendously swollen" hands or arms, and it is unclear if she will regain her lost mobility, they said.
Although she still has "cognitive confusion," the lawyers said, she has been speaking with those around her.
"She has wanted to know what's happened, and she's asked about several people," Spivey said. "She's asked about the victim's family."
Pike was sentenced to death for her role as a teenager in the 1995 torture and murder of her 19-year-old schoolmate Colleen Slemmer.
She is the first person known to have survived a "completed execution attempt" in the US, her lawyers say, calling it a violation of the Constitution's prohibition on cruel and unusual punishments.
A UNIQUE CASE Pike's lawyers are unexpectedly continuing their litigation against state officials, seeking to pierce the secrecy that normally surrounds execution procedures in Tennessee and other states.
Earlier on Wednesday, a judge in Davidson County Chancery Court, I'Ashea Myles, agreed to order Tennessee officials to preserve all evidence from the failed execution, including syringes, drug packaging and lot numbers, catheters, intravenous lines and gurney restraints.
The all-female execution team requested by Pike used at least seven needles during a grueling ordeal that lasted more than two hours, and one needle was bent 90 degrees when it was pulled out, her lawyers said.
Myles largely sided with Pike's lawyers at the end of Wednesday's hearing, describing the litigation, which began in January in an effort to prevent the scheduled execution, as unusual because no one had anticipated Pike surviving.
"This case is unique, to say the least," Myles said.
She also ordered the state to preserve internal communications about the attempted execution, including incident reports, witness accounts and encrypted messages.
She has yet to rule on a request by Pike's lawyers that the Tennessee Department of Correction let them take any residual traces of the execution drugs for chemical analysis.
The Tennessee Department of Correction has opposed what it says is a "duplicative and unnecessary" preservation order, arguing it is already legally required to preserve all evidence and that it was already willing to share most, if not all, of what Pike's lawyers sought.
Tennessee and other US states have long struggled to acquire execution drugs. They cannot be obtained from major pharmaceutical companies because of a European trade ban on companies that sell products for use in torture or executions.
Tennessee, like other states, has turned to small, largely unregulated compounding pharmacies to make small batches of the drugs, promising to hide their identity.
"Today's hearing was about transparency, about why Christa, the courts, the media and the public should not simply take the state's word about what happened last Wednesday," Luke Ihnen, another lawyer for Pike, told reporters after the judge's ruling.
He repeated the demand that Tennessee Governor Bill Lee commute Pike's sentence to life in prison and never attempt to execute her again. A spokesperson for Lee, who denied a clemency appeal two days before the failed execution, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Pike's lawyers had sought an alternative to lethal injections, saying her small veins and related medical conditions made her afraid that something would go wrong.

FAST

Oct 7 : Teens spend under 15 minutes a day on average on ChatGPT, while less than 2 per cent of them interact with the chatbot for over three straight hours, OpenAI said, as technology companies face scrutiny over the risks AI chatbots pose to children.
Sam Altman's AI company released the figures in its first report on teen use on Wednesday as rapid adoption of AI platforms raises concerns about their impact on adolescent mental health and developmental safety.
Such worries have been amplified by research on social media's harms to young users, with Meta in August agreeing to pay up to $18 billion and limit teens' use of Facebook and Instagram to settle claims that it designed the platforms to addict children.
OpenAI said in nearly half of teen conversations where a break reminder appeared, the user either took a break or ended the chat within five minutes, aiming to show that its steps to regulate teen usage were working.

The company said users with access to its dedicated teen version sent more education-related messages and used tools like learning visualizations and Study Mode.
It is now looking to add a college application planning tool that would help students with requirements, deadlines and financial-aid steps, as well as new study features such as flashcards and easier quiz-making tools.
OpenAI began rolling out ChatGPT for Teens in August. The mode turns on automatically based on age information or when a user is estimated to be under 18, allowing parental controls and limiting conversations on sensitive topics.
But a report by non-profit Common Sense Media on Wednesday said ChatGPT for Teens often alerted parents late or not at all when teen accounts held conversations about suicide, self-harm or eating disorders.
The study, which is based on more than a dozen accounts created for testing, found the chatbot did not reliably suggest a crisis hotline or professional help.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the testing does not "accurately reflect" how ChatGPT's teen safeguards work. Citing security and scale as reasons, the company said it may take hours for parent and teen accounts to link and for safety alerts to be active.
"The bulk of their testing may have begun and concluded before activation of parental controls was complete," the spokesperson said.
Common Sense Media said some of its test accounts were linked for long enough and some were not, but none of them produced timely alerts. Notifications only came through for accounts with weeks of sensitive-topic history, it said.

Source: Reuters

items.body:
David Milliken

[ロンドン ７日 ロイター] - ７日の英国債市場では、世界的な債券売りを受けて、３０年債利回りが一時２８年ぶりの高水準に上昇した。同国ではヒーリー財務相が３週間後に控える初の予算案発表に向けた圧力が一段と高まっている。   

英３０年債利回りは１３４１ＧＭＴ（日本時間午後１０時４１分）に１３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し６．０３６％と、１９９８年１月以来の高水準に達した。１日の上昇幅としては８月１４日以来の大きさとなる見通し。

英２０年債利回りも同様に過去最高水準に迫った。英１０年債利回りは１０ｂｐ上昇の５．４８％となった。 

ヒーリー財務相は１０月２８日に初の予算案を発表する。バンク・オブ・アメリカのエコノミストは６日、ヒーリー財務相の予算案により、今会計年度および２０２７／２８年度にそれぞれ公的借り入れが１５０億ポンド（１９９億ドル）増加し、長期的な予算目標の達成に向けた余地が狭まるとの見方を示した。

［リスボン　７日　ロイター］ - 欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのペレイラ・ポルトガル中銀総裁は７日、ユーロ圏の現在のインフレ率は、ロシアによるウクライナ侵攻を起因とする２０２２年のエネルギー危機の際に見られた水準を大幅に下回っており、現時点で二次的な波及効果は見られないと述べた。

ペレイラ氏はリスボンでの記者会見で、その他のモノの価格に関しても足元でインフレ期待が不安定化している様子は見られないと指摘。２２年と現在のインフレの状況を比較すると、ユーロ圏とポルトガルのいずれにおいても「違いは顕著だ」とし、「総合インフレ率、コアインフレ率ともに現在は２２年を大幅に下回る水準にある」と語った。

items.title: 米1年先インフレ期待3.9％、23年5月以来の高水準＝ＮＹ連銀9月調査
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク　７日　ロイター] - 米ニューヨーク連銀が７日発表した９月の消費者調査によると、米国民の現在および将来の家計状況に対する見方が悪化する中、１年先のインフレ期待が３年超ぶりの高水準となった。

１年先のインフレ期待は３．９％と、前月の３．６％から上昇し、２０２３年５月以来の高水準となった。３年先のインフレ期待は３．３％と、前月の３．２％から上昇。５年先のインフレ期待は３．０％で横ばいだった。 

ガソリン、食料品、家賃、医療費、大学費用など、同連銀が追跡する全カテゴリーについて、家計は将来的に値上がりすると予想した。

連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）当局者の多くは、足元のインフレ高止まりの主な要因として、トランプ大統領の関税措置の継続的な影響と中東での戦争に起因する原油価格の急騰、さらにテクノロジー分野における過熱した投資ペースによる圧力を挙げている。 

一方、労働市場に対する見通しは若干改善し、１年後に失業率が上昇しているとの見方は前月から弱まった。また、非自発的に失業した場合に新たな職を見つけられる確率は高まった。

また、家計消費支出の伸び見通しは前月から上昇し、２３年５月以来の高水準となった。

US FCC to vote on advancing new spectrum auction to boost 'direct to device' services

WASHINGTON, Oct 7 : The US Federal Communications Commission said on Wednesday that it will vote on October 29 on whether to advance a new auction of wireless spectrum to boost "direct-to-device" services.
The FCC told Reuters it will also hold an initial vote on modernizing its rules for "direct-to-device" services and to finalize rules to allow drone operations within the 800 MHz cellular band. 
Direct-to-device satellite technology allows smartphones and other devices to connect directly to satellites and is being developed by SpaceX, Amazon's Leo and others.
The FCC in January said it was approving SpaceX's request to deploy another 7,500 second-generation Starlink satellites as it works to boost internet service worldwide, bringing the total to 15,000 satellites.

"The ‘direct-to-device’ proposals work to continue leveraging this cutting-edge tech to end cell phone dead zones and provide service directly from next-gen satellite constellations to your smartphone," FCC Chair Brendan Carr said in a statement.
Carr said last month that a series of upcoming wireless spectrum auctions over the next couple of years could generate more than $100 billion in proceeds.
The FCC is proposing to auction 25-megahertz of key spectrum for direct to device operations and make an additional 482 megahertz of spectrum available for supplemental coverage from space and consider other regulatory changes to promote more flexible terrestrial, satellite, and hybrid business arrangements for direct to device service.
 SpaceX acquired 65 megahertz of wireless spectrum from EchoStar opens new tab for $19.6 billion through two deals announced last year, giving Starlink airwaves to expand into mobile services. The commission late Tuesday approved SpaceX's plan to use new spectrum it acquired to expand its direct to device plans.
SpaceX's ambition to build a full-fledged mobile service rattled investors in the US wireless sector after the company in August outlined plans that could eventually pit Starlink against the three major US telecoms.
Last week, AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon named wireless industry veteran Paul Roth as interim chief executive of their new joint venture aimed at expanding satellite-enabled mobile coverage.
The FCC last week moved to release more spectrum to boost in-home satellite broadband.

items.title: Monedas cotizan dispares ante avance del dólar; bolsas caen siguiendo a Wall Street
items.author: Manuel Farías
items.creator: Manuel Farías
items.summary: La principales monedas de América Latina cerraron mixtas el miércoles, en una jornada de avance del dólar en los mercados globales, luego de que más temprano de los precios del crudo subieron y provocaron temores por la inflación, y tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de la Reserva Federal.
items.body:
La principales monedas de América Latina cerraron mixtas el miércoles, en una jornada de avance del dólar en los mercados globales, luego de que más temprano de los precios del crudo subieron y provocaron temores por la inflación, y tras la divulgación de las minutas de la última reunión de la Reserva Federal.
* Las bolsas, en tanto, bajaron en línea con el descenso de Wall Street, que también comenzaba a girar su atención hacia los resultados corporativos del tercer trimestre.
* El índice dólar , que mide el desempeño del billete verde frente a una canasta de seis monedas pares, trepó un 0,35%, y tras recortar brevemente sus ganancias, volvió a repuntar después de conocerse las minutas de la Fed.
* Los responsables de la política monetaria de la Fed estuvieron divididos el mes pasado respecto de los motivos para subir las tasas de interés, mostraron el miércoles las minutas de la reunión de septiembre.
* "Algunos participantes" consideraron que el alza era necesaria para contener el impacto de las perturbaciones de los precios de la energía y otros factores, mientras que un núcleo más "duro" la vio como imprescindible para protegerse de una inflación emergente impulsada por la demanda.
* Pese a que datos económicos y algunos comentarios de autoridades de la Fed han reducido las expectativas de un incremento del costo del crédito a finales de octubre, los mercados descuentan un alza para diciembre.
* Los retornos de los bonos del Tesoro, en tanto, revirtieron sus avances por la tarde, tras alcanzar nuevos máximos en décadas, ante el descenso de los precios del petróleo y una sólida subasta de notas a 10 años.
* El crudo cambió de tendencia y cayó el miércoles, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas y dar prioridad al diésel.
* El peso mexicano bajaba hacia el cierre un ligero 0,05%, a 17,9855 unidades por dólar, luego de tres sesiones de alzas; mientras que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, descendió un 1,04%, a 64.632,80 puntos, también después de tres avances consecutivos.
* "Hacia el 'overnight', prevemos un rango entre $17,89 y $18,10, ante la moderación del dólar estadounidense a mitad de jornada, a la espera de la publicación de las cifras de inflación de septiembre y de las minutas de Banxico el día de mañana", dijo Monex en un reporte.
* El real brasileño cayó un 0,83%, a 5,0156 unidades por dólar la venta, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) retrocedió preliminarmente un 0,72%, a 204.348 puntos, en una jornada de ajustes tras las fuertes alzas del lunes luego del resultado de la primera ronda de las elecciones presidenciales del domingo, donde Flávio Bolsonaro superó a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
* El peso chileno , cerró la jornada con una baja del 0,63%, a 978,20/978,50 unidades por dólar, presionado por el avance global del billete verde. Asimismo, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) retrocedió un 1,47%, a 10.999,64 puntos.
* El peso colombiano cedió parte de sus alzas de más temprano y cerró con una leve alza de un 0,08% a 3.239 unidades por dólar; mientras que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el COLCAP (.COLCAP) , terminó con caída de un 2,09% a 2.534,9 puntos.
* Los agentes locales permanecían a la expectativa del dato de inflación de septiembre, que apuntaba a un aumento, elevando las expectativas del mercado de un nuevo incremento en la tasa de interés este mes.
* El peso mayorista argentino cambió de tendencia y se apreció un 0,13%, a 1.518 por cada dólar, con el banco central (BCRA) regulando la liquidez e interviniendo en la plaza de contratos de futuros para frenar bruscas fluctuaciones intradiarias.
* El BCRA compró 45 millones de dólares y suma algo más de 14.700 millones de dólares adquiridos, contra los 10.000 millones comprometidos en un acuerdo vigente con el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI).
* Mientras, el índice accionario líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires retrocedió un 2,51% al cierre, luego de acumular un alza del 3,7% en los dos primeros días de la semana.
* La moneda peruana, el sol , se depreció un 0,29%, a 3,4440/3,4450 unidades por dólar. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) perdió un 1,31%, a 1.571,13 puntos.

items.title: ＩＥＡ、備蓄放出加速で1億バレル供給へ　ディーゼル優先
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kate Abnett　Holger Hansen

[ブリュッセル／パリ　７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Kate Abnett　Holger Hansen

[ブリュッセル／パリ　７日　ロイター] - 国際エネルギー機関（ＩＥＡ）は７日、中東情勢を背景にした燃料価格の高騰と供給混乱に対応するため、３月に開始した戦略石油備蓄放出を加速させるとともに、ディーゼル（軽油）の備蓄放出を優先する方針で合意した。

ＩＥＡは３月、過去最大規模となる４億バレルの備蓄放出を開始したが、このうち約１億バレルが市場にまだ供給されていない。ＩＥＡはこの日、備蓄放出を可能な限り迅速に進めることで、この約１億バレルが市場に届くとの見通しを示した。ディーゼルを優先するとしたものの、ディーゼルと原油の内訳は明らかにしていない。

主要７カ国（Ｇ７）は２日、世界のエネルギー市場の安定化に向けＩＥＡを通じてディーゼルなどの備蓄１億バレルを協調放出するとする首脳共同声明を発表。Ｇ７はトランプ米大統領がディーゼルを多く市場に供給しなければ米国からの軽油輸出を禁止する可能性があると警告したことを受け、協調放出方針を発表した。

ＩＥＡのこの日の表明はＧ７の協調放出の発表を受けたもので、ＩＥＡのビロル事務局長は声明で「ＩＥＡ加盟国は３月の共同対応で発表した備蓄放出を加速させ、可能な限り早期に完了させることを支持した。現在のディーゼル市場の逼迫状況を踏まえ、可能な範囲でディーゼル備蓄の放出を優先することも支持した」とした。

ＩＥＡは来週に開かれる理事会で今回示した方針について検証する。

ＩＥＡの発表を受け、欧州連合（ＥＵ）加盟国は今後の備蓄放出は３月に承認された数量の範囲内で実施されるべきとの認識で一致。また、フランスは戦略備蓄から１０００万バレルのディーゼルを放出すると発表した。

WASHINGTON, Oct 7 : A Democratic member of the Federal Communications Commission urged the agency on Wednesday not to approve a petition to allow political AI-generated robocalls from conservative political group Club for Growth.
The group, which is spending millions of dollars ahead of the November US congressional elections, asked the FCC to allow it to make political calls to cell phones "using an artificial or prerecorded voice - including an AI-generated voice - without obtaining prior express consent."
FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez said that if "the FCC allows a dark money group to flood Americans' phones with AI-generated robocalls they never agreed to receive, it would bring chaos so close to Election Day." 
She added that "consumers reasonably expect the rules protecting them from unwanted robocalls to hold steady while they decide how to vote, not for the FCC to change them at the 11th hour to unleash a deluge of political AI slop on their phones."

Club for Growth President David McIntosh said in a statement that the group wants "the FCC to treat First Amendment-protected political speech the same way it already treats wireless calls about package deliveries, bank accounts, and doctor's appointments."
The group, which backs conservative economic views on taxes, regulations and cutting the size of government, plans to spend $175 million in the midterm congressional elections, it said on its website.
The group argued it is incorrect to refer to the calls as robocalls because a human initiates the dial to a cell phone and then an AI agent handles an interview.
The FCC, in describing the petition, said the system "uses a perfunctory human being for the sole purpose of clicking on a ‘send’ or similarly termed button to transmit thousands of text messages per hour."
A number of public interest groups on Monday urged the FCC not to grant the petition.
"Using robocalls, a hated form of communication, to deliver political messages, a sensitive topic almost nobody wants to hear about from AI-generated strangers, will enrage a wide swath of the 98 per cent of the country that has a cellphone," said the comment signed by groups including the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights, Consumer Federation of America, Common Cause and Public Citizen.
The FCC is considering comments on the petition until October 19. A spokesman for FCC Chair Brendan Carr declined immediate comment.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Spanish unions call general strike for November 11, weeks before snap election
items.author: Mireia Merino, David Latona
items.creator: Mireia Merino, David Latona
items.summary: Trade unions in Spain on Wednesday announced a nationwide general strike over housing issues for November 11, a protest that will take place a few weeks before a snap election in which rising rents and evictions have become campaign topics.
items.body:
Trade unions in Spain on Wednesday announced a nationwide general strike over housing issues for November 11, a protest that will take place a few weeks before a [USN:L8N45R0GH TEXT:"snap election"] in which rising rents and evictions [USN:L8N45Q06Q TEXT:"have become campaign topics"].
The country's two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, said they had agreed on the date, although it still needs to be formally ratified by other unions in a meeting later on Wednesday. It will be the first general strike jointly backed by Spain's two largest unions in 14 years.
The strike will be the latest in a series of demonstrations provoked by the [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"eviction of an 87-year-old woman"] in Madrid, with activists camping on one of the capital's main squares calling for solutions to a mounting housing crisis.
Those protests, along with [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"parliament's rejection last week"] of decrees aimed at curbing evictions and limiting rent pressures, prompted Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call an [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"early election"] for November 29.
Sanchez is seeking to shift the political narrative from his government's [USN:L1N4510WI TEXT:"handling of a migrant crisis"] in Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta and a [USN:L1N42U0KB TEXT:"series of corruption cases"] involving his Socialist Party and his family to the housing crisis, an area in which he believes he can harness growing resentment about rising rents.
Spain has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set to grow to more than a million by 2028, according to the Bank of Spain.
With fewer people able to afford a home, renting has increased sharply, putting pressure on that market. The average rental price of €1,176 ($1,315) is equivalent to about 98.7% of a young person's average monthly salary in Spain, according to the Youth Council of Spain.
"We cannot ignore the fact that housing is where most of our wages go. What is the point of raising the minimum wage if housing costs are rising three, four or five times faster?" said Tenants' Union spokesperson Valeria Racu.
($1 = 0.8946 euros)

items.summary: ［ブリュッセル　７日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ブリュッセル　７日　ロイター］ - ユーロ圏の高官は７日、フランス経済は非常に堅調でいかなる課題にも対応する能力があるとの見解を示し、国債利回り上昇の影響が他のユーロ圏の経済に広がる兆候は今のところ見られていないと述べた。

ユーロ圏財務相会議の準備に携わる高官は「これまで目にしているのはニュースに反応したフランス国債利回りの動きであり、その反応はおおむね理解できる」と語った。

フランスの金融システムは「非常に堅固だ」と指摘し、「政治的に複雑な状況にあるものの、問題解決の選択肢はあり、特に心配はしていない」と述べた。その上で、「責任ある予算を毎年成立させることができる均衡点を見いだす必要がある。それぞれの政治勢力が駆け引きを止め、経済に対する責任に真摯に向き合う必要がある」と強調した。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary:
Jonathan Saul

[ロンドン　７日　ロイター] - 湾岸諸国の産油国による輸出拡大が進む中、ホルムズ海峡を通過するタンカーへの攻撃が先週、週単位ではイラン戦争開始以降で最多となった。海事安全保障筋が明らかにした。

items.body:
Jonathan Saul

[ロンドン　７日　ロイター] - 湾岸諸国の産油国による輸出拡大が進む中、ホルムズ海峡を通過するタンカーへの攻撃が先週、週単位ではイラン戦争開始以降で最多となった。海事安全保障筋が明らかにした。 

３人の安全保障筋が同地域から得た情報を基に分析したデータによると、９月２８日─１０月５日までの１週間に、ホルムズ海峡周辺で原油タンカーや液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）、液化石油ガス（ＬＰＧ）のタンカーに対する攻撃は少なくとも１２件発生した。 関係筋によると、これは２月２８日に米国とイランの戦争が始まって以来、１週間あたりの攻撃件数としては最多となる。

米国主導による多国籍の共同海事情報センター（ＪＭＩＣ）は４日付の報告書で、同海峡では、イランの「革命防衛隊（ＩＲＧＣ）」による攻撃や攻撃未遂のほか、ドローン（無人機）の上空通過、監視活動、ＶＨＦ無線による呼びかけなどの嫌がらせ行為が続いていると説明。「こうした行動は、主要な輸送路沿いで存在感を示し、通航する船舶への圧力を維持しようとするイランの意図を引き続き示している」と指摘した。

国連の国際海事機関（ＩＭＯ）がまとめた別のデータによると、同週に船舶が関与した事案は９件だった。海事関係筋は、ＩＭＯは事案の確認や公式記録に時間がかかる傾向があると指摘した。

ＩＭＯの別のデータによると、件数で比較可能な直近の週は７月１３日の週で、発生した事案は８件だった。

items.title: Denmark says Russia has conducted sabotage attacks against its defense firms
items.author: Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen
items.creator: Jacob Grønholt-Pedersen
items.summary: Russia has begun sabotage operations against Danish companies supplying Ukraine after concluding that broader disruption efforts failed to curb Western military support for the country, a Danish intelligence official said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Russia has begun sabotage operations against Danish companies supplying Ukraine after concluding that broader disruption efforts failed to curb Western military support for the country, a Danish intelligence official said on Wednesday.
The shift reflects a significant escalation in Moscow's [USN:L8N45F1L2 TEXT:"hybrid warfare"] campaign, the official, from the Danish national security and intelligence service (PET), told a homeland security conference in Copenhagen.
"What we saw in the spring was a lot of planning, but very little carried out; what we saw in early summer is that they started to carry out a lot more," the official said.
Russia concluded that its previous broad-spectrum targeting "did not have the effect of deterring the Western (military alliance) NATO from supporting Ukraine," the official added, and while Moscow maintains political control over operations, its operational boldness is growing and Russia is now "trying to hit targets that have a direct impact on the front line. That means weapons production."
Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. The Russian embassy in Copenhagen rejected the allegations on Wednesday, accusing Danish authorities of making unfounded accusations against Russia.
The official cited a [USN:L1N40Y0RY TEXT:"Russian defence ministry list"] of alleged European drone and drone component manufacturers that Moscow said in April amounted to potential military targets, without elaborating further.
Russia is increasingly using [USN:L1N44V0FB TEXT:"untrained proxies"] — including homeless people and people addicted to drugs — recruited via Telegram and other social media platforms. Recruitment typically starts with low-threshold tasks such as reconnaissance or photography, then escalates toward actual sabotage operations, PET has said.
"It could be anyone just looking for quick money," the official said. "If the first person isn't successful, they'll throw another one at the problem until they succeed."
Denmark's defence intelligence service last month said Russia is likely to [USN:L8N45G0M0 TEXT:"intensify hybrid attacks"] against the West in coming months, after Germany blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack at [USN:L8N44T1P2 TEXT:"Leipzig/Halle Airport"] in August.
In September 2025, before Denmark hosted an EU summit, [USN:L5N3VG0CN TEXT:"drones disrupted air traffic"] at six Danish airports, including Copenhagen, the Nordic region's busiest, in what Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen called a hybrid attack on her nation.

items.title: Webull sinks after US House panel report flags China ties
items.author: Jayasree Prabhu
items.creator: Jayasree Prabhu
items.summary: Shares of Webull dropped to a near-four-month low on Wednesday after a US congressional panel said the online trading platform was "tied in structural ways" to the Chinese government, prompting a strong rebuke from the company.
items.body:
Shares of Webull (BULL.O) dropped to a near-four-month low on Wednesday after a US congressional panel said the online trading platform was "tied in structural ways" to the Chinese government, prompting a strong rebuke from the company.
The bipartisan House Select Committee on China said in a report released on Wednesday that it found "a profound gap" between the company's public marketing and actual control, sending Webull's shares plummeting 19.1%.
The findings underscore growing scrutiny of Chinese links to companies operating in key areas of the US economy, including financial services.
"Webull has made every effort to cooperate with the Committee, but did not hear from them for more than 20 months before this report was released," a company spokesperson said.
"It is deeply disappointing that the Select Committee published a report containing significant inaccuracies and unsupported conclusions without ever seeking clarification from Webull," the spokesperson added, noting that the company stores US customer data in the US.
CNBC first reported the details of the congressional panel's report earlier on Wednesday.
"Using technology providers in mainland China and an opaque China-linked ownership structure, Webull exposes its data to our foremost adversary. Investors should heed this information when choosing who they do business with," said John Moolenaar, who is leading the committee with Ro Khanna.
Analysts at Scotiabank said the near-term question is whether the findings prompt executive agencies or financial regulators to initiate or broaden their own reviews.
"For now, the report will weigh on valuation rather than actual financial results," the brokerage said.
A TENSE RELATIONSHIP While the US and China have been under a tariff truce for about a year, tensions remain. Last week, Congressman Ro Khanna, a Democrat, warned that [USN:L1N45M17H TEXT:"Beijing could steal"] AI model weights developed by OpenAI, Anthropic and other top US firms, erasing the US edge over China.
"I want to emphasize that protectionism does not make the US more competitive. China firmly opposes the US overstretching the concept of national security," a spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in the US said in an emailed statement to Reuters.
Chinese President Xi Jinping has also described the relationship between the two superpowers through the "Thucydides Trap," a theory that competition between a rising power and an established one tends to lead to war.
US President Donald Trump's lavish three-day summit last month for President Xi [USN:L1N45G0E0 TEXT:"delivered no breakthroughs"] on thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the war with Iran.
"The potential regulatory and operational implications of these findings create a level of uncertainty that we cannot reasonably incorporate into our estimates," Siebert Financial analyst Brian Vieten said, while suspending his buy rating and price target on Webull's stock.

items.title: 米政府とグーグル、メタＣＥＯのバイオハブに参画　生物学ＡＩに18億ドル投資へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Krystal Hu

[７日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Krystal Hu

[７日　ロイター] - 米政府と米メタ・プラットフォームズ、グーグル親会社のアルファベットが、非営利研究機関「バイオハブ」に参画し、生物学研究用の人工知能（ＡＩ）モデルの学習に向けたオープンデータセットの構築に乗り出す。この取り組みへの投資総額は１８億ドルに達する見通し。バイオハブが７日に明らかにした。

「バイオハブ」にはメタ、グーグル傘下グーグル・ディープマインド、創薬スタートアップのアイソモルフィックラボが共同で３億ドルを投じる。米エネルギー省は実験室での測定、モデリング、計算に今後５年間で５億ドル超を拠出する。また、米国立衛生研究所（ＮＩＨ）は、５億ドル超の連邦資金でこれまでに構築されたデータセットとリポジトリを調整し、バイオハブがこれらをＡＩの訓練用に標準化する。

バイオハブはメタのマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）と妻のプリシラ・チャン氏による慈善事業として運営されている。

モデル訓練向けの生物学データの獲得を巡っては、アンソロピックやオープンＡＩも同様の取り組みを進めている。アンソロピックはＡＩ技術を応用した医薬品開発の本格化に向け、生物学の研究を行うための実験施設（ウェットラボ）を開設した。オープンＡＩ財団はＡＩ研究向けの生物・医療データセット構築のため、１億２５００万ドル超の助成プログラムを開始した。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ドバイ ７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ドバイ ７日 ロイター] - イラン当局者は７日、同国の核開発計画に関する米国の「要求や構想」はイラン側の要求と相いれないとの認識を示した。

バンス米副大統領が、イランは米国の要求を満たし７カ月に及ぶ戦争を終結させるためには、ウラン濃縮能力を「意味のある形で」削減する必要があるとの考えを示したことについて、当局者はロイターに対し、「バンス氏の発言は米政権の考えや要求を反映したものだ。米国側には要求を示し、自らの考えを持つ自由があるが、その内容はイランの要求とは相いれない」と語った。

さらに、イランの核開発計画を巡り、米国との交渉は一切行われておらず、核協議を開始するには米国がイラン側の条件を満たす必要があると述べた。また、核濃縮に関する条件はイランにとっての「レッドライン（越えられない一線）」であり、「この点についてはいかなる形でも柔軟性を示すことはない」とした。ただ、濃縮の詳細を巡り後日協議することは可能との認識も示した。

PARIS, Oct 7 : Revolut will cover the cost of customers wanting to change their identity documents after the London-based bank was tricked into giving hackers the data of hundreds of customers, the company's CEO for Western Europe said on Wednesday.
Revolut, Europe's most valuable startup, said it had sent the customers' personal data to hackers who had taken control of an Italian government agency email address, in an incident first disclosed last month. 
Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier, Revolut's CEO for Western Europe, told BFM TV in an interview that the company would not pay ransoms to hackers, when asked if they had paid one. Revolut previously said it had not received a ransom demand.
Cossa-Dumurgier said Revolut had provided assistance for the 680 affected clients, 55 of whom are in France.

"If they ever have to change their ID documents, we're taking care of the associated costs", she added, without specifying whether this had happened yet or how much it could cost the company.
Financial institutions are required to send customer data to authorities when asked to do so as part of investigations into potential crimes.
Matteo Piantedosi, Italy's interior minister, told lawmakers on September 30 that the email address to which Revolut sent customer data came from the Reggio Calabria police's email system, but was an address that had never been used before.
Revolut could have and should have verified the request by doing minimal due diligence, the minister said.
A spokesperson for Revolut declined to comment on the interior minister's remarks.
Cossa-Dumurgier said that government agencies are sometimes the "weak link" in the system and that Revolut's own systems had not been compromised.

Analysis:Crypto donors navigate mid-term spending dilemma after Senate bill defeat

Oct 7 : After suffering a major legislative defeat at the hands of Senate Democrats last month, the crypto industry is grappling with a dilemma three weeks out from the November election: punish Democrats, or preserve the bipartisan ties it has spent years building.
During the current and previous election cycles, the industry has spent more than $300 million backing crypto-friendly Democrats and Republicans in roughly equal measure, hoping to pass legislation US crypto companies say will put them on a solid legal footing and allow them to thrive.
That strategy paid off with last year's new law promoting dollar-backed cryptocurrencies, but suffered a major blow last month when all Senate Democrats and a handful of Republicans voted against advancing the Clarity Act, which the industry says would have provided the legal clarity it has long lobbied for.
US President Donald Trump's personal crypto ventures became a flashpoint in the bill negotiations, prompting Democrats to push for tougher restrictions on officeholders' crypto dealings. Their decision to vote against the bill despite winning many concessions angered crypto executives, while the broader fight has made crypto more of a partisan issue, said analysts.

Nine Democrats are up for reelection in the Senate, including some the industry had viewed as allies. With polls showing the party has a slight edge, the crypto industry is weighing whether to continue with its bipartisan strategy in the Senate, or to reward Republicans, who overwhelmingly supported Clarity, said four executives involved in the discussions.
While it's unlikely a Democratic-led Senate will pass crypto legislation, turning the midterms into a referendum on Clarity could squander years of relationship-building and alienate lawmakers who may be in power next year, some executives warn.
“It's a pretty hard needle to thread," said Ron Hammond, head of policy and advocacy at crypto trading firm Wintermute, adding that the big crypto spenders have been "navigating this very carefully."
CRYPTO HAS PUNISHED ADVERSARIES BEFORE
Fairshake, a crypto super PAC backed by Coinbase and Ripple among others, started the year with $193 million. On Monday, it said it would back 32 House candidates spanning both parties, but has not announced a Senate strategy. It has spent on 57 races this cycle, winning many.
“Fairshake has always been and always will be an issue-focused organization. We back pro-crypto candidates who support American innovation in both parties," said spokesperson Geoff Vetter.
Crypto PACs have previously targeted vulnerable adversaries. In 2024, Fairshake spent about $40 million successfully unseating former incumbent Ohio Senate Democrat Sherrod Brown, who criticized the industry's Washington influence. In a sign of what may come, the PAC is spending $30 million opposing his bid to return to the Senate.
Digital Freedom Fund, a super PAC backed by crypto entrepreneurs Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, is also spending $3 million opposing Brown and supporting current Ohio Republican Senator Jon Husted, who voted for Clarity, federal filings show.
It's also spending $400,000 in the race for Iowa's open Senate seat, splitting the cash between backing pro-crypto Republican Ashley Hinson and opposing her Democratic rival.
Spokespeople for the Winklevoss twins and Hinson did not respond to requests for comment. Ripple declined to comment.
A spokesperson for Brown's campaign accused Husted of being "for sale." A Husted campaign spokesperson said Brown was "terrified of having his abysmal record splashed across TV screens."
Until recently, the industry's aggressive spending made candidates think twice about crossing it, analysts say, but executives worry it's a risky strategy, especially against incumbents. Many believe crypto can still be a bipartisan issue and that the industry should find ways to settle scores without jeopardizing those ties.
Among those up for reelection, for example, are New Jersey's Cory Booker and Virginia's Mark Warner, both senior Democratic lawmakers whom the industry sees as key allies. They broadly supported crypto legislation but ultimately opposed Clarity, citing insufficient curbs on officeholder crypto dealings.
Warner and Booker sit on the Senate Banking and Agriculture committees respectively, which jointly drafted the bill. With both senators in relatively safe races, attacking them could backfire, executives said. Spokespeople for the senators' campaigns did not respond to requests for comment.
Senate control would also hand Democrats committee oversight powers which they plan to use to probe crypto companies with ties to Trump. In what analysts said was a potentially ironic twist, there is a chance that Brown, whom recent polls put slightly ahead of Husted, could reprise his leadership of the Banking Committee if he wins.
One of the crypto executives who wished to remain anonymous said attacking Democrats "didn't do us a lot of good," and others expect the industry will ultimately focus on rewarding friends in either party.
"I do think you're going to see the industry lick its wounds and get back aggressively to supporting the pro-Clarity type folks," said Josh Riezman, chief legal and strategy officer at crypto firm GSR.
Stand With Crypto, a nonprofit backed by Coinbase, has endorsed dozens of candidates and is spending on advertising in some races. Its executive director Mason Lynaugh last month warned that the Clarity vote had exposed which officials were "against" the industry.
But most of its latest endorsements are for House or Senate lawmakers who voted for Clarity on both sides of the aisle.
“We have the potential to move the outcomes or at least play a significant factor in helping reelect these crypto champions," said Lynaugh.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Revolut will cover costs for customers hit by data hack, Western Europe CEO says
items.author: Elizabeth Howcroft
items.creator: Elizabeth Howcroft
items.summary: Revolut will cover the cost of customers wanting to change their identity documents after the London-based bank was tricked into giving hackers the data of hundreds of customers, the company's CEO for Western Europe said on Wednesday.
items.body:
Revolut will cover the cost of customers wanting to change their identity documents after the London-based bank was tricked into giving hackers the data of hundreds of customers, the company's CEO for Western Europe said on Wednesday.
Revolut, Europe's [USN:L6N45R0BS TEXT:"most valuable startup"], said it had sent the customers' personal data to hackers who had taken control of an Italian government agency email address, in an incident first disclosed [USN:L1N455038 TEXT:"last month"].
Béatrice Cossa-Dumurgier, Revolut's CEO for Western Europe, told BFM TV in an interview that the company would not pay ransoms to hackers, when asked if they had paid one. Revolut[USN:L6N458127 TEXT:" previously said"] it had not received a ransom demand.
Cossa-Dumurgier said Revolut had provided assistance for the 680 affected clients, 55 of whom are in France.
"If they ever have to change their ID documents, we're taking care of the associated costs", she added, without specifying whether this had happened yet or how much it could cost the company.
Financial institutions are required to send customer data to authorities when asked to do so as part of investigations into potential crimes.
Matteo Piantedosi, Italy's interior minister, told lawmakers on September 30 that the email address to which Revolut sent customer data came from the Reggio Calabria police's email system, but was an address that had never been used before.
Revolut could have and should have verified the request by doing minimal due diligence, the minister said.
A spokesperson for Revolut declined to comment on the interior minister's remarks.
Cossa-Dumurgier said that government agencies are sometimes the "weak link" in the system and that Revolut's own systems had not been compromised.

items.title: ノーベル化学賞の硤合氏、「受賞しても文句言われない」　カガン氏との栄誉に喜び
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - ２０２６年のノーベル化学賞を受賞した硤合憲三・東京理科大名誉教授（７６）は７日、都内の同大で記者会見し、世の中には他に重要な研究が多数あると指摘しつつ、自身の成果が「受賞できても文句は言われないとは（思っていた）」と語った。「研究に対する意味合い、位置付けも今回の受賞で認識していただけた。非常に喜んでいる」と話した。

今年の化学賞は「不斉有機合成における非線形効果と自己触媒作用の発見」を理由に硤合氏と仏パリ第１１大学のアンリ・カガン氏（９５）が共同で受賞した。非対称な「鏡像」分子を巡る長年の謎を解明し、医薬品製造において重要な発見をもたらしたことが評価された。

硤合氏は、尊敬する著名なカガン氏とともに受賞したことをとりわけ喜んでいると語った上で、「暗い地面を頭にヘッドライトだけを着けて、そこをずっとたどって行っているような気分」だったとこれまでの研究を振り返った。「もちろん完全にまだ解明したわけではなく、まだまだわからない面白いことがあるはず。今後ともそういう分野の研究が進むように微力ながら尽力したい」と述べた。

また、受賞により「興味を持たれる方はもちろん、必ずしもそうほどでもなかった方にも、ちょっと気を向けていただけるじゃないかな」「日本は有機合成（研究）の非常に盛んな国。これからますます皆さんが研究成果を出していただけるきっかけになればという風に考えている」とも述べた。 

硤合氏は広島県出身。１９７９年に東京大学大学院で博士号を取得した。米ノースカロライナ大学で研究し、帰国後の１９８１年から理科大で教壇に立った。

硤合氏は「傍から見たら苦しいことが続いていたかもしれないけど、全然本人はそうは思ってない。新しい事実がどんどん見つかるわけですからね。それはそれで楽しいというか、感動したことはある」と答えた。理科大の教職員や学生などへの感謝も口にした。研究成果について問われると、幾度も手ぶりを交えて説明する姿が目立った。

一方、研究成果が実際にどういう形で応用されているのかについて問われると「応用ができるに越したことはないが、化学賞だけ皆さん、応用が何にできるかって聞かれるが、物理学賞、宇宙のことってあんまり応用って質問されませんよね。応用オンリーではないとかねがね思っている」と答えた。 日本人としての受賞についての質問には「日本人かどうかというところはあまりこだわりを持っていなくて」と話した。

受賞の連絡は、夕方から夜ごろ、近所のスーパーに１人で食材を買いに出かけている時に電話で受けたという。

（岡坂健太郎　編集：久保信博）

items.title: NSE cautions investors over pricey overseas ETFs as demand surges
items.author: Reuters
items.summary: The NSE has cautioned investors about the escalating hazards linked to international exchange-traded funds as they experience steep premiums. While certain ETF prices have risen dramatically, their underlying net asset values stay constant. This disparity is primarily due to supply limitations and new regulations impacting ETF units. Investors should proceed cautiously; purchasing at inflated prices may result in sudden declines.
items.body: The NSE on Wednesday cautioned investors against rising risks of investing in international exchange traded funds (ETFs).It said several of these funds were trading at significant premiums to their underlying net asset values (NAVs), implying that investors were essentially buying international ETFs at elevated prices. Here are the key details.* Prices of some ETFs investing in overseas securities have surged even as the NAVs of their underlying overseas holdings have remained broadly stable, NSE said.* Premiums have widened sharply in recent weeks, with some ETFs trading roughly 65%-80% above the value of their underlying holdings at various points in September, according to publicly available market data.* NSE attributed the divergence to supply constraints and regulatory changes. It said that Indian mutual funds have exhausted regulatory overseas investment limits, which has restricted the creation of fresh ETF units.* The regulatory changes, which mandate that ETF price bands be linked to the previous day's NAV from April 1, 2027, could impact how such products trade relative to their underlying assets.* Investors purchasing such units at steep premiums may be exposed to the risk of an abrupt fall in prices, unrelated to movements in the underlying securities, NSE said, urging investors to exercise caution.* Assets in mutual fund schemes investing abroad rose nearly 55% year-on-year to about 485 billion rupees in August 2026, while investor folios increased more than 40%, according to AMFI data.* The demand has been buoyed by the performance gap between Indian and overseas markets. Over the past year, the Nifty 50 has fallen about 8% and the Sensex about 9%, while the Nasdaq-100 has gained roughly 24%.

items.title: Canada's Weston family to buy UK's Boots in $8.9 billion deal
items.author: James Davey, Raechel Job
items.creator: James Davey, Raechel Job
items.summary: The Canadian branch of the Weston family agreed on Wednesday to buy Britain's Boots from Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family in an $8.9 billion deal, pledging to invest in the retailer's stores and online and expand healthcare services.
items.body:
The Canadian branch of the Weston family agreed on Wednesday to buy Britain's Boots from Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family in an $8.9 billion deal, pledging to invest in the retailer's stores and online and expand healthcare services.
Wittington Investments, Limited, the Weston holding company, said it would buy Boots' retail operations in the UK and Ireland, Boots Opticians, No7 Beauty Company as well as its Thailand and franchised businesses.
"Boots is one of Britain's most enduring businesses, with a rich heritage, a trusted name and a vital role in everyday life across the UK and Ireland," said Galen Weston, Wittington's chairman, who will become chairman of Boots, which trades from over 1,800 stores and employs more than 50,000 people.
"We see a meaningful opportunity to make a great business even better," Weston said of Boots, which is based in Nottingham, central England.
Private equity group Sycamore, in partnership with Pessina and his family, will retain ownership of The Boots Group's other interests, which are in Farmacias Benavides and Alliance Healthcare Deutschland.
The Weston group owns Canadian grocer Loblaw and Shoppers Drug Mart, Canada's largest pharmacy, health and beauty business and owned London department store Selfridges from 2003 to 2021.
The British side of the Weston family is the majority shareholder of Primark-owner Associated British Foods (ABF.L) .
WESTONS PARTNER WITH FAIRFAX FINANCIAL Wittington is partnering with Toronto-based holding company Fairfax Financial Holdings on the deal, with Wittington having operational control.
"Wittington plans to continue to invest to build on Boots' strengths and potential, including upgrading stores, optimizing the online experience and supporting the expansion of healthcare services," it said.
The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.
Former Currys boss Alex Baldock was recently appointed as CEO of Boots, whose former owner Walgreens Boots Alliance was taken private by Sycamore for $10 billion in March 2025.
Reuters reported in April that [USN:L6N41416G TEXT:"a sale of Boots"] was possible.

Oct 7 : The US government and tech heavyweights Meta Platforms and Google parent Alphabet are joining nonprofit Biohub to build open datasets to train AI models for biological reasearch, bringing total investment in the effort to $1.8 billion, Biohub said on Wednesday.
Meta, Google DeepMind and drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million. The Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over five years in laboratory measurement, modeling and computation. The National Institutes of Health will coordinate datasets and repositories built with more than $500 million in earlier federal funding, which Biohub will standardize for AI training.
The commitments follow the $500 million that Biohub — a philanthropic venture of Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan — put into the project in April.
The investments fund the Virtual Biology Initiative, which aims to measure how cells respond to changes across far more conditions than scientists have so far studied, and use that data to build predictive models that could compress drug development timelines that currently take years.

"Biology has been just sort of a clever discovery-based science until this point," Chan said in an interview. "We have always held this as a community asset, not just for one group, so that it can build upon itself over time.” 
The datasets will eventually be released publicly, but companies that fund them get a head start, according to Biohub's head of science Alex Rives.
"With commercial funders we have embargo periods where there's a period of time where the groups can work on the data, and then it becomes available as a public scientific resource," Rives said. 
The arrangement is how Biohub is drawing private money into a project it describes as open science. Rives said the government-funded work running in parallel will carry no such restrictions, and that Biohub plans to approach pharmaceutical companies and philanthropies next.
Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells, Rives said, while an accurate predictive model will require billions and eventually trillions. Biohub's goal is to close that gap.
"We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," he said.
The data will come from techniques including spatial transcriptomics, which maps molecular activity inside intact tissue, and screens that record how cells respond to changes in environment. Much of it has never been generated in a coordinated way.
Rives said the work would normally take decades and that the partners aim to compress it into five years, with a first dataset ready in about a year. He expects accurate predictive models within five years.
Other AI labs are pursuing similar initiatives. Anthropic doubled down on its biology efforts with a wet lab, while the OpenAI Foundation started a more than $125 million grant program to fund biological and medical datasets for AI research.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Can Wall Street keep partying while bond markets burn?
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: There is a conundrum at the heart of US financial markets right now, it seems. Bond market fears are reaching fever pitch, catapulting Treasury yields to their highest levels in at least 20 years, yet the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are hitting record peaks. What gives?
items.body:
There is a conundrum at the heart of US financial markets right now, it seems. Bond market fears are reaching fever pitch, catapulting Treasury yields to their highest levels in at least 20 years, yet the Nasdaq and S&P 500 are hitting record peaks. What gives?
Investors could be forgiven for doing a double take. Boosted by the frenzied optimism around the AI-driven corporate profit outlook, the S&P 500 is up around 15% and the Nasdaq is up almost 20% this calendar year, even though the benchmark 10-year yield has spiked 120 basis points and the yield on ultra-long US bonds is at a 24-year high.
Soaring borrowing costs and a higher discount rate are typically red flags for stocks. Indeed, history shows that the rising cost of money almost always plays a significant role in severe economic and financial downturns, recessions, and market crashes. So equity investors have reason to be very cautious, especially given the market's historic concentration in a handful of artificial intelligence and tech stocks.
THE ‘WHY’ MATTERS But it's important to ask why bond yields are spiking.
The last time yields moved this much was in 2022 when the Federal Reserve cranked up interest rates aggressively to tackle the post-lockdown inflation whoosh that was then amplified by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The 10-year yield leaped an eye-popping 235 basis points that year, and the S&P 500 slumped 20%.
Back then, sky-high inflation was the big concern.
That doesn’t appear to be the case this time around, although inflation is still above target. If Treasuries were being trounced primarily because of inflation indignation or even fiscal fears, one might expect to see a steeper yield curve and a spike in market-based inflation expectations. Neither has materialized. Breakeven inflation rates on five- and 10-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) are comfortably below their peaks from May, and the difference between short- and longer-dated yields has shrunk across most parts of the curve this year.
Instead, the primary driver of the rise in bond yields appears to be inflation-adjusted "real" yields, a sign that investors are pricing in strong real growth.
As Cullen Roche, founder and CIO at Discipline Funds, put it, "The bond vigilantes keep showing up expecting a funeral, but it turns out they walked into a growth party.”
And if bond yields continue to remain elevated because of robust growth projections and not spiking inflation expectations or other risks, Wall Street could keep on dancing.
WATCH THE TERM PREMIUM The divergence between Wall Street and Treasuries is so extreme that many fund managers say it is time to buy bonds. According to Bank of America, the 10-year rolling return for Treasuries with a maturity of 15 years or more fell to negative 2% last month. That's the worst return in more than a century.
And right now, investors can lock in real, inflation-adjusted yields of nearly 3% over the next decade, and 3.5% over the next three decades. These are generationally high, essentially guaranteed rates of return.
Will this pull capital away from equities? Perhaps, but investors seeking to build a more balanced portfolio may not have better opportunities to do so.
One major threat remains for both bonds and stocks: the term premium. That’s the amorphous degree of extra risk compensation bond buyers demand for buying longer-term debt instead of short-term paper. Sharp, upward spikes in the term premium suggest factors other than growth and inflation, such as doubts around central bank credibility or debt debasement fears, are driving yields higher.
The 10-year US term premium this week has snapped to a new 12-year high of 96 basis points, according to the New York Fed's closely watched Adrian, Crump, and Moench (ACM) model.
It's never clear what is driving the term premium at any particular time, or the ripple effect it will have across markets. But if it continues rising, Wall Street’s party could soon be over.
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

items.title: Workers at Chile's Centinela copper mine strike after talks fail
items.author: Fabian Cambero
items.creator: Fabian Cambero
items.summary: Two unions at Chile's Centinela copper mine rejected further contract talks with Antofagasta Minerals on Wednesday and decided to strike after government-mediated negotiations failed to produce a deal.
items.body:
Two unions at Chile's Centinela copper mine rejected further contract talks with Antofagasta Minerals (ANTO.L) on Wednesday and decided to strike after government-mediated negotiations failed to produce a deal.
The risk of a strike in Chile, the world's largest copper producer, had been supporting global prices as output of the metal has been constrained by operational disruptions, natural events and declining ore grades.
The strike began at 8am local time (1100 GMT).
Union leaders said they wanted all workers to receive the same benefits regardless of union affiliation.
Antofagasta said it was "willing to continue discussions with their representatives in order to reach an agreement that takes into account the interests of both parties."
"Despite the impacts typically associated with a strike, projected production remains unchanged," it added in a statement.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE-Lebanon's Hezbollah gets $200 million from Iran to help displaced, sources say
items.summary: Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant ...
items.body:
EXCLUSIVE-Lebanon's Hezbollah gets $200 million from Iran to help displaced, sources say Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant aid from the group to supporters who bore the brunt of the conflict.
Reuters | Updated: 08-10-2026 00:38 IST | Created: 08-10-2026 00:38 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Hezbollah has received $200 million from Iran to help Lebanese displaced by this year’s war with Israel, two people with direct knowledge of the transfer said, in what would be the first significant aid from the group to supporters who bore the brunt of the conflict. The US disputed the claim. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement that the money "is not there," accusing Hezbollah of "trying to save face with fake stories about cash influxes from Iran."
A Treasury spokesperson said Iran was “running out of money and ways to move money” and that Tehran “does not have money to fund its campaign of terror.” Hezbollah received the cash last month despite a tightening US economic chokehold on Iran and increasing difficulties in getting funds to Tehran's Lebanese ally, said the people.
Intermediaries who moved the money charged a 20% fee, reflecting the risks of dealing with the group, they said. One said this was four times the normal fee. Asked for comment, a Hezbollah official said an amount had been secured and a plan for distributing it would be announced in the coming days, without elaborating on the source of the funds.
The Iranian foreign ministry, Iran's permanent mission in Geneva, and the Lebanese government did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Israel’s bombardment and invasion of Lebanon uprooted hundreds of thousands of Hezbollah’s Shi’ite Muslim constituents after the group entered the regional war in support of Iran on March 2.
But those displaced have so far received little to no assistance from Hezbollah, an armed group founded by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards in 1982 which has suffered heavy Israeli blows in two wars since 2024 and is designated a terrorist group by Washington. The State Department's Pigott said Hezbollah had caused misery for Lebanese and had itself been decimated, while its backer Tehran was suffering under a US blockade of oil exports. "The United States will continue to strangle Hezballah's finances through sanctions while supporting the ability of Lebanon's legitimate government to rebuild the South," Pigott said.
AIDING 50,000 FAMILIES Hezbollah would use the funds to pay an initial $3,000 per family, and priority would go to those whose villages have been destroyed or are inaccessible due to Israeli occupation, the sources said. These number around 50,000 families, one of the sources said.
Iran has maintained financial support to Hezbollah through years of crippling US sanctions: it transferred $1 billion to the group in the first 10 months of 2025, according to the US Treasury Department. Tehran has never acknowledged financing Hezbollah. Iran's policy of funding regional proxies has stirred domestic protester anger against the clerical rulers in the past and could prove particularly sensitive at a time of worsening hardship in Iran.
Iran had promised Hezbollah more funding after Tehran signed an interim deal with Washington in June that allowed Iran to sell its oil, Reuters reported at the time. That agreement collapsed in July. Washington has since intensified economic pressure on Iran, tightening sanctions and imposing a naval blockade to block Iranian oil exports.
Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said in a speech last month that the group would soon contribute to a project aimed at housing thousands of people displaced by the war, using “available resources and donations”, without elaborating. Hezbollah's ability to fund local services and provide post-conflict aid has helped shore up its support in the past. Following a war with Israel in 2006, the group immediately handed out large cash payments to those impacted and moved swiftly to help rebuild Beirut's southern suburbs, a stronghold.
But this time there has been little sign of reconstruction. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said last month that the total reconstruction costs from the two wars since 2024 could exceed $27 billion. A COSTLY WAR
The two sources provided no details on how the money got to Lebanon. One of them said it was increasingly difficult for Hezbollah to move funds via financial companies that once processed such transfers. Such firms based in Iraq and Dubai were no longer an option, and they were also now under pressure in Turkey, this source said.
Hezbollah’s foes believed money was currently the group’s “oxygen”, the source added. Despite the difficulties securing funding, the group had not stopped paying its fighters and the family members of those killed in combat, this source said. In Lebanon, the war has inflicted a heavy price on the Shi’ite Muslim community from which Hezbollah draws support. Israel has razed villages across a swathe of territory it has seized in the south, saying it aims to shield northern Israel from Hezbollah attack.
Israeli attacks in Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since March 2, according to Lebanon’s health ministry. Its toll does not say how many combatants may be among the dead. Hezbollah has not disclosed figures on its war dead. Reuters reported on May 4 that several thousand Hezbollah fighters had been killed in the war. (Additional reporting by Simon Lewis; Writing by Tom Perry; Editing by Peter Graff, Nick Zieminski and Daniel Wallis)

Oct 7 : Global stocks and the euro pulled back on Wednesday as oil prices held near $100 a barrel amid renewed Middle East tensions, while uncertainty about US Federal Reserve rate policy and France's fiscal condition weighed on overall sentiment.
The S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq slid about 0.2 per cent, a day after both hit record highs. 
The pan-European STOXX 600 <.STOXX> index ended 1 per cent lower, giving up most of the gains from the last three sessions. Banks took a beating once again, down 3.3 per cent. MSCI's main world stocks index fell 0.6 per cent.
Oil prices settled lower on Wednesday following a choppy session after the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up a release of oil stocks and prioritize diesel in a bid to curb record-high fuel prices as the Iran war squeezes global supplies. Brent crude futures  settled down 38 cents, or 0.38 per cent, at $100.20 a barrel.

The direction of interest rates also remained in focus.
Minutes released on Wednesday showed Federal Reserve policymakers were divided last month over the rationale for raising interest rates. They showed that "some participants" saw a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay, but a more hawkish core viewed it as necessary to guard against emerging demand-driven inflation.
Russ Brownback, BlackRock's deputy chief investment officer of global fixed income, said in a note that the latest rate increase did not foretell a predetermined tightening cycle.  
"The committee's decision is more nuanced than a simple conclusion that economic growth is too strong to engender price stability," Brownback wrote. "In other words, the Fed is reinforcing its commitment to be vigilant — not necessarily embarking on a sustained tightening campaign."
US Treasuries rose in afternoon trading on Wednesday, with yields backing away from their highs as oil prices fell and a strong $39 billion auction of 10-year notes reassured investors that demand for long-term government debt remained intact despite recent market volatility.
The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes was last at 5.284 per cent.
EURO DOWN
The rekindling of investor concerns weighed on the euro, which slipped 0.6 per cent to $1.119. It slid to a 17-month low against the dollar at $1.1161 earlier this week. The dollar index rose 0.37 per cent, following a 0.27 per cent slide in the prior session. 
French bonds have been under pressure as expectations of higher European Central Bank rates and political uncertainty before the 2027 election raise doubts over France's ability to fix its finances.
Wider yield spreads in the euro area weigh on the single currency by boosting expectations of ECB monetary easing, reviving worries about fiscal sustainability and stoking fears of increasing fragmentation in the euro area.
"The interest rate spread between Germany and the US became more negative, which provided support to the US dollar against the euro," Georgette Boele, senior currency and oil strategist at ABN AMRO, said.
"We continue to believe that financial markets are pricing in too many rate increases by the Fed and the ECB," Boele said.

items.title: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
items.author: Makini Brice, Janis Laizans
items.creator: Makini Brice, Janis Laizans
items.summary: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality.
items.body:
The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"student protests"], after a 15-year-old boy's [USN:L1N45R08Q TEXT:"hand was blown off"] during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality.
Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday.
The wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron.
Speaking to the nation on Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would review the demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October on issues ranging from renovating buildings to make more teachers available, but gave no details.
"In the past, too many promises were not kept, quite simply because they were untenable," Lecornu said. "What I want are concrete, quick and fully funded answers."
The lack of an immediate government response, which was decried by student leaders after talks at the education ministry earlier on Wednesday, appeared unlikely to quell the protests. At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school.
"We saw there were lots of crumbling walls, a shortage of teachers in public schools, absent teachers," said Gabriel Fillieule, who used to attend a public school but now goes to a private one. He and others said they were protesting to demand better learning conditions for all.
POLICE'S USE OF FORCE BEING INVESTIGATED While most of Wednesday's blockades were peaceful, police used tear gas and pushed back protesters in a street barricaded by rubbish bins outside Sciences Po university in central Paris.
Rights groups, labour unions, students and some opposition politicians have accused the police of using disproportionate force to quell the wave of protests.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said he had ordered the suspension of the use of stun grenades following an incident in the northern city of Lens on Monday in which there was a "strong possibility" the firing of a stun grenade had caused a teenager to lose his hand.
"I am suspending their use for the high-school students' movement until light has been shed on what happened in this case," said the minister, who added that 18 incidents in total had been referred to the police inspectorate for investigation.
Protesters have said they blame poor learning conditions for a sharp drop in French teenagers' scores in reading and maths over the past decade.
French 15-year-olds scored 43 points lower in reading in 2025 than in 2015, according to the OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment, the biggest drop among the OECD countries. Their maths scores also dropped the most.
But the government, under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, has little spare cash to address students' complaints of teacher shortages, ageing school buildings and inequalities between schools in affluent and poor areas.
TWENTY-FOUR HIGH SCHOOLS DAMAGED BY FIRE OR VANDALISM Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has acknowledged the "legitimate" demands of France's students but also described the unrest as the most violent student demonstrations in decades.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray told parliament that 24 high schools had been damaged by fire or vandalism to the extent that they would remain closed for weeks, meaning some 30,000 students would receive no in-person teaching until they reopened.
He estimated it would cost €20 million to €30 million ($22 million to $34 million) to fix the damage.
Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to opinion polls, said those who damaged schools should pay for the repairs rather than taxpayers.
The government has adopted a similar stance and has a bill going through parliament that aims to set up such a system.
According to an Elabe poll for BFM TV, 72% of French people think the students' demands are legitimate, but 55% of them think the protests should stop.
UNREST ELSEWHERE Elsewhere in Europe, where budgets have been under pressure as governments respond to successive cost-of-living and energy crises, students in parts of Belgium staged similar protests.
In the Belgian city of Liege in the southern French-speaking Wallonia region, at least 107 people have been arrested in connection with student protests this month, the Belga news agency reported.
Teachers are also on strike.
In Portugal, the main teachers' union FENPROF launched an indefinite strike in mid-September over working conditions, with teachers refusing to do any unpaid work beyond the 35 hours a week mandated by law.
And in Spain, teachers' unions have been protesting conditions in state schools. Teachers in Madrid plan a strike on October 14 to press demands including a reduction in hours, smaller class sizes and higher salaries.
($1 = 0.8952 euros)

Oct 7 : Life sciences company Danaher said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient.
Here are more details:
• The lab, projected to operate at scale in early 2027, will combine AI, robotics and technologies from several Danaher operating companies in one connected workflow to develop custom antibodies and other molecular tools
• It is expected to make discovering molecules eight times faster and unlock a tenfold increase in generating target-binding molecules annually

• The lab uses AI to help create new molecules that can bind specifically to a biological target, including antibodies, then builds and tests each one, feeding every result back into the model to improve the next design
• The lab is an example of a broader program across Danaher, intended to create a fleet of smart instruments, the company said

items.title: 米30年住宅ローン金利、3年ぶり高水準　中間選挙控え購入環境悪化
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Ann Saphir

[７日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Ann Saphir

[７日 ロイター] - 米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が７日発表した３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利（２日までの週）は７．４９％で、前週から１９ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し、２０２３年１１月以来、約３年ぶりの高水準となった。トランプ大統領の共和党が議会の過半数を維持できるかを左右する中間選挙を４週間後に控え、住宅購入環境が悪化している。

住宅ローン金利は米１０年債利回りと密接に連動しており、同利回りは今週、原油価格の高騰によるインフレ圧力への懸念や、米景気の底堅さを示す指標を背景に２４年ぶりの高水準を付けた。

ロイター／イプソスの世論調査によると、１１月３日の投票に向けて米国民が最も重視している問題は生活費の高騰で、トランプ氏の支持率が過去最低の３２％に落ち込んでいる一因にもなっている。

住宅ローン金利は、米国とイスラエルが２月下旬にイランへの攻撃を開始して以降、約１．４％ポイント上昇している。

先週の住宅ローン申請は前週比４．２％減。借り換え申請が大幅に減少したという。全体の申請数は１月以降５０％近く減少し、２５年２月以来の低水準となっている。

ＭＢＡの副チーフエコノミスト、ジョエル・カン氏は「現在の金利水準では、借り換えを検討する住宅所有者はごく少数であり、借入コストの上昇により、多くの潜在的な借り手が住宅購入市場から離れている」と述べた。
