items.title: MFs, advisers adopt 'wait-and-watch' stance on duration after RBI rate rise
items.summary: Debt fund managers and wealth advisers favour accruals and shorter-duration bonds, awaiting clarity on inflation and peak policy rates before adding duration exposure ...
items.body:
Home / Markets / News / MFs, advisers adopt 'wait-and-watch' stance on duration after RBI rate rise

MFs, advisers adopt 'wait-and-watch' stance on duration after RBI rate rise Debt fund managers and wealth advisers favour accruals and shorter-duration bonds, awaiting clarity on inflation and peak policy rates before adding duration exposure

Debt mutual fund managers are turning cautious on longer-duration bonds as the RBI begins its rate-hike cycle. (Representative Image)

Abhishek Kumar Mumbai 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 07 2026 | 11:23 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Debt fund managers struck a cautious note on government bonds, particularly longer-duration securities, following the announcements by the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Wednesday. The policy, delivered against the backdrop of persistent global risks, marked the beginning of a rate-hike cycle that fund managers believe could cumulatively amount to 100 basis points (bps) or more.
  A rise in interest rates is negative for bonds, particularly longer-duration securities, as it leads to a decline in their prices, and results in mark-to-market losses for investors.
  According to most debt mutual fund (MF) managers, the current strategy is to focus on accruals or carry (interest income), while waiting for the right opportunity to add duration through higher-duration government bonds.
 

  “Our preference today is to earn carry at the shorter end, stay patient on duration, and use periods of yield repricing to gradually add duration when the risk-reward becomes more favourable,” Axis Mutual Fund said in a note on Wednesday.
  Edelweiss MF and Bandhan MF shared a similar view.
Also Read

A new policy cycle premium

  “Interest rates generally peak out at the later stages of a rate-increase cycle. Until there is greater visibility on the peak in policy rates, investors should focus on accruals,” said Edelweiss MF.
  “We remain conservatively to very conservatively positioned on duration risk across a host of our fixed-income funds. We will look closely for any signs of moderation in the global themes,” said Suyash Choudhary, chief investment officer – fixed income, Bandhan MF.

  Wealth managers are also taking a cautious approach towards long-duration bonds and funds.
  “Until there is greater visibility on inflation and the terminal policy rate, duration should, therefore, be avoided,” said Yogesh Kalwani, head of investments at InCred Wealth. “We recommend allocating up to 60 per cent of the fixed-income portfolio to accrual-oriented strategies, with average maturities of up to three years, providing relatively lower sensitivity to further rate increases while locking in attractive yields,” he added.
  The fund manager preference is also currently in the shorter side of the yield curve.
  "We see value in AAA-rated bonds maturing in two to three years and offering yields of around 7.75 per cent to 8.25 per cent," said Edelweiss MF.

  "We prefer the one-three-year segment of the curve, particularly high-quality corporate bonds, where favourable carry, ample liquidity, and limited CD (certificate of deposit) issuance create an attractive risk-reward balance," Axis MF stated.                                                            Bonding it right

items.title: 独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進　マスク氏が歓迎
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Marie Mannes　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テス...
items.body:
独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進　マスク氏が歓迎
10/7 19:43 配信

資料写真：2026年4月14日、中国・上海で行われた政府主催のメディアツアーの際に、テスラ・ギガファクトリーに掲げられたテスラのロゴ。 REUTERS/Go Nakamura/File Photo

Marie Mannes　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は７日、同社の運転支援システム「フルセルフドライビング」に対するドイツ政府の支持を歓迎した。同氏は、交通安全の専門家らが「安全性の主張が誇張されている」と警告する「フルセルフドライビング」について、欧州全域での承認を目指している。

マスク氏は、ドイツのビルガー交通相が欧州全域での「フルセルフドライビング」の承認を推進していることを受け、Ｘにドイツ語で「ありがとう」と投稿した。

ビルガー氏は６日の声明で、先月にテスラと数多くの技術的詳細や責任問題について協議した結果、「フルセルフドライビング」のＥＵによる迅速な承認を提唱していると述べた。

協議の一環で、ドイツはテスラと、「フルセルフドライビング」で制限速度を最大１０％まで超過してもよいことで合意した。速度超過が主な争点の一つとなっている欧州の承認プロセスにおいても、ドイツはこのアプローチを支持する方針だ。

一方、交通安全の専門家や一部の規制当局は、テスラが採用している「速度オフセット機能」（システムが制限速度を超えて走行することを可能にする機能）は、欧州での承認前に削除されるべきだと主張している。

ビルガー氏はまた、システム名が多少誤解を招くという懸念に対処するため、テスラがシステム名を「テスラ・アシスト・ドライビング」に変更することを提案したと明らかにした。同システムは運転を支援するものではあるが、完全な自動運転ではない。

フルセルフドライビングはすでにオランダやベルギーなど欧州の一部で認可されている。

しかし、スウェーデンやフランスを含むいくつかのＥＵ加盟国は、同システムが制限速度を超えることへの懸念を表明しており、１０月に予定されていたＥＵの採決は、一部の国が追加試験を行う間、少なくとも１２月まで延期された。

items.title: Wall Street ends lower, off record highs, as Treasury yields climb
items.author: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
items.creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
items.summary: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs.
items.body:
Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs.
All three major US stock indexes were modestly lower, with the S&P 500 and the Dow snapping four-day winning streaks. The Nasdaq notched its first down day in six.
The small-cap Russell 2000 (.RUT) underperformed its larger cap counterparts, dropping 1.3%.
In the wake of Tuesday's stock market rally, Brent crude settled above $100 per barrel and long-dated Treasury yields touched a [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"24-year high"].
Iran war-related [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"supply concerns"] have led to soaring oil prices, which in turn have revived inflation worries and raised the chances of a prolonged central bank rate hiking cycle. Those concerns, combined with mounting corporate and sovereign debt levels, have caused a global bond selloff, which rattled global markets in recent weeks.
Investors "have been looking for some relief on oil, which would drive some relief on rates and that would therefore help the stock market," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at GLOBALT in Atlanta.
"The third quarter was supposed to be the weak quarter of the year; we were supposed to get a correction," Martin added. "That didn't happen, so it's three cheers and let's take some money off the table."
Stocks pared losses after [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"crude prices"] turned lower following the International Energy Agency's agreement to speed up the release of oil stocks, prioritizing diesel.
[USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Minutes"] from the US Federal Reserve's September monetary policy meeting, at which the central bank unanimously approved its first interest rate hike since July 2023, revealed divisions over the rationale of the increase. Some participants saw a hike as necessary to keep the impact of energy price shocks at bay, while others felt the increase was necessary to curb demand-driven inflation.
Financial markets are currently pricing in a 17.2% likelihood that the Fed will implement a second consecutive rate hike at the conclusion of its October meeting, down from 37.6% a week ago, per CME's FedWatch tool.
"The market’s Fed expectations are going to seesaw as it gets new bits of data," Martin said. "There's still an expectation for more rate hikes, but it isn't necessarily going to be a hike every meeting and that's what the market is telling you; October will be a pause."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 341.11 points, or 0.66%, to 51,180.17, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 17.18 points, or 0.22%, to 7,801.75 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 61.19 points, or 0.22%, to 27,538.69.
Among the 11 sectors in the S&P 500, industrials (.SPLRCI) suffered the steepest percentage drop, while healthcare stocks (.SPXHC) led the gainers.
Following the upward march of benchmark Treasury yields, the 30-year fixed [USN:L1N45T0EH TEXT:"mortgage rate"] surged last week to a near three-year high, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Housing (.HGX) and homebuilders (.SPCOMHOME) slipped 2.3% and 2.9%, respectively.
Chip stocks (.SOX) , which have soared over 80% so far this year, dropped 1.2%.
[USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) lost 2.5% following media reports that Elon Musk's aerospace firm was seeking $40 billion in financing to fund purchases of Nvidia chips.
Next week, third-quarter reporting season is expected to begin in earnest with a spate of high-profile financial firms expected to post results.
Investors are likely to scrutinize the extent to which massive expenditures on AI technology are beginning to show results, while also watching for clues regarding the health of the US consumer at a time of mounting inflationary pressures.
Analysts currently expect year-on-year S&P 500 earnings growth of 30.6%, on aggregate, for the July-through-September period, according to LSEG.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.34-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 115 new highs and 497 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 1,421 stocks rose and 3,371 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.37-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 9 new 52-week highs and 12 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 32 new highs and 250 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 16.21 billion shares, compared with the 17.57 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

items.title: Apple's smart home push could test a market still struggling with adoption
items.author: Harsh Shivam
items.summary: Samsung SmartThings update and new local-control features come as Apple reportedly prepares a wider smart home push, while Matter and on-device processing aim to address compatibility and reliability ...
items.body: Apple is reportedly preparing to make a bigger push into the smart home market, with a new home hub, an updated HomePod mini and a new Apple TV expected on October 13. A Bloomberg report also suggests that the company is working with LG on a range of connected home devices, including a smart doorbell, thermostat, deadbolt lock and security cameras. The move puts Apple more directly against Amazon, Google and Samsung, which already have connected home platforms spanning speakers, displays, televisions, appliances, cameras, thermostats and other devices. Apple’s reported plans also come as Samsung updates SmartThings with local device control and support for the latest Matter standard. The developments point to a market that has expanded in terms of available hardware, but has struggled to turn connected devices into a mainstream household purchase. ALSO READ: Apple partners with LG on doorbells, lock, thermostat in smart home pushSmart home market is growing, but at a slow paceData from International Data Corporation (IDC) shows that global smart home device shipments grew 0.6 per cent in 2024 before rising 4.4 per cent in 2025. The increase in 2025 suggests a recovery in shipments, but does not indicate a rapid expansion of the category. Market estimates also present a different picture when household penetration is considered. Market data platform Statista expects smart home household penetration to reach 82.1 per cent globally in 2026, with the market generating $159.5 billion in revenue. However, the same data puts average revenue per installed smart home at only $20.18. Statista calculates this by dividing smart home hardware revenue by the number of households with at least one active smart home device. The low average spending suggests that much of the market remains concentrated around individual devices rather than complete home automation systems. Having a smart device is not the same as having a connected home. A household with one smart bulb or plug can be counted as part of the smart home market. A more complete setup involving smart locks, thermostats, security cameras, sensors, lighting and a central controller costs far more.Why consumers have not adopted connected homes at scaleOne of the biggest problems has been that smart home devices have not always worked well across different platforms. Amazon, Google, Apple and Samsung have each built their own ecosystems, while device makers have historically relied on proprietary apps and connectivity standards. A consumer buying products from multiple brands could therefore end up managing several apps, accounts and hubs. The problem becomes more visible when automation is involved. A basic routine can depend on a device connecting to Wi-Fi, communicating with a cloud service and then sending an instruction to another device.ALSO READ: What happens when AI learns from info increasingly shaped by AI itself?Internet connectivity is another weak point. Cloud-dependent devices can become unavailable when the home internet connection goes down, even when the devices themselves are still powered. That is a bigger problem for products such as lights, locks and switches than it is for entertainment devices. Consumers expect a physical light switch or door lock to work without depending on an external server. Cost is another barrier. A smart plug or basic connected bulb can be inexpensive, but a larger installation involving cameras, locks, sensors, thermostats and a central hub can quickly become expensive. This leaves the market with a large number of individual smart devices but fewer households with fully connected homes.Matter has not removed the ecosystem problemMatter was introduced to address some of these compatibility issues by providing a common standard for smart home devices. Matter is essentially a universal, open-source smart home connectivity standard that allows devices from different manufacturers to work together securely and locally. The Connectivity Standards Alliance has continued to add device categories and capabilities to the standard but interoperability is still not the same as a common user experience. A Matter-compatible device can work with multiple platforms, but the features available can depend on the platform controlling it. Different versions of Matter also need to be supported by the hubs and controllers involved. The result can be a situation where a device is technically compatible with several ecosystems but does not offer the same functionality across them. Matter’s multi-admin feature was meant to solve some of these issues by allowing the same device to be controlled through more than one smart home platform. In theory, a light or sensor set up through Apple Home could also be shared with Google Home or Samsung SmartThings. But setting this up can still involve moving the device between ecosystems, scanning Matter pairing codes and dealing with connection or pairing failures. A common standard has made devices more compatible, but it has not made the setup process equally simple across platforms.Samsung is pushing more control into the homeSamsung’s latest SmartThings update addresses one of the more practical problems with connected homes: dependence on the cloud. When a smartphone and compatible SmartThings hub are connected to the same Wi-Fi network, the phone can now communicate directly with the hub instead of routing the command through Samsung’s cloud. Samsung says this can improve response times by about 30 per cent under controlled testing and allows connected devices to remain controllable during temporary internet disruptions. The update also adds support for Matter 1.6. This brings four new device categories to SmartThings, including energy meters, closures such as specialised doors and gates, irrigation systems and soil sensors. The change is significant for Samsung because SmartThings spans smartphones, televisions, appliances and dedicated hubs. The company is trying to make those devices function as controllers for a wider set of products rather than relying on each connected device to communicate with its own cloud service. Samsung’s approach also shows why local processing and control are becoming more important as smart homes expand. A connected home with dozens of devices generates a constant stream of commands and sensor data. Sending every action through the internet adds latency and creates another point of failure. However, it should be noted that local control does not remove cloud services from the smart home. Samsung’s system still switches to cloud-based remote control when a user is away from the home network. Older devices that depend on their manufacturers’ cloud servers can also remain unusable during an internet outage.Apple is entering a market that already has established platformsApple’s reported plans are broader than adding another smart speaker. The company is expected to introduce a smart home hub with a roughly six-inch display, alongside a refreshed HomePod mini and Apple TV. The hub is expected to act as a central interface for controlling connected devices and could use Apple’s updated Siri capabilities. Apple is also reportedly working with LG on devices including a video doorbell, thermostat, smart deadbolt, temperature sensor and indoor, outdoor and floodlight cameras. The products are expected to work with Apple’s smart home ecosystem and support standards such as Matter and Thread. That gives Apple a route to expand beyond the limited number of first-party smart home products it has offered so far. The challenge is that Amazon and Google have been building their respective home platforms for years. Amazon has Echo speakers, Fire TV devices, a smart thermostat and Ring security products, while Google has Nest speakers, displays, cameras, doorbells and thermostats. Samsung has a different advantage. SmartThings can be used across Samsung televisions, smartphones and home appliances, giving the company a large installed base of devices that can also act as parts of a smart home system. Apple therefore enters the category with a large device ecosystem of its own, but not necessarily a corresponding lead in home automation hardware.The smart home is moving towards a central controllerThe smart home market is moving towards a model in which the central device does more than issue voice commands. Apple’s reported hub, Samsung’s SmartThings platform and products such as newer local smart home hubs from companies including UGREEN and Anker point towards a greater role for a central device that connects different hardware, processes information locally and manages automation. UGREEN’s HomeAgent hubs, for example, combine local storage, on-device AI and Matter-based device control. Anker’s MindBase takes a similar approach, combining local storage with processing for connected cameras and other smart home devices. The shift towards local processing also addresses one of the basic problems that has held back connected homes. A smart home needs to be reliable before consumers are willing to depend on it for everyday functions. Apple’s entry could bring more attention to the category, while Samsung’s latest SmartThings update shows that established players are still working on the basic infrastructure behind connected homes. The next phase of the smart home market may therefore depend less on how many new devices are launched and more on whether those devices can work together without adding complexity for households.

items.title: Russia says it properly informed WHO of plague institute worker's death, blasts media coverage
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Russia informed the World Health Organization about the death of a laboratory worker at a Siberian plague research institute last week in line with established procedures, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday, accusing the media of providing false information about the case.
items.body:
Russia informed the World Health Organization about the death of a [USN:L8N45R0KA TEXT:"laboratory worker"] at a Siberian plague research institute last week in line with established procedures, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Wednesday, accusing the media of providing false information about the case.
Peskov was commenting on an ABC News report that the United States had lodged a formal diplomatic complaint over Russia's handling of the reported death, urging Moscow to provide greater transparency about the incident.
The laboratory worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people and dispatch the head of Russia's health watchdog to the Irkutsk region.
Peskov said much of the reporting surrounding the incident was false and that people should rely on information released by state health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor.
On Tuesday the watchdog [USN:L8N45S0R0 TEXT:"said"] that no cases of plague had been detected among anyone who had come into contact with the deceased, and locals said their lives had barely been disrupted.
Peskov said no phone call had been scheduled at this point between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, who said on Tuesday that he would speak to Putin "very soon" about the case.

items.title: TSX posts steepest decline in four months as bond yields climb
items.author: Fergal Smith
items.creator: Fergal Smith
items.summary: Canada's benchmark stock fell the most in four months on Wednesday as investors weighed elevated bond yields and trade uncertainty, with financial and metal mining shares leading declines.
items.body:
Canada's benchmark stock fell the most in four months on Wednesday as investors weighed elevated bond yields and trade uncertainty, with financial and metal mining shares leading declines.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended down 607.65 points, or 1.7%, at 35,041.86, its steepest decline since June 5 and the lowest closing level in two and a half months.
The US 10-year benchmark, a global benchmark for long-term borrowing costs, touched a fresh 24-year high before clawing back some of their increase on a strong auction.
"When yields go up, you get headwinds with materials," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James.
The materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, declined 2.9% as gold dropped to a two-month low. A stronger US dollar, along with elevated US Treasury yields, reduced the appeal of the non-yielding metal.
Anglo American's (AAL.L) proposed $54 billion merger with Canada's [USN:L8N45T1LE TEXT:"Teck Resources"] (TECKb.TO) and the sale of its Brazilian nickel business have become test cases for navigating geopolitical complexities as they await antitrust approval, CEO Duncan Wanblad said. Shares of Teck lost 2.2%.
US President Donald Trump said Canada has been difficult to deal with as his administration seeks to reach a new [USN:S0N42W00J TEXT:"trade agreement"] with Ottawa.
"As this tariff uncertainty continues, you're going to see more and more downward pressure materialize for consumers and businesses and that's going to weigh down on financials," Dehal said.
Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) were down 2.3% as major bank stocks posted declines. It included a 3.3% drop for the shares of Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD.TO) .
Industrials (.GSPTTIN) lost 1.65% and energy (.SPTTEN) ended 0.75% lower.
[USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled down 1.3% at $88.28 a barrel after the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up a release of oil stocks and prioritize diesel in a bid to curb record-high fuel prices as the Iran war squeezes global supplies.

items.title: 独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築　最高価格帯に注力
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Rachel More　Ilona Wissenbach

[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高...
items.body:
独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築　最高価格帯に注力
10/7 19:11 配信

写真はポルシェのロゴ。3月10日、ドイツ・ケルンで撮影。REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch

Rachel More　Ilona Wissenbach

[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級スポーツカーメーカー、ポルシェは７日、販売台数の減少を前提に事業を再構築すると明らかにした。需要が低迷する中でも、高級モデルへの注力で利益率の回復を目指す。

再建計画では、将来の損益分岐点となる販売台数を２０万台未満に引き下げる方針を示した。昨年の総納車台数２７万９４４９台を大幅に下回る水準となる。

ポルシェの世界納車台数は上場を果たした２０２２年から既に１０％近く減少した。中国での需要急減と米国の関税が打撃となっている。

南西部バイザッハの開発センターで開いた投資家向け説明会で、ミヒャエル・ライタース最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「９１１」などの高級スポーツカーに注力することで経営を立て直せると訴えた。年間販売の最高価格帯にある１万台について、販売価格の引き上げを目指す。

「世界で最も魅力的なスポーツカーメーカーとしてのポルシェの地位を強化したい」と述べ、ブランド価値の面でフェラーリやルイ・ヴィトンと肩を並べる存在に位置付けた。

＜２桁の利益率回復へ険しい道のり＞

ライタース氏は当面コスト削減に重点を置くと説明した。

ポルシェは今回の戦略で、グループ営業利益率の長期目標を１５％に設定した。おおむね５年以内を指す中期では、１０─１５％を目指す。利益率は上場した４年前の１０％台後半から、２５年には１．１％に急低下した。

発表を受けて株価は３．２％上昇した。

ライタース氏によると、現状では中期目標の下限を達成する見通しだ。それ以上の改善には、一段と踏み込んだ事業再編か「より好ましい事業環境」が必要になるという。

同氏は既存の人員削減策や管理職を４０％減らす計画に加え、開発費と販売費の削減で経営基盤を強化すると述べた。コスト削減に向け、同じフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）傘下の高級車メーカー、アウディとの車台共用も拡大する方針だ。

items.title: Microsoft brings more AI to PCs as it challenges Apple
items.author: Stephen Nellis
items.creator: Stephen Nellis
items.summary: Microsoft unveiled on Wednesday an AI coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, challenging Apple's push to bring more AI into personal devices.
items.body:
Microsoft (MSFT.O) unveiled on Wednesday an AI coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, challenging Apple's (AAPL.O) push to bring more AI into personal devices.
The software company also presented at the event in San Francisco a high-powered Surface laptop called Ultra powered by Nvidia's (NVDA.O) [USN:L6N42909E TEXT:"RTX Spark chips"]. Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft is seeking to turn Windows into a platform for AI agents to handle tasks such as writing computer code or tackling complex business projects on desktops and laptops.
For Microsoft, the move represents a bet that some work that currently happens in its costly Azure cloud computing data centers can shift to high-powered Windows machines in businesses and homes, a market where the firm retains a stronghold — and where its customers foot the hardware bills. It is a market opportunity rival [USN:L6N45D0ZZ TEXT:"Apple is also chasing"] with new Mac computers.
For Nvidia, cracking the Windows PC market could help it go after one of the last major markets dominated by Intel (INTC.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) .
As a guardrail against increasingly autonomous AI agents that have created security risks, Microsoft said it was releasing Microsoft Execution Containers, a tool to prevent agents from accessing data and doing unauthorized tasks when running on a laptop or desktop machine. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia will use the tools, said Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president for Windows and devices.
“We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said.
Davuluri said new tools would let IT departments set rules for agents and the Windows operating system would enforce those rules on each employee’s machine.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who joined Nadella on stage, said Microsoft’s new execution container technology, which goes by MXC for short, "is going to revolutionize how agents are built and deployed.”
“Without it, (agents are) a complete nonstarter,” he said.
Nvidia is [USN:L6N45K077 TEXT:"trying to prevent"] a repeat of the hack of AI hub Hugging Face, while Apple is looking to [USN:L6N45O14K TEXT:"tighten up the process"] for giving AI agents full access to a Mac computer's hard drive.
AI MOVES TO THE PC Microsoft also unveiled AI models that previously required cloud access but can now run locally on high-powered Windows desktops and laptops, including Nvidia's open-source Nemotron model. Davuluri said a version of Chinese AI firm DeepSeek's V4 model can run on machines with at least 60 gigabytes of memory and outperform OpenAI's GPT-5 on some coding and reasoning tasks.
Microsoft is taking a similar approach with its own Copilot AI assistant, splitting tasks between the cloud and individual laptops. “Copilot will still use the cloud for the hardest tasks, but for times when cost or privacy matter more, it can delegate down to local models that run directly on your computer,” said Microsoft’s Copilot chief Jacob Andreou.
Davuluri also said Meta's (META.O) Muse personal assistant will come to Windows devices as a native app, using some of Microsoft’s new security tools, and that OpenClaw, the open-source AI agent system, can also work with those security tools.
PRICE BARRIER One of the key challenges Microsoft and Nvidia face is the steep pricing of these devices after a memory-chip crunch drove up costs.
The new Surface Laptop Ultra will start at $2,599 and rise to $5,899 for a model with a 20-core processor, 128 gigabytes of memory and one terabyte of storage.
Apple's MacBook Pro with a 40-core graphics chip, 128 GB of memory and two TB of storage costs $6,700, although the machines are not directly comparable. Microsoft's entry-level Ultra costs more than Apple's $1,999 base MacBook Pro, but comes with 24 GB of memory compared with 16 GB on Apple's entry-level model.
When Microsoft originally pitched the idea of running AI tasks on PCs two years ago to save costs, the laptops were mostly priced below $2,000, but Nvidia increased the price of an AI desktop machine called the DGX Spark by about 75% since its launch to $6,950 amid rising memory costs.
Two years ago, "the software wasn't ready, but the hardware was. Now the software is ready and the hardware is too expensive to actually run it locally," said Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. "So it's becoming this thing where only the people who have the budget can really afford to run AI locally."

items.title: Trump rallies for Paxton in third Texas trip in a month as Republicans defend stronghold
items.author: Nandita Bose
items.creator: Nandita Bose
items.summary: US President Donald Trumpmade his third trip to Texas in a month on Wednesday to campaign for Republicans who now face unexpectedly tight midterm election battles as they seek to retain control of Congress.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump made his third trip to Texas in a month on Wednesday to campaign for Republicans who now face unexpectedly tight midterm election battles as they seek to retain control of Congress.
Trump spoke in a packed arena in San Antonio to support Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, who is locked in a close race with Democrat James Talarico. A loss on November 3 would complicate the party's path to retaining its slim Senate majority and mark a major setback in a Republican stronghold.
Trump expressed appreciation for Paxton's loyalty. He endorsed Paxton in the primary after faulting the incumbent Republican senator, John Cornyn, for not supporting him during tough times.
"He was with us all the way," Trump said of Paxton. "He's a fantastic man and what a job he's done."
Supporters, some waving cowboy hats, cheered for Trump and shouted "USA," drowning out several protesters who interrupted the event in a Texas city led by a Democrat. Trump said the protesters should "get the hell out of here."
The rally was Trump's latest effort to mobilize his supporters for Paxton after staging an unusual [USN:L6N45M0UV TEXT:"mi"][USN:L6N45M0UV TEXT:"dterm convention"]in Dallas, in part to boost him. But Trump has also publicly criticized his longtime ally, calling Paxton "a pain in the ass sometimes" last week before adding that Republicans "need Ken so badly."
Trump's repeated trips to Texas are part of a broader push in Republican-leaning states, which were expected to be safely in hand but have instead become midterm battlegrounds. His 32-day campaign blitz has taken him through Texas, Oklahoma, Alabama, Ohio and Nebraska, while Vice President JD Vance has campaigned in Alaska. Trump and Vance carried all six states in the 2024 presidential election.
Republicans are struggling as voters focus on high costs and the war with Iran, giving Trump [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"record-low approval ratings"]. A Reuters/Ipsos poll completed Monday put his approval at 32%, with Democrats leading Republicans 44% to 37% among registered voters.
Trump surprised some Republicans in May by backing Paxton in a party runoff over Cornyn, whom party leaders saw as a safer bet. Republicans are now spending heavily to defend territory they once expected to win comfortably.
Trump won the state by 14 points in 2024, but recent polls have shown Talarico ahead of Paxton. Republicans are also defending competitive House of Representatives seats in South Texas. Both Trump and Paxton attacked Talarico repeatedly in their remarks.
For Trump, the stakes are also personal. James Henson, director of the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin, said losing the Senate race would be "devastating for Republicans and devastating for Donald Trump" given his support for Paxton. "I think the president clearly will do a lot to try to avoid that outcome," Henson said.
Trump's political operation has also poured millions into competitive House races. In San Antonio, Republican Carlos De La Cruz, an Air Force veteran, is running in a newly redrawn district, part of a Republican-led remapping that Democrats have called a partisan gerrymander. De La Cruz is expected to speak at Wednesday's rally.
AN UNEASY ALLIANCE Trump and Paxton's relationship has appeared awkward at times. Paxton was recorded telling donors that [USN:L6N45M0UV TEXT:"Republican candidates' numbers fell"] after the Trump-centered convention in Dallas, according to the New York Times, while Trump has publicly mocked Paxton's clothes, speaking style and appearance.
"So to be honest with you, the numbers, when we did that convention, it dropped our numbers. Everybody's numbers dropped," Paxton said in the recording. His campaign has disputed suggestions that the remarks amounted to criticism of Trump. A spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment.
A New York Time/Siena University poll released October 3 showed Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 45% among likely voters. Brandon Rottinghaus, a political science professor at the University of Houston, said rallying Trump's base was "necessary but not sufficient" for Paxton.
"Trump's visits are a catch-22," Rottinghaus said. "The president can inspire as much as he can repel."
Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott, a close Trump ally who is also in a closer-than-expected re-election race, planned to skip Wednesday's rally, citing other campaign events.
"My rallies are saving the Republican Party, again," Trump said in an all-caps post on Truth Social on Tuesday.
Republicans are betting Trump can still turn out the voters who powered his 2024 victory even as his broader standing has weakened.
The latest Reuters/Ipsos poll showed that just 24% of Hispanic voters approved of his performance. They were an important part of Trump's success in 2024, when he won nearly half the Hispanic vote, and are a bigger demographic in Texas than most states.

items.title: AI companies run virtual drug trials, aim to improve success of human studies
items.author: Deena Beasley
items.creator: Deena Beasley
items.summary: Novartis’ experimental del-desiran for a rare type of muscular dystrophy was expected to be a winner, with the Swiss company's CEO predicting annual peak sales of $5 billion. When a late-stage trial missed its goal last month, shares fell 11%, erasing $30 billion in market value.
items.body:
Novartis’ (NOVN.S) experimental del-desiran for a rare type of muscular dystrophy was expected to be a winner, with the Swiss company's CEO predicting annual peak sales of $5 billion. When a [USN:L8N45006F TEXT:"late-stage trial"] missed its goal last month, shares fell 11%, erasing $30 billion in market value.
AI start-up BioinvestGPT was not surprised. In July, it ran a simulated trial to measure how virtual patients would respond to del-desiran and predicted an insignificant clinical benefit.
It and other artificial intelligence companies say they are working with some drugmakers on virtual trials to boost the odds an experimental medicine will prove safe and effective when used by actual patients in an expensive traditional clinical trial.
The global biopharmaceutical industry spends some $140 billion a year on human clinical testing, but only around 12% of drug candidates are approved by regulators — a rate that has changed little in decades.
AI firms say simulations are being used to identify which pharmaceutical programs are worth moving forward and to assess the value of acquisition targets. As AI tools get better at flagging clinical risks, they say unexpected trial failures may become less frequent.
Human clinical trials typically start with small Phase 1 studies primarily to gauge safety, followed by mid-stage Phase 2 and the large Phase 3 trials required by regulators that also assess efficacy. The process takes years, compared with a month or less for some AI simulations.
"We shouldn't only ask how to run trials faster. We should ask how to run fewer trials that are going to fail," said Francisco Beca, chief medical officer at QuantHealth, an AI clinical trial simulation platform headquartered in Tel Aviv.
Investment in AI drug discovery more than doubled to $8.4 billion in 2025 compared to 2023, according to a recent report from McKinsey . It said spending is currently focused where the technology works best today, particularly molecule design, rather than the industry's major bottlenecks, such as proving a drug will work as intended through lengthy trials.
Pharma companies are "dipping their toes" into AI trial modeling, said McKinsey partner Alex Devereson. They are using different types of the technology, internally or with partners, to do things like assess drug candidates before committing capital to a program, he said.
US health regulators last week announced a set of initiatives aimed at speeding drug trials. If successful, the program could help create a path for predictive AI to be used in clinical development, a federal health official said.
FIVE OUT OF SIX CORRECT Copenhagen-based BioinvestGPT in July shared with Reuters its detailed analyses of the likely outcome of several high-profile drug trials before the results were known and has so far been correct in five of six.
They include the negative result for del-desiran, success for Moderna (MRNA.O) and Merck's (MRK.N) [USN:L1N44F0SC TEXT:"melanoma vaccine"], a weak clinical benefit for AstraZeneca (AZN.L) and Ionis' (IONS.O) heart drug [USN:L6N43B0BH TEXT:"Wainua"], the first failed trial for Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) heart drug [USN:L4N43X1AC TEXT:"ziltivekimab"], and success for [USN:L4N45R0K6 TEXT:"Vaxcyte's"] (PCVX.O) pneumococcal vaccine.
The fundamental goal of the pharma industry is proof of a superior clinical benefit compared to the standard of care, said Bragi Lovetrue, who co-founded BioinvestGPT with his wife Idonae Lovetrue in 2024.
The AI platform uses DNA sequencing to simulate a human body matching the eligibility criteria for a specific clinical trial. A virtual trial is then done using a model of the test drug.
"We can pinpoint the reason why a drug is effective and safe, and in many cases, why not," Lovetrue said.
The simulations are not always right. The predictive AI forecast positive results for Novartis' [USN:L4N44W1D6 TEXT:"pelacarsen"], which lowers blood levels of a cholesterol-carrier called lipoprotein(a). Novartis in September said the drug did not cut the risk of a major heart attack or stroke in patients with a genetic risk factor in a late-stage trial.
A subsequent analysis showed "we got the mechanism wrong," by not accounting for genetically set variations in the size of the lipoprotein, Lovetrue said.
QuantHealth, which uses real-world data and AI to simulate patient-level responses to therapies, has published its simulations of ulcerative colitis and cholesterol drug trials.
BIOGEN, TAKEDA TRIALS PREDICTED TO FAIL BioinvestGPT has done predictions for a wide range of trials.
For anticipated trial results expected before year-end, the AI company predicts failure for two Phase 3 trials of Biogen's (BIIB.O) litifilimab in the most common type of lupus, as well as for Phase 2 studies of Japanese drugmaker Takeda's (4502.T) zasocitinib in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
The AI model shows that both drugs are "suboptimal" for those specific trial populations.
Biogen's drug, which targets an immune cell receptor called BDCA2, is also being studied in a [USN:L4N45O11Z TEXT:"different type"] of lupus. Takeda filed recently for US approval of zasocitinib, which blocks an enzyme called tyrosine kinase 2, in plaque psoriasis and has a Phase 3 trial in psoriatic arthritis.
Takeda research chief Andy Plump said TYK2 was identified as a target by analyzing human genetics, while machine learning was used to optimize and "polish" the structure of the daily pill.
"I have immense confidence in this mechanism," Plump said. "I don't think we are near being able to use tools like AI to make definitive predictions."
Diana Gallagher, Biogen's head of clinical development for multiple sclerosis, immunology and Alzheimer's, said the company uses "every tool available to us," including AI.
She said only two biologic drugs have been approved for lupus and AI algorithms that rely on historical data could be prone to predicting a negative result.
QuantHealth's Beca and other experts said human trials will always be necessary, but AI simulations can be valuable when assessing the potential of an experimental drug.
"Is it still ethical in 2026 to expose patients to a trial that most likely will fail?" he said. "With the advancement of this (AI) technology, come 2027, 2028, or 2029, probably the answer is going to be that it no longer is."

items.title: Most US voters say Trump, Congress don't take AI risks seriously, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
items.author: Courtney Rozen, Jason Lange
items.creator: Courtney Rozen, Jason Lange
items.summary: A new Reuters/Ipsos poll showed that wide swaths of the electorate see AI as a major threat to American jobs, underscoring growing skepticism of the technology from voters across the political spectrum.
items.body:
Most US voters think President Donald Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new regulations for the technology, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll .
The six-day survey, which ended on Monday, showed that wide swaths of the electorate see AI as a major threat to American jobs, underscoring growing skepticism of the technology from voters across the political spectrum.
The fast-advancing technology has become a matter of keen national interest amid reports of AI agents running amok and hacking into corporate computer networks, and warnings from prominent researchers that it could one day pose an existential threat to humanity. Noisy, power-hungry data centers that power AI also increasingly pose a nuisance when they pop up near neighborhoods while jacking up utility bills.
Some 57% of registered voters in the poll — including a third of self-identified Republicans — said the Trump administration has not taken AI risks seriously enough or at all. Some 54% said the same about Congress.
Artificial intelligence has become a significant campaign issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections when control of Congress is up for grabs. Some 62% of voters in the poll said the technology could get out of control and risk the future of humankind, roughly the same share of voters with that view in a Reuters/Ipsos poll from August of last year.
Trump has repeatedly voiced unhesitating support for AI and the construction of data centers, arguing they are vital to US competitiveness even as bipartisan criticism of the technology grows. He often says the US tech industry will fall behind its Chinese counterparts when asked why his government hasn't set limits on the technology's use and development, a point that AI safety advocates say is misguided.
"That's an important concern but it's not top of mind for most Americans, nor should it be," said Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI staffer who quit in 2024 because he believed the company wasn't behaving responsibly.
The more pressing concern is that AI could cost people their jobs or threaten human health and safety, he said.
In a statement to Reuters about the president's handling of AI, a White House official pointed to Trump's new [USN:FWN45O1EJ TEXT:"task force,"] which he said is in charge of ensuring that "America continues to lead the world" on the technology.
"The Trump administration’s priority is to ensure there is a booming economy so that workers have many opportunities and experience limited volatility from any short-term disruptions," the official said when asked about voters' AI-related employment fears.
LITTLE FEDERAL ACTION While high-profile leaders ranging from US Senator Bernie Sanders — a democratic socialist who caucuses with Democrats — to Steve Bannon — a hard right ally of President Donald Trump — have [USN:L6N45616D TEXT:"called"] for federal action, little has come so far.
Trump last week [USN:L1N45K0VR TEXT:"said"] executives from the six leading AI developers agreed to a set of voluntary safety principles, including working with "independent auditors" to assess whether AI systems are working as their designers intended.
The safety agreement with the companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Congress has so far failed to agree on legislation that would set guardrails on the technology, and lawmakers are expected to be away from Washington until after the midterms.
The new Reuters/Ipsos poll found 84% of voters saw AI as a threat to American workers. By comparison, only 60% saw illegal immigration as a threat to American workers, while 74% viewed competition from foreign workers that way and 73% said the same of large corporations.
A bipartisan majority of voters - including 80% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans - said they supported stricter government regulation on AI.
Many voters also oppose building the data centers that power AI, which has become a pressing issue in congressional and statewide races across the country as candidates from both parties urge a pause in the current construction boom.
Fifty-six percent of voters in the Reuters/Ipsos poll back limits on building data centers, including 69% of Democrats, 55% of independents and 43% of Republicans.
The poll also found growing unease with the ways that AI could be used in warfare. Some 57% of voters think the US government should not use AI to determine the target of a military strike, up from 49% in a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in August 2025.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online and nationwide, gathered responses from 4,506 US adults, including 3,526 registered voters. The survey has a margin of error of 2 percentage points.

写真は米ドルと中国人民元の紙幣。2023年1月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Andrea Shalal

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - ロックフェラー財団などの専門家らは７日、多額の債務を抱える開発途上国が経済成長を図り、必要な投資を行い、民間資本を活用できるよう、新たな資金へのアクセスを支援するイニシアチブ「成長・投資リセット」を提案した。

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）、世界銀行、２国間公的債権者、民間貸し手らの取り組みを調整することで、低所得国が深刻な債務危機に陥るのを防ぐことを目的としているという。

必要な政治的合意を確保し、英国が議長国を務める来年の主要２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０） の下で取り組みを前進させることを目指す。論文執筆者らは「開発途上国は不可欠な投資を圧迫する前例のない利払い負担に苦しんでいる。緊急の対策が講じられなければ、状況はさらに悪化するだろう」と述べた。

執筆者の１人によると、開発途上国における利払い額は平均して歳入の１０％を超えており、１０カ国ではその額が公共投資を上回っている。債務水準が持続可能な約４０カ国がこのイニシアチブの適用対象となるが、一部の国では依然として債務再編が必要になるという。

今回の提案は来週バンコクで開催されるＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会を控えて行われた。

［香港　７日　ロイター］ - 香港株式市場は下落した。アジア市場全般の軟調な地合いを受けた流れで、原油価格が上昇する中、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株とバイオテクノロジー株が下げを主導した。

ハンセン指数は０．６％安、ハンセン中国株指数も０．６％安で引けた。

ハンセンテック指数は０．７％下げた。

テンプルトン・グローバル・インベストメンツのリサーチ責任者、バッセル・カトゥン氏はリポートで「政策支援にもかかわらず中国市場は低調にとどまった。消費需要の弱さと製造業指標のまちまちな結果が、テクノロジー分野への選別的な関心を打ち消した」と述べた。

この日は香港上場の中国ＡＩ・テック企業が売り圧力にさらされた。

ＡＩ開発企業のミニマックスが４％下落し、半導体メーカーの華虹半導体とテクノロジー大手アリババはそれぞれ３％下げた。

バイオテクノロジー株は前営業日の急伸を受けて２．８％下落した。

景気活動の鈍化を背景に、香港の９月のＳ＆Ｐ購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は０．３ポイント低下して４９．２となり、市場心理の弱さに拍車をかけた。同指数は好不況の分かれ目となる５０を２カ月連続で下回った。

中国本土の金融市場は国慶節（建国記念日）の連休で１０月１日から７日まで休場で、取引は１０月８日に再開する。

次期ＴＯＰＩＸに35銘柄採用、日本マクドナルドＨＤなど　除外候補は683銘柄
10/7 18:13 配信

東証。4月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Hiroko Hamada

［東京　７日　ロイター］ - 日本取引所グループのＪＰＸ総研は７日、ＴＯＰＩＸ改革の第２段階となる見直しで、新たに３５銘柄を採用すると発表した。既存銘柄のうち、基準未達となった移行措置銘柄は６８３銘柄。次期ＴＯＰＩＸの構成銘柄（２０２８年７月末）は９８６銘柄となる見込み。

新規では、日本マクドナルドホールディングス、フェローテック、ワークマン、タイミー、トライアルホールディングスなどが採用された。プライム市場以外では、スタンダードから２３銘柄、グロースから１２銘柄が選定された。

移行措置銘柄には、パソナグループ、三菱総合研究所、コジマ、学研ホールディングス、ブックオフグループホールディングス、テレビ東京ホールディングスなどが入った。

定期入れ替えはプライム、スタンダード、グロースの全市場を対象に、年間売買代金回転率と浮動株時価総額の累積比率という流動性基準をもとに年１回、１０月末に実施される。継続基準を満たさなかった移行措置銘柄は、四半期ごとに８段階でウエートを低減する。移行措置銘柄の再評価は２０２７年１０月に実施される予定で、２７年１０月時点で継続基準を満たした場合は段階的ウエート低減を停止する。２回目の定期入替は２８年１０月。

items.body:
ドイツ輸出、今年の伸び率見通しを1％に上方修正＝業界団体
10/7 18:09 配信

写真は独ブレーマーハーフェンのコンテナターミナル。2025年8月撮影。REUTERS/Leon Kuegeler

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - ドイツ卸売・貿易連盟（ＢＧＡ）は７日、２０２６年の輸出伸び率見通しを０．６％から１％に上方修正した。欧州での堅調な需要に支えられて予想外に好調だった上半期を受けた。

ＢＧＡによると、上半期の輸出総額は約８１８０億ユーロ（９１６０億ドル）で前年同期比３．９％増となり、輸入は約７１２０億ユーロで４．７％増加した。

通年の輸入伸び率見通しは３％に据え置いた。

ＢＧＡは「ドイツの対外貿易は安定しつつあるが、好転にはまだ程遠い」と述べ、米国および中国への輸出が低迷していることに言及。サプライチェーン（供給網）と市場の多様化を図るとともに、欧州企業の中国市場へのアクセスを改善するよう求めた。

「リスク軽減はデカップリングを意味してはならず、戦略的自立は自給自足を意味してはならない」と述べた。

items.title: Russia says plague institute worker's death does not risk an epidemic
items.author: Andrew Osborn, Jennifer Rigby
items.creator: Andrew Osborn, Jennifer Rigby
items.summary: Russia's health regulator said on Wednesday there were no risks of an epidemic breaking out in Siberia after a plague institute worker there died, as the World Health Organization pressed Moscow for more information about her cause of death.
items.body:
Russia's health regulator said on Wednesday there were no risks of an epidemic breaking out in Siberia after a [USN:L1N45S0CY TEXT:"plague institute worker"] there died, as the World Health Organization pressed Moscow for more information about her cause of death.
Russian authorities say [USN:L1N45R0VI TEXT:"the 28-year-old laboratory worker"] died last Friday from pneumonia of an as-yet unestablished origin, in [USN:L1N45S0CY TEXT:"a case that has prompted international concern"], including from US President Donald Trump. Around 200 people were initially placed in quarantine.
Asked on Wednesday whether the death was caused by a bioweapon, Trump told reporters: "Well, we don't think so. We're going to find out soon enough, but we don't think so."
He said Russia was not saying much about the situation but "they do say they have it very much under control," adding he had set up a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"They're sharing (information) a little bit with our people. We expect them to share it a lot with our people," said Trump, speaking in the Oval Office.
Global health officials - as well as the world's media - have been particularly alert to pneumonia cases of undetermined cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading fatal respiratory illness in China.
However, the cause of individual pneumonia cases can often not be determined.
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Director Erica Schwartz said at an event the agency was prepared to monitor and screen travelers although the risk to the US was [USN:L4N45T1BB TEXT:"extremely low"].
The WHO initially said it estimated the risk of the Russia case to the public as low, based on what had been made known, but told a press conference on Wednesday it could not make a fuller risk assessment due to insufficient information from the Russian authorities.
Rospotrebnadzor, Russia's health watchdog, said on Wednesday it was winding down precautionary measures it had put in place after concluding there was no risk of an epidemic and that it had shared its latest information with the WHO.
[USN:L8N45S0R0 TEXT:"No cases of plague had been detected"] among anyone who had come into contact with the deceased worker, Darya Shipilova, it said, and 90% of those placed in quarantine had been released after nearly 5,000 lab tests had failed to detect any dangerous pathogens.
It said Shipilova had been vaccinated and had therefore been "immune to the dangerous infections with which she worked". It did not say, however, what had caused the pneumonia which killed her or how she fell ill.
WHO CALLS FOR MORE INFORMATION Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director-general of the WHO in Geneva, said on Wednesday his organisation needed more information from Russia to understand what had happened.
"We would like more information to understand which laboratory tests were conducted, which pathogens were evaluated, and if this individual didn't die from plague, then how did she die?" Maria Van Kerkhove, director of the WHO's department of epidemic and pandemic management, told a virtual press conference.
Tedros said the WHO had offered assistance to Russia and also repeated a request for Russia to verify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause".
KREMLIN CRITICISES 'FALSE INFORMATION' IN MEDIA The Kremlin said Russia had properly informed the WHO about the incident in line with established procedures.
When asked about the WHO's request to respond to reports about a second person in Siberia allegedly falling ill, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged caution when it came to using media reports as a reference for what was happening.
"There is a great deal of media coverage, and the vast majority of what the media are reporting about this situation is false information," said Peskov.
He advised the media and others to rely on information provided by the health regulator. It did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on Wednesday about the WHO's questions.
EXACT CAUSE OF DEATH REMAINS UNKNOWN Some Western media outlets have reported — citing unnamed "Russian media" — that a second person in Siberia had died, saying they had died of plague.
Reuters was unable to find any such stories in Russian media or any evidence that a second person in Siberia had died although some bloggers on social media were making — without evidence — such assertions.
After the press conference, the WHO sent Reuters a link to a story about a potential second case by the Russian media organization starhit.ru, a celebrity gossip outlet, and a follow-up from British newspaper the Daily Mail.
Tedros said it was important to be transparent based on the lessons from COVID, adding, "We don't have any mandate actually to see whether this media is credible or not."
Russia has not formally responded to the reports about a second person dying, Tedros said, adding that he had heard only informally that Russia had denied those reports.
Tedros' call for more information echoed that of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has also said Moscow needs to share more information about the incident.
Pneumonia, a lung infection, can have a variety of causes including plague as well as other bacterial infections or viral respiratory diseases, such as flu or COVID-19.

items.title: We need a solution with the NBA, says Panathinaikos owner
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Europe’s biggest basketball clubs must find a way to work with the NBA, Panathinaikos owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos said on Wednesday, a day after they rejected a proposal from the U.S. league to join up for a new continental competition.
items.body:
Europe’s biggest basketball clubs must find a way to work with the NBA, Panathinaikos owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos said on Wednesday, a day after they rejected a proposal from the U.S. league to join up for a new continental competition.
On Tuesday, the continent's top clubs [USN:L6N45S0UD TEXT:"turned down"] an offer from the NBA, raising the prospect of a battle for Europe's teams, players and commercial riches.
Sources familiar with the discussions told Reuters that the Euroleague's shareholder clubs rejected a collaboration offer from the NBA in their meeting in Italy, though the door on a deal was not yet closed.
"All together we have turned the sport we love into a competition where the NBA, I repeat, the NBA, the top league in the world wants to invest and make Euroleague a part of their world," Giannakopoulos said in a social media post.
"With huge respect but also proud of what we have finally ... achieved we must together find a solution," he said.
His Athens-based team are seven-time European champions and one of the Euroleague heavyweights. The Euroleague is eager to press ahead with expansion and it is unclear whether the NBA will submit a revised proposal.
A senior sports executive told Reuters any collaboration was unlikely to begin before 2028 because it would be difficult to organise a new competition in time for the 2027-28 season.
Although the clubs rejected the current proposal, talks with the NBA could continue.
ONE LEAGUE "Whatever happens, it's the union of these 13 clubs that will, I believe, create the value for developing a product," Gaetan Muller, Deputy chairman of ASVEL, the Lyon-based Euroleague club, told Reuters on Wednesday.
"As for the NBA, we know their product is ultra bankable, well marketed, with massive TV rights. I hope that, in the long run, a common path will be found.
"For us, a strong league is a single league. It's obvious that NBA Europe and the Euroleague would be much stronger together," Muller said. "The ideal would be to have one single product, clear and simple: with the strength of Euroleague on the sporting and fan side, and the strength of the NBA on the marketing and bankable brand side.
"But all of this can't be done just any old way. There have been 26 years of (Euroleague) history, and that doesn't just get erased."
The clubs on Tuesday agreed to convert into franchises but stopped short of formally approving an expansion of the competition from 20 to 24 teams, delaying that move by a month. The decision to go to a franchise model will give the clubs a more permanent stake in the competition than their existing long-term licences.
Spanish radio network Cadena SER reported on Wednesday that the rejected proposal included an offer of 520 million euros ($582.14 million) for the Euroleague’s shares.
The NBA did not immediately respond to a request for comment. NBA Europe's managing director, George Aivazoglou, is due to speak at a conference in London on Thursday.
"They have a clear path to launching in 27-28, a year from now. And they can launch their league without poaching any of those clubs," said Daniel Kelly, associate dean and clinical professor at NYU's Tisch Institute for Global Sport.
"But the better deal is to align with Euroleague and bring in some of those clubs because then you have a critical mass of fan bases and you're not starting from scratch."
($1 = 0.8933 euros)

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
(７日１７：３５に配信した記事です)

Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 日本株が年末高に...
items.body:
再送-〔兜町ウオッチャー〕米中間選「ねじれ」でも株高の経験則、今年はＡＩ規制に要警戒
10/7 17:44 配信

写真は2024年2月、都内の株価ボードで撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

(７日１７：３５に配信した記事です)

Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 日本株が年末高に向けて勢いを維持できるかどうかを見極める上で、１１月３日投開票の米中間選挙の結果が注目されている。予測市場では民主党の下院奪還が有力視されているが、過去の経験則（アノマリー）では「ねじれ議会下での株高」が日米ともに高い確率で起こっている。ただ、民主党が勢力を拡大し人工知能（ＡＩ）データセンター建設の規制強化の波が広がるようだと相場の腰折れにもつながりかねないだけに楽観はできない。

＜選挙後３カ月、日本株３％高＞

三井住友ＤＳアセットマネジメントが１９８２年以降の過去１１回の米中間選挙を検証したところ、Ｓ＆Ｐ５００種株価指数は、選挙前の３カ月間に平均３．８％、選挙後の３カ月間に平均５．９％上昇した。選挙後上昇の確率は８１．８％に上る。同社の市川雅浩チーフマーケットストラテジストは「政局の不透明感は選挙の約１カ月前から市場で消化され始め、選挙後にあく抜けし、一段高になる傾向がある」とみている。

日本株はどうか。市川氏は、株価動向のばらつきは米株より大きく「日本固有の要因の影響も受けるため、米国株ほどきれいな形にはならない」と指摘。それでも、８２年以降の１１回で日経平均株価は、選挙前の３カ月間に平均で約３％下落し、選挙後の３カ月間に約３．３％上昇した。選挙の約１カ月前から株価は上昇し始め、選挙後に一段高になる流れは米国株と同じという。

もっとも、足元の相場は、平均的な選挙年とは様相が異なる。８月３日から今月６日までの上昇率は約１０％と、過去１１回の同期間平均の約マイナス４％を大きく上振れている。成長期待のある半導体株が相場をけん引していることに加え、国内のインフレ環境も異なることが影響していそうだと市川氏はみている。

＜強まるねじれ観測＞

今回の米中間選挙では、トランプ大統領の共和党が議会で主導権を失うシナリオが意識されている。予測市場ポリマーケットでは６日時点で、民主党が下院を奪還する確率は９３％、上院を奪還する確率は６５％に達する。ＪＰモルガンの集計では、１９３４年以降の中間選挙で、現職大統領の与党は平均して下院で約２７議席、上院で約３議席を失ってきた。現在の議席数は、下院で共和２１９（うち無所属１）、民主２１４、欠員２、上院で共和５３、民主４７（うち無所属２）となっている。

大統領が共和党、上下両院が民主党となる完全なねじれの場合、法律の制定や予算関連法案の成立には野党の協力が必要となり、内政上の政策が停滞しやすくなる。下院のみ民主党が多数となる部分的ねじれでも、法案は両院での可決が必要なため、立法面での制約は大きい。一方、閣僚や連邦判事などの主要人事には上院の承認が必要なため、上院の多数を維持できれば、大統領は人事を通じて政策を進める余地を保てるとされる。

＜ねじれは株価にプラスの経験則も＞

過去には「ねじれ」が株価にプラスだった様子もうかがえる。ねじれは「主に政策面でのダウンサイドリスクを限定的にする要因として、市場にプラスに働く」とＪＰモルガンの西原里江チーフ株式ストラテジストは分析する。ＪＰモルガンによる１９５０年以降の集計では、新議会の発足から任期２年間でみるとＳ＆Ｐ５００のリターンは、上下両院で多数派が異なるねじれ議会下でプラス２５％となり、単一政党が両院を支配する場合のプラス１８％を上回る。

ねじれによって、急進的な法案が通りにくくなり、政策変更に伴う不確実性が抑えられるためとされる。ＪＰモルガンは、メディケイドの追加削減や連邦政府による薬価規制の拡大の可能性が低下するヘルスケアや、既に予算が確保されている防衛・インフラ関連が恩恵を受けやすいとの見方を示す。

民主党が両院を制するケースでは、メディケイド削減が延期・撤回されれば、医療保険の対象者が維持される病院運営関連や、支援拡大が見込まれるクリーンエネルギー関連が下支えされる一方、共和党が議会の支配を続ければ、ＡＩインフラ整備の拡大や従来型エネルギー、電力網インフラに追い風という。

＜一段高に業績裏付け必要か、ＡＩ投資に目配り＞

株価の発射台が高まる中で中間選挙を迎えることになるが、ＵＢＳ　ＳｕＭｉ　ＴＲＵＳＴウェルス・マネジメントの小林千紗日本株ストラテジストは日本株について「（選挙後は）不透明感が解消することで、年末に向けていったん株高になるのではないか」とみる一人だ。

金利の高止まりが警戒される中ではバリュエーションの伸び余地が限られそうな一方、「業績が崩れなければ、株価には上昇余地がある」と小林氏はみている。中間選挙は、国内の３月決算企業の中間決算シーズンとも重なる。

もっとも、ねじれになれば、民主党主導でデータセンターの規制を強める機運が高まりかねず、「投資が後ずれするリスクが意識されてくる可能性がある」という。一方、次期大統領選に向けて政策変更の不確実性を意識した企業が、短期的にはＡＩ設備投資を前倒しする可能性もあるとＪＰモルガンは予測する。

ＡＩ投資のスケジュールに変化が生じれば、株価にも影響が及ぶ可能性がある。日経平均で比重の高い半導体関連株の業績を直接左右しかねないだけに「選挙後もデータセンター投資を巡る動向への目配りを怠れない」とＪＰモルガンの西原氏は話している。

（平田紀之　編集：橋本浩）

items.body:
ＡＭＤ、サムスンとのファウンドリー提携を引き続き模索＝ＣＥＯ
10/7 17:40 配信

写真は米半導体大手ＡＭＤのリサ・スー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）。1月5日、米ネバダ州ラスベガスで撮影。REUTERS/Steve Marcus

[ソウル ７日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手ＡＭＤのリサ・スー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は７日、サムスン電子とのメモリーおよびファウンドリー（受託生産）事業における提携の機会を引き続き模索していると述べた。

• 半導体メモリーの供給引き締まりを受けて、スー氏はＡＭＤが「顧客と協力してメモリー・フットプリントを最適化し、今後さらに多くのコンピューティング需要を満たせるようにしている」と述べた。

• ソウルを訪問しているスー氏は記者団に対し、ＳＫハイニックスの幹部と会談したほか、サムスン電子の幹部とも会談する予定だと明らかにした。

• スー氏は、メモリーサプライヤーに対し「より速く、可能な限り迅速な」生産体制構築を促していると語った。

• 「われわれは韓国のサプライチェーン（供給網）に大きく依存している」とスー氏。サムスンとＳＫハイニックスは「データセンターにおけるわれわれの広範な目標を達成するための鍵」だと付け加えた。

• スー氏は、データセンターの需要は全体として依然として非常に堅調であり、ＡＭＤの製品ポートフォリオ全体で強い需要の兆しが見られると述べた。

items.body:
日本のリーダーシップ、フィジカルＡＩ時代の鍵＝インテルＣＥＯ
10/7 17:38 配信

写真は米半導体大手インテルのリップブー・タン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）。6月2日、台北市内で撮影。REUTERS/Tsai Hsin-Han

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手インテルのリップブー・タン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は７日、都内で赤沢亮正経済産業相と会談し「先進的な製造や材料、半導体技術における日本のリーダーシップがフィジカルＡＩ（人工知能）の時代を実現する鍵になるだろう」と述べた。

その上で、日本政府やパートナーと連携してサプライチェーン強化や次世代技術の前進を図り、日米両国に「長期的な経済的価値を生み出していく」と話した。赤沢氏は「フィジカルＡＩ時代の到来を見据え、インテルと日本のさらなる連携強化に向けた議論ができることを楽しみにしている」と応じた。 

タン氏が、インテル製品が搭載されていることを表す「インテル入ってる」のキャッチフレーズは日本発で、そこから「インテル・インサイド」という英語表現にもなったエピソードを紹介し、赤沢氏が「最も印象的なテレビコマーシャルの一つだ」と応じ、笑いを誘う場面もあった。

タン氏は、日本法人５０周年の記念式典出席のため来日。都内で開かれた式典では、楽天グループの三木谷浩史会長兼社長、富士フイルムホールディングスの後藤禎一社長らが祝辞を述べた。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Rae Wee

[シンガポール ７日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は７日、エネルギー価...
items.body:
ＩＭＦ専務理事、エネルギー高や債務・ＡＩリスク警告
10/7 17:32 配信

写真は国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のロゴ。2024年11月、米ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Rae Wee

[シンガポール ７日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は７日、エネルギー価格の高止まりや記録的な公的債務、人工知能（ＡＩ）投資ブームに伴うリスクが世界経済を脅かしていると警告し、各国政府に財政・金融政策による対策を講じるよう促した。

ゲオルギエワ氏は来週バンコクで開かれるＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会を前に講演し、世界経済には二つの相反する力が働いていると述べた。中東の紛争によるエネルギー供給へのマイナスのショックと、ＡＩによる需要へのプラスのショックで、後者もインフレをあおっていると指摘した。

「この二つの力が及ぼす影響には世界各地で大きな差がある」と述べ、ＡＩブームの恩恵が多くの国に届いていないとの見方を示した。

ＩＭＦの最新の世界経済見通しでは、戦争で甚大な被害を受けた国・地域の下方修正幅が最も大きくなると説明した。民間施設や経済インフラに大きな被害が出ているウクライナや、イランの攻撃とエネルギー輸出の急減に見舞われた湾岸諸国が含まれる。

ゲオルギエワ氏の講演原稿では、世界経済見通しで２０２６年の世界全体の成長率予測を変更するかどうかは示されなかった。

「湾岸での戦争が近く終わったとしても、エネルギー高の問題は当面続く公算が大きい」と予想し、北海ブレント原油先物は、２７年を通じて原油価格が高水準にとどまることを示していると述べた。

エネルギー価格の上昇は、インフレ率や政策金利、指標国債利回りを押し上げており、米国、ドイツ、日本の１０年物国債利回りはそれぞれ０７年、０９年、１９９６年以来の高水準に達し、なお上昇していると指摘した。

＜増大する債務負担＞

ゲオルギエワ氏は公的債務の増加についても総会で協議されると述べた。ＩＭＦによると、公的債務は第２次世界大戦後で最高水準にあり、３０年までに国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）比で１００％を超える見通しだ。

債務負担については、米国を筆頭とする先進国が「最も問題が深刻だ」と指摘。債務のＧＤＰ比は新興国や低所得国を上回っていると述べた。政策当局はもはや、成長率の上昇だけに頼って財政問題を解決することはできないと強調した。

「それでも、債務の多い先進国では断固とした行動が見られない。今必要なのは、信頼できる中期的な財政再建計画だ。場合によっては、金融政策の負担をいくらか軽減するためにも、財政措置を前倒しで実施し計画を支える必要がある」と述べた。

「多くの国では今、金融政策で慎重ながらもタカ派寄りの姿勢を取るのが適切かもしれない」とし、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）、日銀による利上げは「極めて適切だ」と評価した。

＜ＡＩに多くのリスク＞

ゲオルギエワ氏はＡＩに伴うリスクも指摘した。ＡＩ投資の対ＧＤＰ比は、鉄道や送電網、通信インフラへの投資を上回る可能性が高いという。

経済・金融面でＡＩへの集中が進むにつれ、ＡＩ企業は高い企業価値を正当化するため、生産性と利益の向上を実現するよう迫られているとし、市場の失望が「広範囲に及ぶショック」に発展しかねないと警告した。

一方、ＩＭＦの研究では、ＡＩを適切に活用すれば、世界の年間成長率を０．５％ポイント押し上げる可能性があると述べた。

ＡＩへの備えが鍵になると強調。「労働市場への大規模な悪影響、サイバー面や安定性を巡る深刻なリスク、最先端のモデルが人間の制御を離れて暴走する恐れなど、ＡＩに伴う重大な危険の管理に役立つ」規制上の歯止めも必要だと訴えた。

講演後の対談では、現在の環境で金融政策が担う「最も重要な役割」は物価安定に注力することであり、中央銀行は物価安定を維持する決意を伝える必要があると述べた。「それができるのは中銀が独立性を保ち、国債を買い入れて財政側の負担を軽減するよう求める財政側からの圧力に抵抗できる場合だけだ」と語った。

items.author: ロイター

items.summary: [７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラとスペースＸの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）であるイーロン・マスク氏は...
items.body:
ＴＳＭＣは「テラファブ」を運営しない＝マスク氏
10/7 17:24 配信

写真はイーロン・マスク氏。2023年6月、パリで撮影。REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

[７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラとスペースＸの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）であるイーロン・マスク氏は７日、「テラファブ」の半導体製造施設を自身が率いる企業が建設・運営すると表明し、台湾の半導体大手ＴＳＭＣはその一部をサブリースする可能性があるとの見解を示した。

• テラファブは米テキサス州で計画されているテスラとスペースＸの共同プロジェクトで、人工知能（ＡＩ）チップを製造する巨大工場の建設を目的とする。

• ＴＳＭＣがこの工場を所有・運営するのが最も可能性の高いシナリオだとするＸ上の投稿に対し、マスク氏はこれを否定。「私たちが工場を建設し、運営する。その点については、一切の疑いの余地はない」と書き込んだ。

• 「ＴＳＭＣが希望すれば、テラファブの一部をサブリースすることはあるかもしれないが、それ以上のことはない」とした。

• マスク氏は先週、テラファブにおけるＴＳＭＣとの協力の可能性について協議があったと述べたが、詳細については明かさなかった。

• これに先立ち、ブルームバーグ・ニュースは７日、米半導体大手インテルのリップブー・タンＣＥＯが、同社がテラファブに関与し続けると語ったと報じていた。

• ＴＳＭＣとインテルはコメント要請に即座には回答しなかった。

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 中西祐介官房副長官は７日午後の会見で、同日厚生労働省が発表した８月の毎月勤労統計（速報）で実質賃金が前年比で８カ月連続増となったことを受け、政府としては「賃上げの力強い動きを定着させていくために、中小企業や小規模事業者の労働生産性の継続的な向上支援に取り組むなど、引き続き各種支援策を講じていく」と述べた。

先月厚労省がまとめた２０２６年度の地域別最低賃金が、過去２番目に高い引き上げ額となったことを指摘し「今後、着実に賃金の底上げにつながっていくと考えられている」とした。

items.summary: According to The Express Tribune, government-subsidised flour has largely disappeared from the open market, allowing commercial prices to rise significantly. A 20kg bag of fine flour is currently ...
items.body:
Pakistan’s flour crisis deepens as prices soar, artificial shortage claims grow According to The Express Tribune, government-subsidised flour has largely disappeared from the open market, allowing commercial prices to rise significantly. A 20kg bag of fine flour is currently being sold for Rs3,120, while an 80kg bag of coarse flour has climbed to Rs13,200.
ANI | Updated: 07-10-2026 19:47 IST | Created: 07-10-2026 19:47 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Peshawar [Pakistan], October 7 (ANI) The price of flour has surged sharply in Peshawar, with a 20-kilogramme bag of coarse flour reaching Rs3,300, triggering higher roti prices and growing public anger over what residents and traders allege is an artificially created shortage across the region, as reported by The Express Tribune. According to The Express Tribune, government-subsidised flour has largely disappeared from the open market, allowing commercial prices to rise significantly. A 20kg bag of fine flour is currently being sold for Rs3,120, while an 80kg bag of coarse flour has climbed to Rs13,200. A 20kg bag of chokar is also being sold for Rs1,480. Flour dealers have made crores of rupees in profits within days amid the sudden escalation.
Allegations that some traders are deliberately creating an artificial shortage have also prompted law-enforcement agencies to monitor major dealers and flour warehouses across the city. The crisis has directly affected tandoors. Bakers have increased the price of a 50-gram roti from Rs20 to Rs30. In markets including Khyber Bazaar, Ashraf Road, Karachi Market, Namak Mandi and Government College Chowk, single rotis have reportedly stopped being sold, with consumers instead offered double rotis for Rs40. Residents have also complained that the weight of rotis continues to decline.
The Peshawar administration has yet to take visible action despite complaints from citizens, who have urged authorities to enforce official prices and prescribed weight standards for roti. Meanwhile, the Food Department has presented figures showing that subsidised flour is still being distributed across the province, as cited by The Express Tribune. 417,168 bags were supplied at official rates last week through 1,611 active dealers. Peshawar Division received 101,955 bags, followed by Malakand with 120,737 and Mardan with 59,389. Other allocations included Hazara 38,129, Bannu 12,588, Dera Ismail Khan 41,688 and Kohat 42,682 bags, as reported by The Express Tribune. (ANI)

items.summary: [東京 ７日 ロイター] - 旅行大手エイチ・アイ・エスは７日、タイ法人のサーバーが第三者による不正アクセスを受け、...
items.body:
ＨＩＳタイ法人に不正アクセス、最大627人分のパスポート情報流出か
10/7 16:13 配信

[東京 ７日 ロイター] - 旅行大手エイチ・アイ・エスは７日、タイ法人のサーバーが第三者による不正アクセスを受け、最大６２７人分のパスポート情報が流出した可能性があると発表した。対象は２０１７年、１９年─２０年、２４年─２５年に同社のサービスを利用してタイに出発した顧客。パスポートの番号や有効期限といった情報が流出した可能性があるが、電話番号やクレジットカード情報は含まれていない。

不正アクセスを検知したのは２５年１２月１１日で、速やかに該当サーバーをネットワークから切断し、外部からのアクセスを制限した。同年１２月２９日には、日本で取得した個人情報の一部がサーバー内に含まれることを確認し、個人情報保護団体などに報告。２６年２月２４日には、外部専門家の調査でパスポート情報が含まれることが判明し、保存されている全ファイルを精査することを決定した。

公表に時間を要した理由については、サーバー内に個人情報と無関係のデータも大量に保存され、ファイル形式や保存状態が多岐にわたるため、手作業を含めて精査・照合の作業が必要だったと説明している。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: 香港株式市場は下落した。アジア市場全般の軟調な地合いを受けた流れで、原油価格が上昇する中、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株とバイオ...
items.body:
アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（7日）
10/7 16:11 配信

香港株式市場は下落した。アジア市場全般の軟調な地合いを受けた流れで、原油価格が上昇する中、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株とバイオテクノロジー株が下げを主導した。    ハンセン指数は０．６％安、ハンセン中国株指数も０．６％安で引けた。    ハンセンテック指数は０．７％下げた。    テンプルトン・グローバル・インベストメンツのリサーチ責任者、バッセル・カトゥン氏はリポートで「政策支援にもかかわらず中国市場は低調にとどまった。消費需要の弱さと製造業指標のまちまちな結果が、テクノロジー分野への選別的な関心を打ち消した」と述べた。    この日は香港上場の中国ＡＩ・テック企業が売り圧力にさらされた。    ＡＩ開発企業のミニマックスが４％下落し、半導体メーカーの華虹半導体とテクノロジー大手アリババはそれぞれ３％下げた。    バイオテクノロジー株は前営業日の急伸を受けて２．８％下落した。    景気活動の鈍化を背景に、香港の９月のＳ＆Ｐ購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は０．３ポイント低下して４９．２となり、市場心理の弱さに拍車をかけた。同指数は好不況の分かれ目となる５０を２カ月連続で下回った。    中国本土の金融市場は国慶節（建国記念日）の連休で１０月１日から７日まで休場で、取引は１０月８日に再開する。

ソウル株式市場は下落。サムスン電子の決算発表を控えて半導体株が売られ、総合株価指数（ＫＯＳＰＩ）は約２％下げ、９月１７日以来の安値で終了した。

サムスン電子は序盤の上昇を失い、１．２９％安で終了。ＳＫハイニックスは２．８２％下落した。

ユジン投資証券のアナリスト、ホ・ジェファン氏は「米国株が最高値を更新したにもかかわらず、国内市場は債券利回り上昇への懸念から外国人の売りで軟調だった」と指摘した。

サムスンは８日に第３・四半期の決算速報を発表する。ＬＳＥＧスマートエスティメートがまとめたアナリスト２１人の予想によると、サムスン電子の第３・四半期営業利益は前年同期の９倍弱に膨らむ見通し。実現すれば４四半期連続で過去最高を更新する。８月下旬時点の予想からは７．７％下方修正された。

売買された９１７銘柄のうち、値上がりは３３３、値下がりは５２７。

外国人投資家は２兆６０００億ウォン（１９億４０００万ドル）の売り越し。

韓国市場は祝日で９日は休場。

シドニー株式市場は小幅安。世界的な金利上昇と原油高が続く中、投資家は様子見姿勢だった。

市場は来週発表されるオーストラリア準備銀行（中央銀行）の９月理事会議事要旨に注目している。同理事会で政策金利は１５年ぶりの高水準に引き上げられた。政策担当者のインフレに対する見方が焦点だ。また１０月末に発表される７─９月期の消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）も金利の方向性を占う手掛かりとなる。

銀行株指数は０．６％下落。四大銀行ではウエストパック銀行が最も下げ１．２％安。

鉱業株指数は銅価格下落を受けて０．３％安。ＢＨＰが０．７％、リオティントは０．６％それぞれ下落した。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:

items.body:
独鉱工業生産、8月は予想上回る伸び　建設・機械がけん引
10/7 16:10 配信

ベルリンにあるメルセデス・ベンツのエンジン工場。6月9日撮影。REUTERS/Axel Schmidt

Aleksandra Kret

[７日 ロイター] -  ドイツ連邦統計庁が７日発表した８月の鉱工業生産は前月比で２．０％増加し、伸び率は２０２５年３月以来の大きさとなり、市場予想の０．５％を大きく上回った。ライン川の水位低下による物流混乱にもかかわらず、建設と機械の生産が活発となり伸びをけん引した。 

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏は８月の鉱工業生産の増加について「大きなサプライズだ」とし、「ドイツの河川の水位が低く、サプライチェーンに悪影響が及んだことを踏まえると、生産の減少も排除できなかった。それだけに今回の増加は一層歓迎すべきものだ」と述べた。

＜建設が自動車の弱さを相殺＞

建設部門が９．３％増と全体の伸びをけん引した。

エネルギーと建設を除く鉱工業生産だけで見ると０．６％増で、機械・設備生産が５．３％増と伸びに寄与した。

自動車産業は５．４％減と、再び落ち込んだ。

ドイツ自動車工業会（ＶＤＡ）によると、これは８月の季節的な工場休止が昨年同月よりも集中したことが一因という。

ギッツェル氏は、９月は自動車産業が巻き返す可能性が高く、鉱工業生産を再びプラス圏に押し上げる公算が大きいと指摘。「ドイツの国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は２０２６年に１％を超える伸びとなる可能性が十分にある」と語った。

鉱工業部門は、ドイツで拡大する国防支出に加え、人工知能（ＡＩ）を含むデジタル化の恩恵を受けている。

ドイツ復興金融公庫（ＫｆＷ）のエコノミスト、セバスティアン・ワンケ氏は「この動きは、ＡＩやデータセンターを巡るブームがドイツにも到来したことを示している」と述べた。

変動の平準化した３カ月間で見ると、６─８月の鉱工業生産は直前の３カ月間と比べて０．４％増加した。

８月の鉱工業生産は前年同月比（暦効果調整後）で２．３％増となった。

items.title: Individuals exempt from reporting foreign earnings; RBI to issue FAQs soon
items.summary: Even in the case of entities, there is a provision for self-declaration up to a cap of ₹10 lakh per bill, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said.
items.body:
Home / Finance / News / Individuals exempt from reporting foreign earnings; RBI to issue FAQs soon

Individuals exempt from reporting foreign earnings; RBI to issue FAQs soon Even in the case of entities, there is a provision for self-declaration up to a cap of ₹10 lakh per bill, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said

Reserve Bank of India | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 07 2026 | 6:23 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Clarifying that individuals do not need to report imports or export earnings, the Reserve Bank on Wednesday said it will publish FAQs (frequently asked questions) shortly to quell "misunderstandings" around the recently implemented regulatory changes.
Even in the case of entities, there is a provision for self-declaration up to a cap of ₹10 lakh per bill, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said.
Malhotra said the unified Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, implemented from October 1, get services players on par with merchandise entities when it comes to reporting requirements.
"...individuals are not included with respect to the reporting requirements for contracts of a personal nature. There seems to be some misunderstanding on the reporting obligations. We will clarify through an FAQ shortly," Deputy Governor Rohit Jain said.
 

He said the new regulations are aimed at simplification and promoting ease of doing business, and added that sufficient time was given to the members of trade as the guidelines were published in January this year.
Malhotra also said that the reporting on the RBI platform is to be done by intermediaries, including banks or authorised dealers and not by the exporters or importers.
"...we feel it is not a major inconvenience or a burden," he said, adding that some of the information was already being shared by the importers and exporters with the intermediaries.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.author: Fabián Andrés Cambero
items.creator: Fabián Andrés Cambero
items.summary: Dos sindicatos de la mina de cobre chilena Centinela iniciaron el miércoles una huelga tras el fracaso de su negociación contractual con Antofagasta Minerals, lo que genera dudas sobre el eventual impacto en la producción de cobre.
items.body:
Dos sindicatos de la mina de cobre chilena Centinela iniciaron el miércoles una huelga tras el fracaso de su negociación contractual con Antofagasta Minerals, lo que genera dudas sobre el eventual impacto en la producción de cobre.
El riesgo de una paralización ya había estado apoyando los precios globales del cobre en momentos en que la extracción del metal se ha visto restringida por diversos problemas operativos, eventos naturales y bajas leyes de mineral.
"La huelga se ha hecho efectiva conforme al plan sindical de manera ordenada y pacífica. Se ha levantado un campamento de huelga que tiene por finalidad visibilizar el conflicto y mantener reunidos e informados a los trabajadores", dijeron los gremios en un comunicado.
La paralización inició el miércoles a las 8.00 hora local (1100 GMT).
La compañía lamentó el inicio de la detención y detalló en un comunicado que los trabajadores equivalen al 22% de la dotación propia de la mina.
"La Compañía respeta la decisión de los trabajadores y mantiene su disposición a continuar las conversaciones con sus representantes para alcanzar un acuerdo que considere los intereses de ambas partes", aseguró.
"A pesar de las afectaciones propias de una huelga, la producción proyectada se mantiene sin alteración", agregó.
Explicó que la oferta de la empresa contemplaba bonos finales y préstamo blando por el equivalente de unos 26.400 dólares y un ajuste del sueldo base del 2%, además de otros beneficios.
Sin embargo, los sindicatos afirmaron que la huelga impactará progresivamente la producción ya que asocian sobre el 50% de los operadores de mina críticos, como operadores de pala y perforadoras, y sobre el 60% de los mantenedores de equipos de mina.
Los sindicatos Minera Esperanza y Distrito Centinela, que suman más de 700 socios, buscan que todos los trabajadores reciban el mismo nivel de beneficios independiente del sindicato al que se encuentren afiliados.
"El sindicato mantiene su disposición al diálogo para alcanzar un acuerdo, el que no
prosperó ayer sólo por la negativa de la empresa a abordar un mecanismo eficaz que
garantice la igualdad de trato", agregaron.
Antofagasta sostiene que desde 2020 los calendarios de negociación se separaron y los incrementos se acordaron en momentos diferentes.

items.author: CNA
items.summary: The presence of US forces has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents in Okinawa over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.
items.body:

US forces face curfew, alcohol ban in Japan's Okinawa after murder case

The presence of US forces has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents in Okinawa over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.

Demonstrators take part in a protest outside the Prime Minister's office following the killing of a Japanese woman in Okinawa, for which a US Marine is a suspect, in Tokyo, Japan, on Oct 5, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Kim Kyung-Hoon)

FAST

TOKYO: US soldiers stationed on Japan's Okinawa have been given a month-long curfew and banned from drinking alcohol while they undergo discipline training after a Marine was alleged to have murdered and robbed a local woman .
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday (Oct 3) and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia.
"Every interaction with our neighbours either builds or undermines the trust that is essential to our team. When that trust is damaged, it affects the strength of our alliance and the security of this region," Lt Gen Benjamin Watson said in a statement on Tuesday ordering the measures.

All US military operations on Okinawa will be paused for 48 hours while troops undergo training on standards and discipline, Watson added.
"BRUTAL AND HEINOUS" Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called Saturday's killing "extremely brutal and heinous". She said she had strongly protested to the United States and demanded measures to prevent such incidents in the future.
Yagi died of asphyxiation after Ballard allegedly "pressed on her neck," police told the Stars and Stripes newspaper. 

Devin Jacob Ballard, a U.S. Marine who has been in custody in an alleged robbery and murder of a woman on Japan's southern island of Okinawa, is sent over to the Naha prosecutors' office in Japan, Monday, Oct. 5, 2026. (Kotaro Ueda/Kyodo News via AP)

Hotel staff found the woman unconscious in her room in the early hours of Saturday after she failed to check out. About 200 officers were involved in a search for the man earlier caught on CCTV entering the hotel with the victim, local media reported. 
Okinawa Governor Genta Koja will meet Takaichi on Wednesday to discuss the response to the crime, which sparked protests in Naha and Tokyo.
Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War II until 1972.
That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of its troops.
The 1995 rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen sparked mass demonstrations.
Saturday's killing could complicate Takaichi's efforts to relocate some Marines from the busy Futenma air base to a more remote facility at Henoko. Opponents want the troops moved out of the prefecture.
Okinawa, which is 100km from Taiwan at the closest point, is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China.
